title: Edirne Hacı Hasan Ağa Cami Restitüsyonu
summary: 1365-1453 yılları arasında Osmanlı Devleti’ne başkentlik yapmış olan Edirne, zengin bir mimari dokuya sahiptir. Dini yapılar bu dokunun belirgin öğelerini oluşturmaktadır. Özellikle 15. yy.da Edirne’de çok sayıda merkezi planlı ve tek kubbeli cami inşa edilmiştir. 1700’lü yıllarda yaşanan yangın, depremler ve savaşlar bu camilerde tahribatına neden olmuştur. Çalışma toprak seviyesindeki kalıntılarından yola çıkarak Hacı Hasan Ağa Camisinin restitüsyon projesini tartışmayı amaçlamaktadır. Yapının restitüsyon projesinin incelenmesinde üç yöntem belirlenmiştir. İlk olarak literatür taraması yapılarak tarihsel kaynaklara ulaşılmıştır. story: Edirne was the Ottoman capital from 1365 to 1453, and in the 1400s it filled up with domed mosques built around a single central plan. Fires, earthquakes and wars in the 1700s damaged many of them. This 2022 study starts from what is left of the Hacı Hasan Ağa Mosque at ground level and tries to rebuild, on paper, how it once stood.

title: Origins of translation and simulation in terms of theory and practice: Translation of Muhammad Iqbal's Urdu and Persian poetry in Arabic as a model
summary: Translation has a great importance in the development of human sciences in every age. First, we examine the theories of writers and critics mentioned in the translation and simulation. Translator must know the function of the symbolic language that differs from the metaphors and similes. Translation is the best way to enrich the languages in which the literatures are formulated, which must be in constant contact with what human thought offers, and the writer or translator must take a position of criticism and scrutiny. The translator must not forget that he does not convey the meanings of words only, but also conveys the cultural spirit and emotional life of the era in which these texts were
creator: Salahuddin Mohd. Shamsuddin, Siti Sarah binti Hj. Ahmad
source_name: Al-Dad Journal
scope_basis: Crossref search "persian poetry"; publisher hosted in Malaysia
story: Translating a poem means carrying more than words. This 2021 paper looks at turning Muhammad Iqbal's Urdu and Persian poetry into Arabic, and argues that a translator must also carry the cultural spirit and emotional life of the time the text was written. Symbols, it says, work differently from metaphors and similes, and a translator has to know the difference.

title: Peranan Pengkorporatan Pentadbiran Zakat Terhadap Pengurusan Sumber Manusia: Kajian di Malaysia
summary: This study was conducted to present the relationship between the privatization of zakat administration to human resource management. Data collection was done qualitatively through library research and interviews. The study population consisted of selected states. While the study sample is Johor, Perak, Selangor, Penang and the Federal Territory. Overall, the study proves that the implications of privatization in the administration of zakat provide several advantages compared to states that do not practice privatization. creator: Muhsin Nor Paizin, Suhaili Sarif
source_name: ‘Abqari Journal
scope_basis: Crossref search "zakat management"; publisher hosted in Malaysia
story: Zakat is the yearly charity Muslims give, and in Malaysia it is collected by organised state bodies. This 2021 study asks what happens to the people who run zakat when that administration is turned into a corporation. The researchers used library research and interviews in Johor, Perak, Selangor, Penang and the Federal Territory.

It was written by Hasan Yüksel and published in Sosyal Siyaset Konferansları Dergisi / Journal of Social Policy Conferences in 2024. Its record gives only the title and authors, so this is an outline.

summary: Bu çalışma, dini yapılarda yaygın olarak kullanılan geleneksel kündekâri tekniğinin günümüzdeki uygulamalarını incelemeyi ve bu tekniğin korunması ile sürdürülebilirliğine yönelik öneriler geliştirmeyi amaçlamaktadır. Kündekâri, hem estetik hem de teknik açıdan önemli bir değere sahip bir işçilik yöntemidir. Ahşap malzeme, çevresel etkilere karşı korunması gereken bir malzeme olup, doğru malzeme seçimi ve yüksek işçilikle yapılan üretimle bu etkilere karşı koruma sağlanabilir. story: Kündekâri is a way of building wooden panels from small pieces that lock together, used widely in mosques. This 2025 study looks at the woodwork of the Afyon Paşa Mosque, also called the Umur Bey Mosque, in Türkiye, and at how the technique is done today. It asks how this skilled craft can be protected and kept alive.

Its record gives only the title and authors, so this is an outline.

Sanat ve zanaat karmaşasının tam ortasında konumlanan yorgancılık da tarihsel süreç içerisinde değişim gösteren kültürel anlamları ile günümüzde de varlığını sürdüren ve değişime ayak uyduran bir meslek alanı olarak karşımıza çıkmaktadır. Bu çalışma, Üsküdar’da günümüzde sayıları giderek azalan yorgan ustalarının anlatıları üzerinden yorgancılık mesleğini, meslek folkloru ve kent folkloru çerçevesinde ele almayı amaçlamaktadır. Araştırma, yorgancılığı “kayb

story: Quilt-making sits right between art and craft. This 2026 study visits the last quilt-makers of Üsküdar in Istanbul to see how a traditional trade has changed. Crafts like this carry living heritage, earn a living and help shape a city's culture. The quilt-makers are still working, but their world is shifting around them.

title: Julius Wolff'un Kemik Anatomisi Üzerine Çalışmaları ve Mekanik Adaptasyon Teorisinin Tıp ile Biyomekanikteki Evrimi
summary: Julius Wolff, XIX. yüzyılda kemiklerin mekanik yüklere adaptasyonunu inceleyerek tıp tarihinde önemli bir yer edinmiş ortopedi cerrahı ve anatomisttir. Wolff Yasası olarak bilinen teorisi, kemiklerin üzerlerine binen streslere göre şekil ve yoğunluklarını değiştirdiğini ortaya koyar. Bu yasa, kemiklerin mekanik streslere nasıl uyum sağladığını açıklar. Wolff'un çalışmaları, ortopedi, travmatoloji ve biyomekanik alanlarında temel bir prensip haline gelmiş, kırık tedavisi, implant tasarımı ve rehabilitasyon gibi birçok uygulamaya rehberlik etmiştir. story: Your bones reshape themselves depending on the loads you put on them. Julius Wolff, a 19th-century orthopaedic surgeon and anatomist, described this, and the idea is now called Wolff's Law: bones change their shape and density to suit the stresses they carry. This 2025 article follows how his idea spread through orthopaedics, trauma surgery and biomechanics.

title: Normatif Kabulden Yeni Normale: Beden-Giyim Kuşam ve Mahremiyet Algısının Kuşaklararası Dönüşümü
summary: Beden, yalnızca biyolojik ya da fizyolojik bir varlık olmanın ötesinde; toplumsal ilişkiler içerisinde anlam kazanan, kültürel ve ideolojik kodlarla biçimlenen çok katmanlı bir olgudur. Beden ile mahremiyet arasındaki ilişki, bedenin toplumsal normlar ve kültürel temsiller aracılığıyla şekillenen kamusal sunumunun, mahremiyetin sınırlarını ve algı biçimlerini belirlediği dinamik bir etkileşim olarak karşımıza çıkmaktadır. Günümüzde beden mahremiyetine ilişkin çeşitli anlayışlar; modernleşme, sekülerleşme, tüketim kültürü gibi çeşitli toplumsal dönüşümler çerçevesinde yeniden şekillenmekte, bu da konuyu hem medya ve gündelik yaşam pratiklerinde hem de akademik tartışmalarda güncel ve dikkat ç

story: The body is more than biology. It also carries social meaning and cultural codes. This 2025 study from Türkiye looks at how ideas about the body, clothing and privacy have changed from one generation to the next, moving from what used to be the accepted rule to a new normal.

title: İlhanlılarda Bir Eğitim Modeli: Medrese-yi Seyyâre
summary: XIII. yüzyılın başlarında gerçekleşen Moğol istilâsı, Yakın Doğu’nun ilmî ve kültürel yapısını derinden sarsmıştır. Cengiz Han ve haleflerinin gerçekleştirdiği bu harekât neticesinde birçok medrese, kütüphane ve rasathane tahrip edilmiş, pek çok âlim ve edip ya katledilmiş ya da ilmî faaliyetlerden uzaklaştırılmıştır. Ancak XIII. yüzyılın ikinci yarısından itibaren İlhanlıların siyasî birlik ve idarî istikrarı temin etmesiyle bölgede ilmî ve kültürel bir canlanma yaşanmıştır. Bu dönemde ilim, devletin öncelikli hedeflerinden biri hâline gelmiş ve birçok medrese inşa edilmiştir. Bu teşebbüsler arasında, seyyâr yapısıyla dikkat çeken Medrese-yi Seyyâre de müstesna bir yer tutmuştur. Sultan Ölc

story: In the early 1200s the Mongol invasions shook the learning of the Near East. Many madrasas, libraries and observatories were destroyed and many scholars were killed or driven from their work. This 2026 article looks at what came after, under the Ilkhanids: a madrasa on the move, the Medrese-yi Seyyâre, a school that travelled.

story: In Islamic law, renting was defined as selling the use of something for a price. That made it much wider than renting today. It covered movable goods and property, but also work contracts, transport deals and even the agreement between a patient and a doctor. This 2023 study reads old Ottoman court records from Ebüssuûd Efendi and Şânizâde to see how it worked.

title: Kaedah Terapi Muzik di Hospital (Darüşşifa) Era Kerajaan Seljuk Pada Abad ke-12M sehingga Abad ke-14M
summary: Abstrak: Hospital (darüşşifa) merupakan antara institusi sosial terawal yang dibangunkan oleh kerajaan Seljuk bagi menyediakan khidmat perubatan kepada masyarakat awam di Anatolia. Menariknya, darüşşifa dalam kerajaan Seljuk turut menggunakan terapi muzik sebagai salah satu kaedah bagi rawatan penyakit mental. Justeru, kajian ini dijalankan bagi mengenal pasti institusi darüşşifa dalam kerajaan Seljuk di Anatolia yang menawarkan rawatan terapi muzik sekaligus mengkaji kaedah pelaksanaan rawatan tersebut. Kajian ini menggunakan kaedah kualitatif dengan pendekatan reka bentuk kajian sejarah dan analisis kandungan berpandukan pelbagai sumber berautoriti dan seterusnya dianalisis menggunakan kae

story: Hospitals called darüşşifa were among the first public institutions the Seljuks built in Anatolia, giving medical care to ordinary people. Some of them used music therapy to treat mental illness. This 2022 Malaysian study looks at these hospitals from the 1100s to the 1300s and at how music was used inside them.

title: The Hijab Consumer Attitude toward Hijab Fashion Brand: A Case of the Developing Country
summary: Hijabi women, a rapidly expanding market segment in the fashion business, are drawn to fashion companies in search of modern fashions while respecting their religious obligations. This study examined the degree to which hijabi women were content with the design calibre, how it reflected their social and self-identities, and the degree to which they were willing to pay greater costs for certain fashion names. To achieve this, Hijabi women (n=198) were given structured online surveys, and the data were analyzed using SmartPLS Software. The findings show that hijabistas' willingness to pay higher costs is significantly influenced by the trendy nature of the design and how it reflects their soci

story: Hijabi women are a fast-growing group of fashion shoppers who want modern style that also respects their faith. This 2022 study from Pakistan asked how happy they were with hijab brands' designs, whether the brands reflected who they are, and whether they would pay more for certain names.

title: Conversational Etudes for Cello and Nay to Consolidate Arabic Rhythmic Patterns for Nay Students in Music Department of Yarmouk University

story: The nay is a reed flute heard across Arabic music. This 2024 Jordanian study wrote short duets for cello and nay to help nay students lock in Arabic rhythms. The exercises use rhythms common in Egypt and the Levant, with names like Malfouf, Samaii thaqeel and Wehda kabeera, and even the waltz and the fox.

title: Religious Tourism in Lahore: Case Study of Mosque Architecture under the Mughals
summary: The city of Lahore is well known for both its magnificent architecture and rich cultural legacy. Lahore saw a dramatic transition under the Mughal rule with the building of several famous mosques that continue to draw religious travelers from all over the world. This case study examines the possibilities for religious tourism keeping in view the Mughal era mosques of Lahore, while emphasizing their spiritual appeal and architectural value. The architectural integrity and beauty of these mosques require ongoing preservation and restoration efforts. Religious tourism in Lahore can boost the local economy by creating jobs, generating business revenue, and promoting cultural exchange, thus foste

story: Under Mughal rule, Lahore was transformed by the building of several famous mosques. Those mosques still draw religious travellers from all over the world. This 2023 case study asks how Lahore's Mughal-era mosques could support religious tourism, looking at their spiritual pull as well as their architecture.

title: Viability of Waqf for the realization of SDG–4 (Quality education) in Sokoto state, Nigeria
summary: Delving into the context of Sokoto State's educational landscape, it is identified that some challenges such as low enrolment rates, inadequate infrastructure, and socio-economic disparities affecting access to quality education in the state. story: Zakat is meant to lift people out of poverty. This 2024 study looked at the National Amil Zakat Agency in Merangin Regency, Indonesia, and asked how it collects zakat and hands it out to improve the local economy.

title: The MODERN MOSQUE ARCHITECTURE: A BALANCE BETWEEN GLOBALIZATION AND A SENSE OF REGIONAL IDENTITY
summary: Modern trends of the time require significant changes in the spatial planning, functional and artistic-image design of architectural objects, including religious buildings as mosques. With the changing pace of life characteristic of the era of globalization and the growing level of religious involvement in society, there is a need for new architectural trends. These changes concern both the functional and technological aspects as well as the visual characteristics of buildings, including mosques, which must meet the requirements of modernity. This fact implies the creation of architecture that can meet the needs of the religious community, ensure inclusiveness, sustainability and conformity

story: What should a mosque look like in a fast-changing world? This 2025 study from Kazakhstan looks at modern mosque design and asks how architects can balance global trends with a sense of local, regional identity.

It was written by Masoud Bater, Mahbobeh Rastin and published in Knowledge of Conservation and Restoration in 2025. Its record gives only the title and authors, so this is an outline.

title: Romancing the Sufi: Persian Sufi Poetry under the Western Gaze

story: Persian Sufi poetry became popular in the West. Iftikhar Shafi's 2018 article, "Romancing the Sufi," looks at how Western readers viewed this poetry, sometimes in romanticised ways.

title: Symbolic meaning in Islamic miniature art: A semiotic reading of a miniature by Al-Wasiti
summary: Islamic miniature art crystallized as a distinct form of creative practice across various pictorial schools, despite numerous Orientalist perspectives that dismissed it as marginal or lacking in clear symbolic depth. The features of this creative dimension are evident in the artist's ability to employ diverse artistic, religious, literary, and philosophical contexts shaped by multifaceted socio-cultural and historical interactions. In this context, painting representation in this art form emerges as a plastic interpretation – an aesthetic practice aimed at grounding the artistic act through expressive conceptualizations that forged a new and distinctive artistic vision. This research explore
creator: Habib ben Mohamed Zouinekh

story: Al-Wasiti was a painter of Islamic miniatures. Some Orientalists dismissed this kind of art as shallow, but this 2026 study disagrees. It reads one miniature by al-Wasiti closely, as a set of signs, to show how it draws on religion, literature and philosophy.

title: Maqasid al-Shari’ah in Islamic finance: Harmonizing theory and reality
summary: This paper aims to clarify how maqaṣid al-Shari’ah (objective of Shariah law) plays its role in Islamic finance, particularly in creating a harmony between Shariah rulings in theory and their application in current circumstances. Based on library research, this study applies inductive approach and descriptive method in analysing various literatures. The finding reveals that the roles of maqasid al-Shari’ah are identified as the following: harmonizing between the text of revelation and the actual situation; considering unusual circumstances and overcoming current issues. All of them reflect how maqasid al-Shariah could pragmatically adapt Shariah rulings into the real operation of Islamic fin
creator: Muhammad Shahrul Ifwat Ishak, Nur Syahirah Mohammad Nasir

locator: DOI=10.33102/jmifr.v18i1.334; journal="The Journal of Muamalat and Islamic Finance Research"
scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic finance"; publisher hosted in Malaysia
story: Maqasid al-Shari'ah means the goals behind Islamic law. This 2021 paper asks how those goals can help Islamic finance close the gap between the rulings on paper and what happens in real life today.

title: Pemerkasaan Keharmonian Masyarakat Beragama: Rujukan Pendekatan al-Biruni Berdasarkan Karyanya Kitab Al-Hind
summary: Research article in Jurnal Akidah & Pemikiran Islam by Samsuddin Abd Hamid, Khadijah Mohd Hambali @ Khambali, 2015.

source_name: Jurnal Akidah & Pemikiran Islam

story: A thousand years ago, al-Biruni wrote Kitab al-Hind, a careful study of India's religions. This Malaysian article asks whether his approach can help strengthen harmony between religious communities today. It was written by Samsuddin Abd Hamid, Khadijah Mohd Hambali @ Khambali and published in Jurnal Akidah & Pemikiran Islam in 2015. Its record gives only the title and authors, so this is an outline.

title: Mother Tongue Interference on Arabic Language Communicative Skills among Junior Secondary School Islamic Studies Students in Asa, Kwara State, Nigeria
summary: This paper examines the influence of mother tongue interference on Arabic communicative skills among junior secondary school Islamic Studies students in Asa, Kwara State, Nigeria. The objective is to explore how mother tongue interference affects students' ability to acquire and effectively use Arabic for communication. Findings reveal that students' acquisition of effective communicative skills in the Arabic language is significantly hindered by the phonological, syntactic, and semantic interference of their native languages. This linguistic interference poses a major challenge to students' proficiency in Arabic, which is essential for their academic and religious studies. The paper recomme
source_name: SIBAWAYH Arabic Language and Education
locator: DOI=10.37134/sibawayh.vol6.1.8.2025; journal="SIBAWAYH Arabic Language and Education"
scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic education nigeria"; publisher hosted in Malaysia
story: Your first language can get in the way when you learn another. This 2025 study looked at junior secondary school students of Islamic studies in Asa, Kwara State, Nigeria, and found that their mother tongue affected how well they could speak and communicate in Arabic.

title: Assessment of Alienation among the Madrasa Students of Kashmir Valley
summary: Background: In the Muslim world Madrasa is the main source of education. Throughout the world Madrasas are imparting education to Muslim students. Due to lack of modern education and Urdu medium system in the Madrasa, the students enrolled in these Madrasa could not compete with the other students. So, they face lot of problems in making their psychological and social adjustment. They get alienated from themselves and their society because their degree‟s are not recognized anywhere. This creates lot of difficulties in getting jobs. Objective: The main objective of paper is to assess the level of alienation among male and female madrasa students. Method: The present study was conducted on the
creator: Mohammad Ashraf Malik
source_name: International Journal of Indian Psychology
locator: DOI=10.25215/0202.057; journal="International Journal of Indian Psychology"
scope_basis: Crossref search "madrasa senegal"; publisher hosted in India
story: In Kashmir, many Muslim students learn in madrasas, schools taught largely in Urdu with little modern subject teaching. This 2015 study by Mohammad Ashraf Malik asks what that costs them. Its starting point is a hard problem: when a degree is not recognised anywhere, finding a job gets difficult, and students can end up feeling cut off from themselves and their society. The paper set out to measure that feeling of alienation in both male and female madrasa students.

title: Characteristics of Guidance and Instruction in Islamic Art Stylization
summary: Research article in Fnon Al-Rafidayn Journal by Ruwaida Waadallah, 2024.

story: Islamic art turns natural forms into stylised patterns. This 2024 Iraqi study by Ruwaida Waadallah, in the Fnon Al-Rafidayn Journal, looks at the guiding features and instruction behind stylisation in Islamic art.

title: Management of Waqf Funds in Libyan Law
summary: Endowed funds require someone to preserve, care for, and manage their affairs in terms of exploitation, whether that is represented by construction, rent, or distributing the proceeds to those entitled to them, protecting them from others, preventing any aggression against them, and claiming all their rights, regardless of their hand and wherever they are found. All of this is in order for the endowment to continue for the purpose for which it was established. Therefore, it is inconceivable that an endowment could exist without a guardian. The person in charge of establishing the endowment is called the supervisor, the guardian, or the trustee. This research aims to identify and reveal the m
creator: Salem Milad Al-Saedi
source_name: مجلة الحق للعلوم الشرعية والقانونية
locator: DOI=10.58916/alhaq.v12i1.289; journal="مجلة الحق للعلوم الشرعية والقانونية"
scope_basis: Crossref search "waqf innovation"; publisher hosted in Libya
story: A waqf is an endowment: money or property given so that its income serves a purpose forever. But "forever" needs someone in charge. This 2025 paper from Libya, by Salem Milad Al-Saedi, starts from a simple point: an endowment cannot exist without a guardian. That person, called the supervisor, guardian or trustee, has to look after it, rent or build on it, hand out its income to the right people and defend its rights. The paper looks at how Libyan law handles that job.

title: The Influence of Hindu-Buddhist, Chinese, and European Culture in Exterior Architectural Characteristics of Mosque on Java Island Indonesia

story: Mosques on Java don't all look Middle Eastern. This 2024 study looks at how Hindu-Buddhist, Chinese and European culture shaped their outside architecture. Its record says little more than this, so this is an outline.

title: The local features in the Islamic architecture
summary: Islamic architecture has spread in a wide geographical regions, covering many areas and cities with distinct civilizations, Most of these areas and cities imposed their local architectural features on the forms of Islamic buildings in these areas due to the flexibility that characterized the process of composition output of Islamic architecture represented in different functional patterns as mosques, palaces, schools, baths and markets. This paper tries to study in-depth the existence of these local features and its assets in a range of distinct civilized areas covered by Islamic architecture. Reviewing previous studies concerning the research topic revealed the problem of the research which

source_name: Iraqi Journal of Architecture and Planning
locator: DOI=10.36041/2617-9555.1231; journal="Iraqi Journal of Architecture and Planning"
scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic architecture"; publisher hosted in Iraq
story: Why does a mosque in one city look so different from a mosque in another? This 2026 paper from Iraq, by Ahmad Abdulwahid Thannoon, argues that Islamic architecture spread across many regions, and each place pressed its own local features onto the buildings. Mosques, palaces, schools, baths and markets all bent to local traditions, because the way Islamic buildings were designed was flexible. The paper studies those local features across several regions.

title: Behavioral Approach Towards Islamic Finance in Pakistan: A Preliminary Investigation
summary: Islamic financial practices emphasize on the instillation of Islamic laws in the practices that are considered ethical in this world. The purpose of this paper is to determine the factors of Islamic banking promotion among Pakistani educated community. Demographic factors, attitude and financial recommendation items were examined to determine the influence of these factors in promoting ethical financial instruments. The paper follows quantitative research in nature. It explored more than two theories. After a conceptual analysis of the theory of reasoned action (TRA) and theory of planned behavior, this paper investigates the impact of ethical behavior towards the selection of Islamic financ
creator: Huma Nawaz, Shamaila Nawaz
source_name: Islamic Banking and Finance Review

story: Islamic banking follows rules meant to keep money ethical. But what makes an ordinary person choose it? This 2025 study by Huma Nawaz and Shamaila Nawaz asked educated people in Pakistan. It looked at their background, their attitudes and the financial advice they got, using two well-known theories of how beliefs turn into actions. The question underneath is whether ethical behaviour actually drives people towards Islamic finance.

title: The Muslim Culinary in Ho Chi Minh City
summary: Ḥalāl food is a common feature in Muslim lives across the world. In Muslim quarters of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, locally-made food products are self-recognized as ḥalāl by the community. Ḥalāl food self-recognition is a tradition that exists within closed Muslim communities based on a process of production and consumption standardized by Muslims alone. However, the urban culinary scene has changed as the Vietnamese government issued policies for enhancing the tourism industry and exhorting Muslim enterprises to produce their typical local products. Using qualitative research methods in combination with document analysis, this article shows the sophisticated and varied culinary trade techniq
creator: Tu Anh Phan
source_name: Islamic Studies
scope_basis: Crossref search "culinary tradition muslim"; publisher hosted in Pakistan
story: In the Muslim quarters of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, halal food was traditionally judged halal by the community itself, with Muslims making and eating it under their own rules. Then the government began pushing tourism and encouraging Muslim businesses to sell their local specialities. This 2024 article by Tu Anh Phan, using interviews and documents, shows how varied and clever the community's food trade became as it opened up to the wider city.

title: Improving Halal Food Performance: Scrutinising the Technology Acceptance Model and Halal Traceability System Adoption among Malaysian Food and Beverage SMEs
summary: Halal Traceability Systems (HTS) play an important role in enhancing the competitiveness of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), preserving halal integrity, and improving supply chain transparency. However, limited empirical evidence exists on how cognitive beliefs influence HTS adoption and whether such adoption contributes to financial performance. This study examines the effects of perceived usefulness (PU) and perceived ease of use (PEOU) on the intention to adopt HTS and investigates the impact of adoption intention on the financial performance of halal food among Malaysian food and beverage (F&B) SMEs. The mediating role of HTS adoption intention is also assessed. A quantitative

story: How do you prove the chicken in your burger is really halal? One answer is a halal traceability system, which tracks food along its whole supply chain. This 2026 study by Haslinda Hadis surveyed small food and drink businesses in Malaysia to see whether owners adopt such systems because they find them useful and easy, and whether adopting them actually improves the business's finances.

title: Caracterización de la gestión de residuos hospitalarios y similares en cami vista hermosa, Bogota
summary: Antecedentes. La gestión ambiental de los residuos, se enmarca en la política pública, la cual involucra los residuos de carácter peligroso de una forma generalizada. creator: Juan Carlos Hernández-Criado

story: What happens to the needles, bandages and other waste a hospital throws away? In Colombia, rules for managing hospital waste only arrived in 2000. This 2016 study by Juan Carlos Hernández-Criado looked closely at one public health centre, CAMI Vista Hermosa in Bogotá, measuring and describing how its waste was handled. It is a snapshot of the hidden work that keeps a clinic's rubbish from becoming a danger.

title: AFYONKARAHİSAR’DA TEPME KEÇEDEN ÜRETİLEN CAMİ KAPI PERDELERİ

Yerli yünden yapılan keçe perdelerin esnememesi ve daha dayanıklı olması için kenarları deri ile çevrelenmektedir. Keçe ustası ve saraç ustası keçe perdeyi iş bölümü yaparak üretmektedir. creator: Ülkü KÜÇÜKKURT

story: In Afyonkarahisar, a cold, snowy city in Turkey, some mosques still hang thick felt curtains in their doorways to keep out the winter. This 2023 study by Ülkü Küçükkurt explains how they are made. The felt is pressed from local wool by hand, and its edges are wrapped in leather, often calf skin, so it does not stretch. It takes two craftsmen: a felt master and a saddler, each doing their own part.

story: Üsküdar University's Faculty of Medicine in Istanbul has started work towards accreditation of its medical education, a check that its teaching meets set standards. This 2024 news report from the university announces the step.

title: Climate Change and Environmental Ethics in Islam: A Global Responsibility Analyzing Islamic Teachings on Stewardship (Khilāfah) and Sustainability
summary: Research article in Pakistan Social Sciences Review, 2026.

scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic environmental ethics"; publisher hosted in Pakistan
story: Can religious teachings help with climate change? This 2026 article looks at Islamic ideas of stewardship, called khilafah, and sustainability, treating care for the environment as a global responsibility.

title: Maqasid al-Shariah and Artificial Intelligence: An Islamic Ethical Framework for the Digital Era
summary: The exponential proliferation of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies has precipitated an ethical vacuum in global governance frameworks, with secular regulatory instruments struggling to address the metaphysical and teleological dimensions of autonomous systems. This paper proposes a normative jurisprudential framework grounded in Maqasid al-Shariah (the higher objectives of Islamic law) for the ethical governance of AI. Drawing on the five essential objectives (al-daruriyyat al-khamsah), namely the preservation of life (hifz al-nafs), intellect (hifz al-aql), wealth (hifz al-mal), lineage (hifz al-nasl), and religion (hifz al-din), this study maps each Maqasid onto four pressing AI us
creator: Asad Ibrahim, Arshad Ali
source_name: Islamic Reports
scope_basis: Crossref search "artificial intelligence islamic"; publisher hosted in Malaysia
story: Can rules written centuries ago guide artificial intelligence? This 2026 paper by Asad Ibrahim and Arshad Ali thinks so. It uses Maqasid al-Shariah, the five higher goals of Islamic law: protecting life, intellect, wealth, family line and religion. It maps each goal onto pressing questions about how AI is used, offering a framework for judging technology by what it does to people.

title: Linguistic Halal Readiness: Assessing Arabic Proficiency as a Driver of Service Innovation in Malaysia's Halal Wellness Tourism Policy
summary: This study's goal is to assess whether proficiency in the Arabic language will act as a strategic facilitator in the areas of quality of service and innovation in Malaysia's halal tourism and wellness sectors. This study used two types of qualitative content analyses: Directed Qualitative Content Analysis (DQCA) and Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA) for the evaluation of 47 primary and secondary sources (2020–2026) related to Malaysian national policy, international industry reports, halal wellness standards, Arabic language education frameworks, and scholarly articles written in English. Based on linguistic capital theory proposed by Bourdieu (1991), the findings are categorized along four
creator: Wilailak Wisetrat, Djamel Mahamedi
source_name: Social Reports
scope_basis: Crossref search "halal innovation"; publisher hosted in Malaysia
story: Malaysia wants visitors to come for halal wellness holidays. This 2026 study by Wilailak Wisetrat and Djamel Mahamedi asks whether speaking Arabic could give that industry an edge. It analysed 47 sources from 2020 to 2026, from national policy to industry reports, and treated language as a kind of capital, an idea from the sociologist Bourdieu. The thought is simple: if staff can speak a guest's language, the service changes.

title: Hyperlipidemia and the Role of Blood Lipids According to Iranian Traditional Medicine
summary: Objective: The first and most common cause of death in the world is due to cardiovascular diseases, and hyperlipidemia is one of the important and a critical controllable risk factors for these diseases. The connection between fat metabolism and a wide range of diseases, side effects of chemical drugs, and the increasing attention to the use of natural remedies reveal the necessity of further attention to the viewpoints of other schools of medicine, including complementary medicine. This review study aims to interpret hyperlipidemia from the perspective of Iranian Traditional Medicine (ITM). Methods: This is review study conducted based on a library method using the keywords related to hyper
creator: Alireza Niknafs, Mohamad Reza Rezvanfar
source_name: Complementary Medicine Journal
scope_basis: Crossref search "traditional medicine muslim"; publisher hosted in Iran
story: Heart disease is the world's biggest killer, and high blood fat, or hyperlipidemia, is one risk people can control. This 2021 review by Alireza Niknafs and Mohamad Reza Rezvanfar goes back to old books of Iranian Traditional Medicine to see how that school explained fat in the blood. It is an attempt to read a modern problem through a much older way of thinking about the body.

title: Sosyal Girişimcilik Boyutunda Kütüphaneler
summary: Günümüz teknolojilerinin hızla gelişmesiyle birlikte birçok kurum ve kuruluşun işlevi ve çalışma şekli değişmektedir. Bu değişim kütüphaneleri de doğrudan etkilemektedir. Kütüphanelerin belli başlı temel görevleri bulunmaktadır. Ancak gelişen teknolojilerle birlikte kütüphanelerin görev ve sorumlulukları da değişmektedir. Bu değişime uyum sağlamak yeni yöntemlerin benimsenmesi yolu ile gerçekleştirilebilir. Sosyal girişimcilik kavramı kütüphane hizmetlerinin yeniden planlanıp ele alınmasında yararlı bir olgu olarak ele alınabilir. Bu sayede kütüphanelerin geleneksel görev ve sorumluluk tanımlarının dışına çıkarak sosyal değer yaratabilmesi mümkün olacaktır. Günümüzde kütüphanelerin toplumsal
creator: Ece Helvacıoğlu
source_name: Bilgi Dünyası
scope_basis: Crossref search "ahilik girişimcilik"; publisher hosted in Türkiye
story: Libraries are changing fast as technology changes. This 2013 article by Ece Helvacıoğlu, from Turkey, suggests libraries could borrow an idea from business: social entrepreneurship, which means running something to create value for society. Thinking that way, it argues, would let libraries step beyond their traditional jobs of storing and lending books and do more good for the people around them.

title: Unlocking Halal Food Performance: Exploring Technology Acceptance Model and Halal Traceability System Adoption in Malaysia's Food and Beverage SMEs
summary: The global halal food market has growing demands especially concerning transparency and compliance along halal food supply chains. Malaysia aims to position itself as a global Halal food hub, where the food and beverage (F&B) small and medium enterprises (SMEs) are critical in upholding halal credibility. However, due to resource constraints and a lack of technological readiness, these SMEs face challenges in adopting advanced technologies. This study examines the Halal traceability system adoption of Malaysian F&B SMEs through the lens of the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM). More specifically, it explores the relationships of perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use to the halal tra
creator: Haslinda Hadis, Azaze-Azizi Abdul Adis, Masran Tamin
source_name: Asean Entrepreneurship Journal
scope_basis: Crossref search "halal food"; publisher hosted in Malaysia
story: Malaysia wants to be a world hub for halal food, and small food and drink businesses are key to that. But they often lack money and tech know-how. This 2026 study by Haslinda Hadis, Azaze-Azizi Abdul Adis and Masran Tamin looks at whether these firms take up halal traceability systems, which track food along its supply chain, and how much that depends on the systems seeming useful and easy to use.

title: Revisiting Omani Legacy in Malaya through the Royal Kedah Dress: Reassessment
summary: This paper seeks to examine the legacy of the Omani presence in the states of Malaysia, which arguably has made itself apparent in the royal dress of the Kedah Sultanate. This discovery indeed calls for further investigation, especially on how the Omani dress later became a model for Kedah royal dress which is famously known as Baju Muskat. Further analysis is essential to determine to what extent did the Kedah Sultanate adopted the Omani dress of the Muscati style and what aspects of the Kedah royal dress resemble the Omani dress substantially. source_name: Journal of Islamic Thought and Civilization
locator: DOI=10.32350/jitc.121.03; journal="Journal of Islamic Thought and Civilization"
scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic dress textile"; publisher hosted in Pakistan
story: The royal court of Kedah in Malaysia has a famous outfit called the Baju Muskat. The name points to Muscat, in Oman. This 2022 paper by Mohamad Firdaus Mansor Majdin, Rahmah Ahmad H. Osman and Fauziah Fathil asks whether Omani dress really became the model for Kedah's royal clothes. Its early findings are careful: there are only a few clear similarities, so the link needs more work.

title: The Invocation of Article 19 of the Moroccan Constitution at the Boundary of the Second Legislature
summary: This article analyzes the King of Morocco’s invocation of Article 19 of the Constitution at a critical moment between legislative periods. It examines the constitutional basis, political context, and institutional implications of this use of royal authority, and discusses its significance for Moroccan constitutional practice and the functioning of political institutions.
creator: Abderrahmane Amalou
source_name: Revue Marocaine de Droit, d'Economie et de Gestion (Moroccan Journal of Law, Economics and Management)

scope_basis: Crossref search "moroccan zellige"; publisher hosted in Morocco
story: Article 19 of Morocco's constitution deals with royal authority. This 2026 article by Abderrahmane Amalou looks at a moment when the King used it right at the boundary between two parliaments, and asks what that meant: its legal basis, the politics around it, and what it says about how Morocco's institutions work.

title: Nakş-ı Cihan Meydanı: Mekân, Mimari ve Kronoloji
summary: XVI. yüzyılın sonlarında Safevî Devleti’nin üçüncü payitahtı tayin edilen İsfahan, saray ve hanedan mensuplarının himaye ettiği inşa faaliyetleri sayesinde pek çok yeni kentsel mekân ve anıtsal yapı kazanmış ve yeni bir başkente dönüşmüştür. Yeni payitahtın en önemli kentsel mekânları arasında, I. Abbas’ın himayesinde başkentin yeni ticari, dinî, sosyal ve törensel merkezi olarak inşa edilen Nakş-ı Cihan Meydanı yer alır. İsfahan’ın Safevî payitahtı olmadan önceki ticari, dinî ve sosyal-törensel merkezi olan Harun-ı Velayet Meydanı’nın güneyinde yer alan Nakş-ı Cihan Meydanı, dört kenarı farklı işlevlere sahip yapılarla çevrelenmiş, geniş dikdörtgen bir mekândır. Meydanın etrafı, iki sıralı
creator: Damla Gürkan Anar
source_name: Belleten
scope_basis: Crossref search "osmanlı mimari"; publisher hosted in Türkiye
story: At the end of the 1500s, Isfahan became the third capital of the Safavid empire in Iran, and its rulers built a new heart for the city. Under Shah Abbas I, they laid out Naqsh-e Jahan Square, a huge rectangle south of the old main square. Each of its four sides held buildings with different jobs: trade, religion, social life and ceremony. This 2024 study by Damla Gürkan Anar traces how the square was planned and built.

title: Prof. Dr. Yumuşhan Günay: “Sosyal medya paylaşımları diş estetiğine talebi artırdı”
summary: Prof. Dr. Yumuşhan Günay, sosyal medyada yapılan paylaşımların etkisiyle diş hekimi istihdamının öne çıktığını söyledi.
source_name: üha
scope_basis: Crossref search "sosyal medya din"; publisher hosted in Türkiye
story: Prof. Dr. Yumuşhan Günay says social media posts have raised demand for good-looking teeth, putting dentists in demand. This 2023 news piece is from Türkiye. Its record says little more than this, so this is an outline.

title: Perceptions, practices, and fasting patterns of pregnant women during Ramadan: a multi-center study in Rawalpindi and Islamabad
summary: Research article in Khyber Medical University Journal, 2025.
source_name: Khyber Medical University Journal
scope_basis: Crossref search "ramadan fasting health"; publisher hosted in Pakistan
story: Should pregnant women fast in Ramadan, and how do they? This 2025 study, carried out in Ramadan 1444 in Rawalpindi and Islamabad, Pakistan, asked pregnant women about their views, their fasting patterns and their sleep.

title: Türk yemek kültüründe esnaf lokantaları
summary: Esnaf lokantaları yıllar boyu çevrelerinde yer alan esnafa Türk yemek örneklerini makul fiyatlarla sunan lezzet duraklarıdır. Esnaf tanımına iş yerlerinde çalışanlar, ticaretle uğraşanlar ve işletme sahipleri girmektedir. Esnaf lokantalarının bazıları mikro ölçekte olsa da genellikle küçük işletmelerdir. Yaşadıkları sorunlara bağlı olarak zaman içinde kapananların dışında, ülkemizdeki esnaf lokantalarının bir bölümü halen üçüncü-dördüncü kuşak ve/veya el değiştirme yoluyla günümüzde de varlıklarını sürdürmektedir. Esnaf lokantaları Türk mutfağına özgü yemekleri ile son yıllarda gastronomi turizminden pay alabilecek bir potansiyele sahiptir. Günümüzde seyahat eden altı turistten biri gastrono
creator: Bahar Taner, Şule Çetin
source_name: Toros University Journal of Food, Nutrition and Gastronomy
locator: DOI=10.58625/jfng-2092; journal="Toros University Journal of Food, Nutrition and Gastronomy"
scope_basis: Crossref search "geleneksel yemek"; publisher hosted in Türkiye
story: In Turkey, esnaf lokantası means "tradesmen's restaurant": small places that serve Turkish dishes at fair prices to the shopkeepers and workers nearby. Some are now run by the third or fourth generation of the same family. This 2023 study by Bahar Taner and Şule Çetin argues they could draw food tourists, noting that one in six travellers today is a food tourist.

title: Undermining the Familiar and Embodiment Content in Arabic Calligraphy
summary: Contrary to deconstruction and its destructive pursuit, the concept of undermining the familiar seeks to refute the constants and its known limitations. It is done through the process of receiving and what is imposed by the formation of the word or text or the structural and design structure in general, along with the Arabic calligraphy in particular. This is based on the recipient's understanding and interpretation of the dual phenomenon and the content's manifestation. More accurately, the disclosure of its reality through its expressive phenomenology; for that sake, the research was devoted to studying “undermining the familiar and embodiment content in Arabic calligraphy” including four
creator: Mohammed Radhee Ghadheb, Oday Abdulhameed Majeed, Furat Jamal Hassan
source_name: Journal of Islamic Thought and Civilization
locator: DOI=10.32350/jitc.131.04; journal="Journal of Islamic Thought and Civilization"
scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic calligraphy art"; publisher hosted in Pakistan
story: Arabic calligraphy is writing that is also art. This 2023 paper by Mohammed Radhee Ghadheb, Oday Abdulhameed Majeed and Furat Jamal Hassan studies an idea it calls "undermining the familiar": breaking the expected rules of how a word or text is shaped, so a viewer has to look again. The paper looks at how meaning shows itself through that surprise, in calligraphy and in design more widely.

title: The Influence of Maqashid Shariah-Based Innovation on Startup Sustainability: Evidence from Indonesian Muslim Entrepreneurs
summary: This study investigates the influence of Maqashid Shariah-based innovation on startup sustainability among Muslim entrepreneurs in Indonesia. Using a quantitative approach and Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), the research examines how innovations aligned with the five objectives of Shariah—protection of religion, life, intellect, progeny, and wealth—contribute to the economic, social, and environmental sustainability of startups. The model also explores the moderating role of religio-ethical commitment in strengthening these relationships. Data were collected from 280 Muslim startup founders operating in various halal-related sectors, including food, fashion, fin
creator: Zulfikar Hasan
source_name: Journal of Contemporary Issues and Thought
locator: DOI=10.37134/jcit.vol16.1.10.2026; journal="Journal of Contemporary Issues and Thought"
scope_basis: Crossref search "startup muslim"; publisher hosted in Malaysia
story: Does running a business by Islamic values help it survive? This 2026 study by Zulfikar Hasan surveyed 280 Muslim startup founders in Indonesia, working in halal food, fashion and more. It tested whether innovations linked to the five goals of Islamic law, protecting religion, life, intellect, family and wealth, made startups more sustainable economically, socially and environmentally.

title: Kyrgyzstan: Compliance with banking legislation, Islamic banking department in accordance with AAOIFI Islamic Sharia standards
summary: Research article in Eurasian Journal of Religious studies by M. Shoev, 2023.

story: Kyrgyzstan's banks have an Islamic banking department. This 2023 article looks at whether it follows AAOIFI's Sharia standards. It was written by M. Shoev and published in Eurasian Journal of Religious studies in 2023. Its record gives only the title and authors, so this is an outline.

title: Giovanni Maria Martini, ed. Visualizing Sufism: Studies on Graphic Representations in Sufi Literature (13th to 16th Century).
summary: Research article in Islamic Studies by Carimo Mohomed, 2024.

story: Sufi writers sometimes used diagrams and pictures. This 2024 review by Carimo Mohomed looks at a book edited by Giovanni Maria Martini, Visualizing Sufism, on graphic images in Sufi literature from the 1200s to the 1500s.

title: Accessing the Synergy between Islamic Finance and Economic Development: A Systematic literature Review (2021–2024)
summary: Recent years have seen a rise in scholarly and policy interest in the connection between Islamic finance and economic development; yet, empirical results are still conflicting and context-dependent. In order to evaluate the overall influence of Islamic financing on economic development across various economies, this study does a meta-analytical evaluation of material produced between 2021 and 2024. This paper finds regional differences, methodological trends, and recurrent themes in the relationship between Islamic financing and growth by combining findings from theoretical and empirical research. The analysis shows that Islamic finance's profit-and-loss sharing, risk-sharing procedures, and
creator: Mehwish Malik, Bilal Sarwar
source_name: Islamic Banking and Finance Review
locator: DOI=10.32350/ibfr.131.05; journal="Islamic Banking and Finance Review"
scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic finance"; publisher hosted in Pakistan
story: Does Islamic finance actually help countries grow? Researchers disagree, and results change by place. This 2026 review by Mehwish Malik and Bilal Sarwar pulls together studies from 2021 to 2024 to find the patterns. It points to features like profit-and-loss sharing and risk-sharing, where the bank and the borrower share the ups and downs instead of one side carrying all the risk.

title: Developing Standards for Mosque Design in Lahore, Pakistan
summary: Research article in Journal of Islamic Thought and Civilization by Muhamamd Ilyas Malik, Beenish Mujahid, 2019.

story: Lahore in Pakistan has many mosques. This 2019 study in the Journal of Islamic Thought and Civilization proposes standards for designing mosques in Lahore, to guide how new ones are built.

title: Islamic Education in the Era of Artificial Intelligence: the Prospects and Challenges
summary: This paper explores the intersection of Islamic education and artificial intelligence (AI), delving into the prospects and challenges that arise in the AI era. The introduction establishes the relevanceof addressing this intersection, emphasizing the need to ensure the compatibility of technological advancements with Islamic principles. The prospects section examines how AI can enhance Islamic education, focusing on aspects such as personalized learning, global collaboration, and improved accessibility. Concurrently, the challenges section explores cultural considerations, ethical dilemmas, accessibility issues, and potential biases in AI algorithms. The methodology includes primary sources
creator: Muhammad Jumat Dasuki
source_name: Kunduz University International Journal of Islamic Studies and Social Sciences
locator: DOI=10.71082/4jb41h82; journal="Kunduz University International Journal of Islamic Studies and Social Sciences"
scope_basis: Crossref search "artificial intelligence islamic"; publisher hosted in Afghanistan
story: What happens when artificial intelligence meets Islamic education? This 2025 paper by Muhammad Jumat Dasuki weighs both sides. AI could make learning personal, connect students worldwide and widen access. It also raises cultural and ethical worries, gaps in who can use it, and the risk of bias in algorithms. The aim is to keep new tools in step with Islamic principles.

title: Effect of Ramadan Fasting on Lipid Profile
summary: Research article in Research Journal Of Medical Sciences by K.R. Hasna Parveen, M. Anita, H.R. Haribabu, 2025.

story: Does fasting in Ramadan change the fats in your blood? This 2025 study by K.R. Hasna Parveen and colleagues looks at the effect of Ramadan fasting on the lipid profile, which includes cholesterol and triglycerides.

title: Role of Media Professionals in News Production on Al Hayat Radio And Radio Jordan on the Credibility of Media News: A Comparative Study
summary: The study aims to reveal the role that media professionals have in producing news materials on Al Hayat Radio and Jordan Radio. An analytical and descriptive approach is indicated in order to achieve the research objectives. The questionnaire is used as a data collection tool. The research includes a sample of 80 directors from Radio Al-Hayat and Jordanian Radio in Jordan. The results of the research reveal that the level of the role that news managers have in the production of news materials in Radio Al-Hayat and Jordan Radio is at a high level, and there are statistically significant differences in the level of skills that news managers possess in producing news materials. creator: Ibrahim Mohammad Abdallah AlBreizat, Wesam Almahallawi, Suria Hani A. Rahman

locator: DOI=10.33102/jcicom.vol1no2.20; journal="Al-i’lam - Journal of Contemporary Islamic Communication and Media"
scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic radio"; publisher hosted in Malaysia
story: Why do people trust some news more than other news? This 2021 study compared two stations in Jordan, Al Hayat Radio and Radio Jordan. Researchers Ibrahim AlBreizat, Wesam Almahallawi and Suria Hani A. Rahman surveyed 80 news directors about their role in making the news. It found those managers play a big part, and that their skills vary in measurable ways.

title: Agricultural Development and Popular Participation in Senegal
summary: Focusing on Senegal, this paper argues that agricultural development can succeed only if rural populations participate directly and effectively in its implementation. After placing agriculture at the center of development strategy in the Third World, the author reviews Senegal’s post-independence experience in administrative reform, rural institutions, training, and support structures. The article stresses the need for fair prices, adequate public investment, better-trained rural cadres, stronger agricultural services, and policies that connect growth with social justice. It presents popular participation not as a slogan, but as a necessary condition for sustainable agricultural transformati
creator: Moussa Ndoye
source_name: Revue Marocaine de Droit, d'Economie et de Gestion (Moroccan Journal of Law, Economics and Management)

scope_basis: Crossref search "moroccan zellige"; publisher hosted in Morocco
story: Can farming improve if the farmers themselves have no say? This 2026 paper by Moussa Ndoye, looking at Senegal, says no. It reviews the country's farming policy since independence and argues that rural people must take part directly. It also calls for fair prices, public investment, better-trained rural staff, and growth that comes with social justice. Popular participation, it says, is a necessity, not a slogan.

title: Erken Çocukluk Eğitiminde Astronomi Etkinliklerinin Bilimsel Süreç Becerilerine Etkisi
summary: Bu araştırmanın amacı, okul öncesi dönemde uygulanan astronomi etkinliklerinin çocukların bilimsel süreç becerileri üzerindeki etkisini incelemektir. Çalışma, Adana ilinde bulunan iki okul öncesi eğitim kurumunda öğrenim gören, 48-72 ay yaş aralığındaki toplam 178 çocuk ile gerçekleştirilmiştir. Araştırmada, ön test-son test kontrol gruplu yarı deneysel desen kullanılmıştır. Veri toplama aracı olarak Kavak ve Gül (2021) tarafından geliştirilen “Bilimsel Süreç Becerileri Ölçeği” uygulanmıştır. Ön testlerin ardından deney grubuna sekiz etkinlikten oluşan astronomi etkinlik seti uygulanmış, sonrasında her iki gruba son test uygulanarak veriler toplanmıştır. creator: Mehmet Tunahan Saltan, Gökhan Güneş
source_name: Yaşadıkça Eğitim
scope_basis: Crossref search "astronomi tarihi"; publisher hosted in Türkiye
story: Can stargazing make small children better scientists? This 2026 study by Mehmet Tunahan Saltan and Gökhan Güneş worked with 178 children aged four to six at two preschools in Adana, Turkey. One group did a set of eight astronomy activities, and the other did not. Both groups were tested on scientific skills, like observing and predicting, before and after, to see what the stars had changed.

title: The Archetype and Shifting Morphology of Sri Lankan Mosque Architecture
summary: Sri Lanka is home to a number of historic mosques that date back over a thousand years and were built during various eras. In an attempt to fill the knowledge gap on such topic, particularly in regard to the built context of historic mosques in Sri Lanka, this paper illustrates the plan typology of mosques and compares them with the known Muslims architectural typologies. Is the design of the historical mosques in Sri Lanka related to a particular Islamic architectural style? Was the primary inquiry driving the study? creator: Jesmil Abdul Raheem

locator: DOI=10.51879/pijssl/060402; journal="Praxis International Journal of Social Science and Literature"
scope_basis: Crossref search "mosque architecture"; publisher hosted in Libya
story: Sri Lanka has mosques that date back more than a thousand years. Did they follow a known Islamic style, or something of their own? This 2023 study by Jesmil Abdul Raheem compares the floor plans of these historic mosques with well-known Muslim building types, to see how closely they match. It fills a gap, because the island's mosque architecture has been little studied.

title: Çevrim İçi Yemek Tariflerine Yönelik Betimsel Bir İnceleme: Nefis Yemek Tarifleri Web Sitesi Örneği A Descriptive Review of Online Food Recipes: The Case of Nefis Yemek Tarifleri Web Site

story: Millions of people find recipes online. This 2017 Turkish study by Enes Güleç and Kutay Oktay describes recipes on Nefis Yemek Tarifleri, a popular Turkish recipe website, to see what they look like.

title: Investigating the Structure of Traditional, Contemporary and Post-Islamic Revolution Mosques via the Method of Space Syntax (Case Study: Jameh Mosque of Isfahan, University of Tehran Mosque, Al-Ghadir Mosque, Shahrak-e Gharb Mosque)
summary: Research article in Scientific Journal of Maremat and Me mari-e by Jamal-e-Din Mahdi Nejad, Hamidreza Azemati, 2020.

story: Do mosques built after Iran's Islamic Revolution use space differently? This study compares traditional, modern and post-revolution mosques using a method called space syntax. It was written by Jamal-e-Din Mahdi Nejad, Hamidreza Azemati and published in Scientific Journal of Maremat and Me mari-e in 2020. Its record gives only the title and authors, so this is an outline.

title: Türk Minyatür Sanatında Cennet
summary: Dinlerin birçoğunda ölüm sonrasında ikinci hayat söz konusudur. Kişi öldükten sonra ya da her şeyin yok olması anlamına gelen kıyametten sonra ikinci bir hayat başlayacaktır. Bu hayatta, dünyada iken iyi işler yapanlar rahat edecek, kötü işler yapanlar ise sıkıntıda olacaktır. İslam kültürüne göre de kıyametten sonra ikinci bir hayat olacak ve iyi insanlar yeni yaşamlarını cennette geçireceklerdir. İslam toplumlarının cennet tasavvuru ile ilgili bilgileri içeren çok sayıda eser mevcuttur. Ancak insanların cennetle ilgili ayrıntıları anlayış biçimini en güzel resimlerde görmek mümkündür. creator: Bahattin Yaman
source_name: Belleten
scope_basis: Crossref search "minyatür sanatı"; publisher hosted in Türkiye
story: How do you paint paradise? Turkish miniature painters had to try. This 2008 article by Bahattin Yaman looks at pictures of Jannah, the Islamic paradise, in Turkish miniatures. It points out that though the painter followed the text of the book being illustrated, he also added the picture in his own mind, so each image shows how people of the time imagined heaven.

title: Customer Experience at the Heart of the Moroccan Banking Revolution
summary: This article examines customer satisfaction with Moroccan banks, particularly in the context of the growing digitalization of banking services. Based on a qualitative survey, it identifies the key factors influencing customer satisfaction, including the performance of online services, the speed of request processing, and the quality of interactions with bank advisors. The findings show that banks offering seamless and secure digital services while maintaining high-quality in-branch customer support achieve higher levels of customer satisfaction, loyalty, and corporate image. Conversely, banks with limited online services, high perceived fees, and inadequate branch service generate greater cu
creator: Raja Temnati
source_name: Revue Marocaine de Droit, d'Economie et de Gestion (Moroccan Journal of Law, Economics and Management)
locator: DOI=10.66499/2665-7112.1624; journal="Revue Marocaine de Droit, d'Economie et de Gestion (Moroccan Journal of Law, Economics and Management)"
scope_basis: Crossref search "moroccan zellige"; publisher hosted in Morocco
story: What makes someone happy with their bank? This 2026 study by Raja Temnati looked at Moroccan banks as they go digital. Customers were happiest with banks that had smooth, secure online services and still gave good help in the branch. Banks with weak online services, high fees and poor branch service left people dissatisfied. Fast replies to requests mattered too.

title: Transformation of Artificial intelligence in Islamic Edu with Ulul Albab Value (Global Challenge Perespective)
summary: The face of world industrialization is changing with the Industrial Revolution 4.0. Old-style large companies are increasingly being threatened by new, more innovative companies. Likewise, in the innovation of the Islamic Education system, the need for new skills such as artificial intelligence, data analytics, machine learning, and other digital technologies is increasingly evident. Likewise soft skills related to complex problem solving, critical thinking, collaboration and communication are also increasingly needed. The existence of the face of the world's industrialization has created an impact that has caused panic and anxiety among the people. In the context of Islamic Education, Artif
source_name: Firdaus Journal
scope_basis: Crossref search "artificial intelligence islamic"; publisher hosted in Malaysia
story: Industry is changing fast, and new companies are overtaking old ones. This 2023 paper in the Firdaus Journal asks what that means for Islamic education. It argues students need digital skills like AI and data analysis, but also problem-solving, critical thinking and teamwork. It ties this to Ulul Albab, a Quranic phrase for "people of understanding", as a value to guide the change.

title: Mini-STRs screening of 12 relatives of Hausa Origin in northern Nigeria
summary: Research article in Nigerian Journal of Basic and Applied Sciences by U.U. Akpan, K.O. Adekoya, E.T. Awe, 2018.

story: Mini-STRs are short repeated stretches of DNA used to compare people and test family links. This 2018 Nigerian study screened 12 relatives of Hausa origin in northern Nigeria using them.

title: Barış Manço'da Ahilik Kültürünün İzleri

creator: Enis Yalçın

story: Ahilik, or Akhism, was a brotherhood of craftsmen and traders that grew in Anatolia from the 1200s and valued unity and solidarity. This 2019 study finds traces of Ahi culture in the songs of Barış Manço, the Turkish rock musician.

title: Specific accounting standards for Waqf institutions: The impact of its non-existence to Waqf accounting practices in Malaysia
summary: The purpose of accounting standard is to govern the accounting process and subsequently reporting for entities. Hence, the absence of a specific accounting standard to govern the accounting for an entity would be problematic and would give rise to several issues. This research aims to understand how the absence of a specific accounting standard affects the accounting practices of an entity. The findings show how the waqf corporation tries to adhere to the prevailing accounting standard, which is not specific for waqf institutions, and how important it is to have a specific accounting standard in place for waqf institutions.
source_name: Journal of Emerging Economies and Islamic Research
locator: DOI=10.24191/jeeir.v9i1.11305; journal="Journal of Emerging Economies and Islamic Research"
scope_basis: Crossref search "waqf innovation"; publisher hosted in Malaysia
story: Accounting standards tell organisations how to keep and report their books. Waqf institutions, which manage permanent charitable gifts, have no specific standard of their own. This 2021 Malaysian study asks what problems that gap causes for waqf accounting.

title: Manuskrip Melayu MSS255 Al-Durr al-Nafis : Suatu Kajian dan Analisis Teks Kitab Tasawuf Nusantara Malay Manuscript MSS255 Al-Durr al-Nafis: A Study and Text Analysis of the Sufi Book of the Malay Archipelago
summary: Abstract Kedatangan Islam ke Nusantara telah mewarnai kehidupan masyarakat di rantau ini khususnya dalam bidang pendidikan, bahasa, sastera dan tulisan. Senario tersebut telah melahirkan ramai cendekiawan dan ulama tempatan yang mempunyai kesedaran tinggi dalam aspek keintelektualan. Kebiasaan mereka mempunyai sumbangan dalam penyebaran agama Islam, penghasilan karya atau kitab dan pengajaran serta pendidikan. Artikel ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis salah sebuah teks manuskrip khazanah warisan Melayu dalam bidang tasawuf yang dikarang oleh ulama tempatan. Kaedah kajian merupakan kajian kualitatif dengan menggunakan kaedah dokumentasi iaitu dengan merujuk sumber primer teks manuskrip Melayu
creator: Noor Syahidah Mohamad Akhir (Corresponding Author), Syaimak Ismail, Azrul Shahimy Mohd Yusof
source_name: Journal of Al-Tamaddun
scope_basis: Crossref search "sufi literature manuscript"; publisher hosted in Malaysia
story: Islam's arrival in the Malay world shaped its schools, language, literature and writing, and produced local scholars who wrote their own books. This 2025 study looks at one of them: a handwritten Malay manuscript, MSS255, called Al-Durr al-Nafis, a work on Sufism, the inward, spiritual side of Islam. The researchers read the manuscript itself to analyse its text.

title: The Effectiveness of "Notebook" as an Auxiliary Educational Platform in Teaching Arabic Music History
summary: The current era is defined by a profound technological revolution, with Artificial Intelligence (AI) permeating sectors such as education, healthcare, and economics. AI has evolved into a daily assistant for organizations and individuals alike, with many institutions integrating AI capabilities into their digital platforms to facilitate rapid and highly accurate information retrieval. By leveraging "fed" data, smart assistants and chatbots provide immediate responses to specialized inquiries. In light of these advancements, this research proposes a method for utilizing Notebook (specifically AI-driven notebooks) as an auxiliary platform for teaching "Arabic Music History." The platform is de
creator: Ali Mamdouh Mohamed Ahmed
source_name: Jordan Journal of the Arts
locator: DOI=10.47016/19.1.7; journal="Jordan Journal of the Arts"
scope_basis: Crossref search "arabic music maqam"; publisher hosted in Jordan
story: Can an AI notebook help you learn the history of Arabic music? This 2026 study by Ali Mamdouh Mohamed Ahmed, from Jordan, tests the idea. It proposes feeding an AI-driven notebook with course material so students can ask it questions and get quick answers about Arabic music history, as a helper alongside normal teaching.

title: A recepção da classificação aristotélica das ciências por Ibn Sina (Avicena)
summary: Este artigo analisa a recepção da classificação aristotélica das ciências por Ibn Sina (980-1037). Trata-se de compreender a divisão e os critérios de classificação das ciências segundo Aristóteles e Ibn Sina (Avicena), a partir da exposição e análise dos textos fundamentais destes dois autores sobre o assunto.
creator: Andrei Pedro Vanin
source_name: Intuitio
scope_basis: Crossref search "ibn sina"; publisher hosted in Brazil
story: Aristotle sorted all knowledge into kinds of science. This 2022 Brazilian article looks at how Ibn Sina, known in Europe as Avicenna (980 to 1037), took up and reworked that classification.

story: Can social media decide what job you choose? This 2024 news report from Üsküdar University in Istanbul looks at how social media pressure shapes young people's career choices, with comments from Ertuğrul Tut.

title: Health Implications of Ramadan Fasting in Healthy and Eligible Individuals: A Narrative Review
summary: Research article in Journal of Research and Health by Esmaeel Shirvani, Pooran Asadi, Mahdi Vahdani, 2026.

story: Ramadan fasting is obligatory for healthy adult Muslims, with no eating or drinking from the pre-dawn meal, suhoor, to the sunset meal, iftar. This 2026 review looks at what fasting does to the health of healthy people who are able to fast.

title: Sustainability as cultural value in islamic private higher education

locator: DOI=10.34044/j.kjss.2023.44.1.14; journal="Kasetsart Journal of Social Sciences"

story: Can sustainability be a cultural value at a university? This 2023 study in the Kasetsart Journal of Social Sciences looks at sustainability as a value in Islamic private higher education.

source_name: Erdem

story: Anthologies collect the best writing of a time. In 2019, Adem Ceyhan wrote about a Turkish literature anthology printed in 1892 and 1893, called Enmuzec-i Edebiyyat-i Turkiyye.

title: Pillars of Knowledge Economy for Islamic Art
summary: Research article in TANMIYAT AL-RAFIDAIN by Dr. Ahmed  Mansoor, Dr. Mohammed  Mohamoud, 2013.

source_name: TANMIYAT AL-RAFIDAIN
scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic art brazil"; publisher hosted in Iraq
story: Islamic art could be part of a knowledge economy. This 2013 Iraqi study by Ahmed Mansoor and Mohammed Mohamoud, in the journal Tanmiyat al-Rafidain, looks at the pillars a knowledge economy for Islamic art would need.

title: Towards Understanding Islamic Architecture
summary: This article aims to discuss the meaning, functions and salient characteristics of Islamic architecture. The discussion will be divided into the following sections: (1) the meaning of Islamic architecture; (2) the object that Islamic architecture seeks to achieve; (3) the house and the mosque as examples of Islamic architecture; (4) pragmatism and Islamic architecture; (5) Islamic versus Muslim architecture; (6) the significance of Quṣayr 'Amrah as an example of early Muslim architecture. The article seeks to enhance the awareness, both of the professionals and general readership, as to the importance of correctly conceptualizing the theme of Islamic architecture, especially at the present w
creator: Spahic Omer
source_name: Islamic Studies
scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic architecture"; publisher hosted in Pakistan
story: What makes a building "Islamic"? This 2008 article by Spahic Omer explores what Islamic architecture means and what it tries to achieve, using the house and the mosque as examples. It also separates "Islamic" from "Muslim" architecture, and looks at Qusayr ʿAmra, an early building, as an example of early Muslim architecture.

title: Diagnostic Protocol of Warm and Cold Uterine Temperaments Based on Persian Medicine: A Qualitative Study
summary: Objective: Uterus is an important body organ in women responsible for purifying blood and carrying fetus. In Traditional Iranian Medicine (TIM), identifying the uterine temperament (mizaj) is necessary for prevention, diagnosis and treatment of this organ’s diseases. Many gynecological disorders in TIM including infertility, oligomenorrhea, amenorrhea, hypermenorrhea, vaginitis, cervicitis, urinary incontinence and pelvic pain are related to uterine distemperament (Su-e mizaj). Therefore, their appropriate treatment depends on the correct diagnosis and treatment of uterine distemperament. Criteria for uterine distemperament in TIM resources are qualitative with no method for precise measurem
creator: Atefeh Saeidi, Roshanak Mokaberinejad
source_name: Complementary Medicine Journal
scope_basis: Crossref search "traditional medicine muslim"; publisher hosted in Iran
story: Traditional Persian medicine says every organ has a temperament, warm or cold, wet or dry. This 2021 study by Atefeh Saeidi and Roshanak Mokaberinejad focuses on the uterus. Old texts link many women's health problems, including infertility, to an imbalanced uterine temperament, but describe it only in words. The study set out to build a clear protocol for diagnosing it.

title: Comparative Study of Architecture of the Great Mosque at Samarra, Iraq and Ibn Tulun Mosque at Cairo, Egypt
summary: Ever since the emergence of Islam, mosque has always been the most dominant feature in any Islamic built environment. Over the course of time, mosque architecture has gone through a process of various forms of uses and expressions in terms of its transformation. Its style, layout, building form, type of ornamentation used, building materials and construction technology usually provide vital information not only about the practice of Islam in general but also about the timeline, prevailing geopolitical environment, religious conviction, purpose, need and the region in which the mosque was built. This research paper emphasizes the study of the general characteristics of the two earliest exampl
creator: Zahid Tauqeer Ahmad, Seemin Aslam
source_name: Journal of Islamic Thought and Civilization
locator: DOI=10.32350/jitc.102.16; journal="Journal of Islamic Thought and Civilization"
scope_basis: Crossref search "mosque architecture"; publisher hosted in Pakistan
story: This paper treats two buildings as among the earliest examples of their kind: the Great Mosque of Samarra in Iraq and the Ibn Tulun Mosque in Cairo. This 2020 paper by Zahid Tauqeer Ahmad and Seemin Aslam compares them. A mosque's layout, ornament and building materials, it notes, can reveal the time, the politics, the beliefs and the region that produced it.

title: The Transformation of Islamic Education in Malabar: From Othupalli to Primary Madrasa
summary: Abstract This study investigates the transformation of primary Islamic education in Malabar, focusing on the evolution from the informal Othupalli system to the structured Primary Madrasa system during the twentieth century. This transformation was driven by socio-cultural shifts, political influences during colonial and postcolonial periods, and active community participation, which collectively ensured the preservation and modernization of Islamic education amid the rise of secular schooling. The continued use of Arabi-Malayalam highlights cultural adaptability in sustaining religious knowledge transmission. This study contributes a historically grounded, localized perspective to global sc
creator: Hassan Shareef KP (Author)
source_name: Journal of Islamic Education
scope_basis: Crossref search "madrasa senegal"; publisher hosted in Malaysia
story: In Malabar, on India's southwest coast, children once learned Islam in the othupalli, an informal reading school. In the twentieth century that turned into the organised primary madrasa. This 2025 study by Hassan Shareef KP traces the change through colonial and post-colonial times, and notes the lasting use of Arabi-Malayalam, the Malayalam language written in Arabic script.

title: Is Islamic Finance, Social Finance?
summary: Developments in Islamic Finance and Social Finance and illustrate an increasing interest globally to look at alternative ways of financing and creating value in the society. Islamic Finance and Social Finance are emerging disciplines that challenge and influence the global finance industry and both have similar mandates in terms of their emphasis in ethical business and investment. Islamic Finance is governed by the rules of the shariah that prohibits riba or interest and gharar (uncertainty), sinful business sectors such as pornography and alcohol and unethical practices such as exessive speculation and gambling. These forms of restrictions are similar to the negative screening methodology
creator: Saadiah Mohamad
source_name: Journal of Emerging Economies and Islamic Research
locator: DOI=10.24191/jeeir.v2i2.6368; journal="Journal of Emerging Economies and Islamic Research"
scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic finance"; publisher hosted in Malaysia
story: Islamic finance bans riba, or interest, bans too much uncertainty and gambling, and avoids businesses like alcohol. Social finance is a newer movement that also screens out harmful investments. This 2014 paper by Saadiah Mohamad asks whether the two are really the same thing, since both put ethics at the centre of money.

title: Overview of Macro Nutrient Intake and Nutritional Status of Students at the Putri Hidayatullah Islamic Boarding School, Ternate City
summary: Adolescents are one of the nutritionally vulnerable groups. At this time, adolescents enter the second phase of rapid growth and then physical growth declines as young adults enter. Problems that arise in adolescents are undernutrition and overnutrition. One that is related to nutritional status is nutrient intake which is very influential on a person's nutritional status. Nutrient intake is influenced by eating habits and eating patterns of adolescents themselves. The purpose of this study was to determine the description of macronutrient intake and nutritional status at the Putri Hidayatullah Islamic Boarding School, Ternate City. The type of research used is descriptive research. The samp
creator: Hisdawati Abubakar, Yohannes Willi Helm, Nofiandri
source_name: International Journal of Scientific Research and Management
locator: DOI=10.18535/ijsrm/v9i12.nd3; journal="International Journal of Scientific Research and Management"
scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic boarding school"; publisher hosted in India
story: Teenagers are growing fast, so what they eat matters a lot. This 2021 study looked at girls at the Putri Hidayatullah Islamic boarding school in Ternate City, Indonesia. Researchers Hisdawati Abubakar, Yohannes Willi Helm and Nofiandri measured how much carbohydrate, protein and fat they took in, and checked their nutritional status, looking for signs of under- or over-nutrition.

title: The Functional of Water in Islamic Architecture with Emphasise of Sadra-ied Wisdom
