locator: DOI=10.61186/jria.11.4.4; journal="Journal of Researches in Islamic Architecture"
scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic architecture"; publisher hosted in Iran
story: Water does more than cool a building. This 2023 Iranian article by Mozhgan Rezaei, Azita Balali Oskuei and Mohammad Ali Keynejad looks at the role of water in Islamic architecture through the philosophy of Mulla Sadra. Its record gives only the title and authors.

title: U.S. Military Withdrawal from Afghanistan: War and Peace Journalism in Pakistani Media
summary: When it comes to reporting on war and conflict, according to Galtung (1986, 1998), there are two conflicting frames, war journalism and peace journalism. War journalists cover conflict by reporting it in a way that promotes violence, dominance, and an elitist viewpoint. Peace journalists, on the other hand, report proactively on the reasons and solutions to conflicts, providing all sides with a voice via responsible Media. The present study analyzes how Dawn and the Nation depict U.S. Military Withdrawal from Afghanistan. This study focuses on the war and peace inclination of the Pakistani print media. The war and peace journalism model proposed by Johan Galtung is used to guide this researc
creator: Ruqiya Anwar
source_name: Journal of Media & Communication
scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic media journalism"; publisher hosted in Pakistan
story: When the US pulled its troops out of Afghanistan, how did Pakistan's newspapers tell the story? This 2022 study by Ruqiya Anwar used an idea from Johan Galtung: war journalism focuses on violence and the powerful, while peace journalism looks for causes and solutions and gives every side a voice. It checked which way two papers, Dawn and The Nation, leaned.

title: Türk sinemasında çağdaş auteurler kapsamında bir Türk Yönetmen olarak Şerif Gören ve sineması üzerine bir inceleme
summary: 1960 yıllarında ortaya çıkan sosyolojik ve politik gelişmeler, Toplumsal Gerçekçilik Akımının ortaya çıkmasını ve yükselişe geçmesini sağlamıştır. Siyasetin günlük hayata ve popüler kültüre kadar yayılması, sinema endüstrisinde siyasal filmlerin oluşmasına zemin hazırlamıştır. Türk Sineması’nda Auteur Kuramından etkilenen ve Toplumsal Gerçekçilik Akımı kapsamında filmler çeken Yönetmen Şerif Gören, popüler kültürün ve halkın talepleri doğrultusunda, artık arabesk içerikli filmler çekmeye başlamıştır. Bu bağlamda Gören, sinema endüstrisi ve halkın isteğine bağlı olarak toplumsal yapıyı ve politik unsurları barındıran arabesk içerikli filmler çekerken, bu filmlerinde hem toplumsal sorunlara he
creator: Selda Çalayır
source_name: Journal of Arts
scope_basis: Crossref search "türk sineması"; publisher hosted in Türkiye
story: Şerif Gören was a Turkish film director who made political films in the social realist style. Later, following what audiences wanted, he moved into arabesk films. This 2022 study by Selda Çalayır argues that even then, he kept putting social problems and politics into his work, which is why it treats him as an auteur, a director with his own voice.

title: Re-identification of Falak-ol-Aflak Castle Based on Archaeological Excavations and Architectural Features
summary: Research article in Athar by Ali Sajadi, 2026.

story: Falak-ol-Aflak is a castle in Iran. In this 2026 article in Athar, Ali Sajadi re-identifies the castle using archaeological excavations and its architectural features, so digging is changing what we know about it.

story: Fasting in Ramadan means not eating from dawn to sunset, which raises questions for people with diabetes. Khwaja Nazim Uddin wrote about diabetes and Ramadan fasting in the Journal of Medicine in 2024.

title: Western and Arabic Islamic Architecture Discourse
summary: Many literatures concentrated on the issue of architecture discourse which identified by thespace of conceptual thought that has essential characteristics based on knowledge foundations anddistinctive historical, cultural, religious, and social dimensions. These literatures pointed to westemarchitecture discourse elements and Arabic Islamic architecture discourse and cultural,environmental and doctrinal reference, But these literatures didn''t present clear comparative picturefor those discourses.

title: Research Paper Evaluation of the restoration and technology of tile decorations of Safavid domes in Isfahan from the beginning to the present (Case study: Dome of the Abbasi Grand Mosque, Sheikh Lotfollah Mosque, Chaharbagh School)

story: The mosaic tiles on the Safavid domes of Isfahan have lasted thanks to craftsmen, architects and artists working together. This 2025 study looks at how the tiles were made and restored over time on three domes: the Abbasi Grand Mosque, the Sheikh Lotfollah Mosque and the Chaharbagh School.

title: Reclaiming Islamic Ethical and Epistemic Traditions: Online Calligraphy Education through the Deen Arts Foundation in South Africa
summary: This article examines how online Islamic calligraphy education, as offered by the Deen Arts Foundation South Africa (DAFSA), functions as a pluriversal and ethically grounded practice of epistemic recovery and self-formation in post-apartheid South Africa. It argues that by integrating Islamic pedagogical traditions, centred on adab, ikhlāṣ, and iḥsān, with contemporary digital platforms, DAFSA enables students to reconnect with their Islamic heritage, recover marginalised knowledge traditions, and cultivate moral and spiritual dispositions. Conceptually, the article draws on the notion of field, is guided by a normative ethics of beauty and excellence and applies the Community of Inquiry fr
creator: Aslam Fataar, Widad Sirkhotte
source_name: Journal for Islamic Studies
scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic calligraphy art"; publisher hosted in South Africa
story: Can you learn calligraphy online and grow as a person at the same time? This 2025 article by Aslam Fataar and Widad Sirkhotte studies the Deen Arts Foundation in South Africa, which teaches Islamic calligraphy over the internet. It argues that the lessons, built on values like adab (good manners), ikhlas (sincerity) and ihsan (excellence), help students reconnect with a heritage pushed aside in the past.

title: XIII-XVII. Yüzyıllarda Deşt-i Kıpçak Türkleri Hac Yolunda
summary: XIII-XVI. yüzyıllarda Avrasya göçebeleri arasında İslam dini hızlı bir şekilde yayılmaya başlamıştır. Bilindiği gibi, İslamiyet'in beş şartından biri de Hac'dır'. Ancak Ortaçağ'da ve özellikle de uzak bölgelerden Hacc'a gidenler büyük sorunlarla karşılaşıyorlardı. Uzun mesafe ve yolculuk sırasındaki zorluklar, Deşt-i Kıpçak Müslümanları için de bir sorun teşkil ediyordu. XIII-XV. yüzyıllarda Hacıların Mekke'ye gelişleri ve aynı zamanda da Mısır ve Suriye'ye uğradıklarına dair bilgiler mevcuttur. Dönemin şartları ve bölgedeki düzen, Hacıların Hac yapabilmeleri için söz konusu Arap topraklarına hakim olan yüksek hükümdardan izin almalarını gerektiriyordu. O dönemde bu izin Memlük sultanlarında
creator: V. V. Trepavlov
source_name: Belleten
scope_basis: Crossref search "hac yolculuğu"; publisher hosted in Türkiye
story: Imagine walking from the steppes north of the Black Sea all the way to Mecca. Between the 1200s and 1500s, Islam spread fast among the nomads of the Dasht-i Kipchak, and some set off on Hajj. This 2009 study by V. V. Trepavlov shows how hard it was: the road was long, and pilgrims needed permission from the Mamluk sultans, who ruled the Arab lands on the way.

title: Mosque Decoration between Acceptance and Rejection
summary: This paper discusses the subject of mosque decoration and some of the measures which determine its acceptability or otherwise. Indeed, the matter is a sensitive and double-edged one. Thus, the paper presents an objective, balanced and scientific account of the theme, steering clear of the sentimental aspects of the evidences often put forth by both the proponents and opponents of mosque decoration. The paper is divided into the following sections: 1) The legitimacy of decoration, 2) The function of mosques vis-a-vis their decoration, 3) Broad guidelines that regulate mosque decoration, 4) Decorating the mihrab and the qiblah wall in mosques.
creator: Spahic Omer
source_name: Islamic Studies
scope_basis: Crossref search "eco-mosque"; publisher hosted in Pakistan
story: Should mosques be decorated at all? This 2015 paper by Spahic Omer looks at both sides calmly: whether decoration is allowed, what mosques are for, broad guidelines, and the special case of the mihrab and qibla wall.

title: Nollywood and the leaders of tomorrow: interrogating film content and character formation of the Nigerian child
summary: The intellectual discourse on the influence of films in shaping a child’s ideological leaning is a topic that has generated interest in different parts of the world. The supposed proposition that inapt behaviours, nonchalant attitudes, moral decadence, and violence among children are outcome in most films produced in Nollywood Film Industry calls for serious examination. Hence, to examine the effects which film contents could have on educational development and character formation of a Nigerian child remains the aim of this study. Objectives include; to ascertain the potentials of films content in creating a standard for good leadership skills for the Nigerian child, and to advocate possible
creator: Nkemakonam Aniukwu
source_name: UJAH: Unizik Journal of Arts and Humanities
locator: DOI=10.4314/ujah.v20i3.4; journal="UJAH: Unizik Journal of Arts and Humanities"
scope_basis: Crossref search "nigerian film hausa"; publisher hosted in Africa (multi-country)
story: Nollywood, Nigeria's film industry, is often blamed for teaching children bad habits. This 2020 study by Nkemakonam Aniukwu takes that claim seriously and looks at how film content shapes a Nigerian child's education and character. It also asks the opposite question: can films show children what good leadership looks like?

title: INTRODUCING FA TUNING TO MALAYSIA (2005): THE FIRST DOCUMENTED ADOPTION IN HIGHER-EDUCATION OUD/GAMBUS PEDAGOGY
summary: This practice-based article documents the first documented adoption of Fa tuning in Malaysian higher-education oud/gambus pedagogy in 2005, introduced by the author at ASWARA following a period of study at Beit al-Oud (Cairo). Prior to 2005, local Malaysian practice commonly employed a B–E–A–D–G–C course layout (low→high). The author implemented F–C–D–G–C–F (low→high) on a Yaroub Fadel “Bashir”-style Iraqi oud, strung with Pyramid Laute strings, without requiring organological modification. The tuning was selected for its tonal palette, register balance, and pedagogical advantages in taqsīm training and modal navigation, particularly in Maqām Nahawand and Maqām Rast. Using contemporaneous do
creator: Raja Zulkarnain Raja Yusof
source_name: Journal of Creative Arts
scope_basis: Crossref search "gambus qasidah music"; publisher hosted in Malaysia
story: Before 2005, oud players in Malaysia usually tuned their strings one way. That year, Raja Zulkarnain Raja Yusof, back from studying at Beit al-Oud in Cairo, brought a different system, "Fa tuning", into teaching at ASWARA. He played it on an Iraqi-style oud without changing the instrument. In this 2026 article he documents it as the first recorded use of the tuning in Malaysian university oud teaching, chosen for its sound and for training in the maqam modes.

title: Mehmed Şakir'in Manzum Mesnevi Tercümesi
summary: Mevlana Celaleddin-i Rumî (ö: 672/1273)'nin Mesnevi'si, yazıldığı günden bu güne kadar manzum ve mensur olarak birçok dile tercüme edilen ve üzerine şerhler yazılan bir eserdir. Seyyid Mehmed Şakir (ö. 1252/1836)'in "Tercemânu'l-Ma'nevî fî-Tercemeti'l-Mesnevî" adlı eseri de, Mesnevi'nin manzum tercümelerinden birisidir. Eser, Mesnevi'nin tamamını içeren bir tercüme olması bakımından önem taşımaktadır. Bu yazıda, tam bir nüshası İstanbul Üniversitesi Kütüphanesi'nde bulunan bu eserin Ankara Üniversitesi Dil ve Tarih-Coğrafya Fakültesi Kütüphanesi'nde bulunan gözlerden uzak kalmış ve mütercim Mehmed Şakir'in kendi hattıyla bir nüshası tanıtılmakta, ayrıca mütercimin kimliği açıklığa kavuşturul
creator: Bilal ÇAKICI
source_name: Erdem
scope_basis: Crossref search "mesnevi"; publisher hosted in Türkiye
story: Rumi's Masnavi, written in the 1200s, has been translated many times. In the 1800s, Seyyid Mehmed Şakir, who died in 1836, translated the whole thing into Turkish verse. A complete copy sits in Istanbul University Library. This 2008 article by Bilal Çakıcı introduces another copy, overlooked in an Ankara library, written in the translator's own handwriting, and helps pin down who he was.

title: The Impact of Shariah Governance and Corporate Governance on the Risk Management Practices: Evidence from Local and Foreign Islamic Banks in Malaysia
summary: The purpose of this study is to examine the impact of Shariah governance and corporate governance (CG) on the risk management practices (RMPs) of local Islamic banks and foreign Islamic banks operating in Malaysia. The Shariah governance comprises the Shariah review (SR) and Shariah audit (SA) variables. The study also evaluates the level of RMPs, CG, SR, and SA between these two type of banks. With the aid of SPSS version 20, the items for RMPs, CG, SR, and SA were subjected to principal component analysis (PCA). The study also examines prominent figures such as Ibn Arabi, al-Hallaj, and Ibn al-Farid in Islamic mysticism, alongside Wordsworth, Blake, and John Keats in Christian mystical thought. At the same time, Hafez's fame crossed the borders; the fame of his poetry reached to Bengal. Many notables of the subcontinent were among the fans of Hafez's poetry, wrote poetry in his style, or wrote commentaries on his poetry. The large number of manuscripts of Divan Hafez, as well as numerous Persian and non-Persian commentaries available in libraries across the subcontinent, are p
creator: Khadije Hajiya, Md. Mumit Al Rashid
source_name: Dhaka University Journal of Persian

story: Hafez lived in Shiraz, in Iran, but his poetry travelled far beyond it, all the way to Bengal. This 2022 study from Dhaka shows how deeply Persian poets shaped writing in the Indian subcontinent. It compares two works about Hafez written there, Marj al-Bahrin and Badr al-Sharuh, to see how readers far from Iran understood him.

These women were divided in two groups fasting (n=100), and non-fasting (n=80).Results: The mean age of the mothers was 27.16

This 2018 study from Pakistan by Zahegul Gul, Seema Rajar and Zeenat Shaikh compared 180 women who came to give birth, 100 who had fasted and 80 who had not, to see whether their babies' outcomes differed. The mothers' average age was about 27.

title: Analisis Ketepatan Aplikasi Kiblat dalam Play Store dan Apple App Store Analysis of Qibla App Accuracy in the Play Store and Apple App Store
summary: In today’s era of modern technology, qibla applications, whether in the Play Store or Apple App Store (iOS), have become the preferred choice of the Muslim community. Qibla applications are favoured because they are easy to use in determining the direction of the Qibla. The community’s reliance on Qibla applications is evident in the millions of downloads every day. This trend shows that qibla applications are the main choice of the Muslim community in the 21st century. However, issues arise not only from magnetic interference, but also from the fact that hundreds of applications available on both Android and iOS systems have not all been tested for accuracy. Therefore, this study was conduc
creator: Nurulhuda Ahmad Zaki, Damia Batrisya Hidayatullah
source_name: Jurnal Fiqh
scope_basis: Crossref search "qibla determination"; publisher hosted in Malaysia
story: Millions of people download qibla apps that point toward Mecca for prayer. But do they point the right way? This 2025 Malaysian study, published in a journal of Islamic law, tests how accurate the qibla apps on the Google Play Store and the Apple App Store actually are. Its starting point is simple: the more people rely on a tool, the more its accuracy matters.

title: Romantic Disillusionment and Environmental Catastrophe in Nigerian Petrocinema Film - Blood Vessel
summary: Cinema, particularly petrocinema, has explored the socio-political and environmental consequences of oil extraction globally. The representation of oil and its socio-political impacts have not been sufficiently analysed, particularly within Nigerian cinema. The problem lies in the lack of critical analysis of how Nigerian films anthropomorphically depict petro-narratives, reflecting corporate influence and exposing the environmental and social injustices tied to oil exploitation. The study aims to investigate how Nigerian petrocinema functions as both a medium that conceals and challenges hegemonic power structures linked to oil extraction, with a particular focus on the intersection of oil,
creator: Abdulhamid Badru, Jamaluddin Aziz
source_name: Jurnal Komunikasi: Malaysian Journal of Communication
locator: DOI=10.17576/jkmjc-2024-4004-20; journal="Jurnal Komunikasi: Malaysian Journal of Communication"
scope_basis: Crossref search "nigerian film hausa"; publisher hosted in Malaysia
story: "Petrocinema" means films about oil, and what drilling does to land and people. This 2024 paper studies Blood Vessel, a Nigerian film. It argues that Nigerian films about oil have been studied too little, and it reads this one as a story of romantic disappointment mixed with environmental disaster, showing the damage oil companies leave behind.

title: İznik Çini Fırınları Kazısı Çini Buluntuları Arasından İstanbul’da 17. Yüzyıl Mimarisinde Karşılaşılan Çinilere Ait Bazı Örnekler

İznik’te, Osmanlı Dönemi’nde çini ve seramik atölyelerinin yoğun olduğu bölge içerisinde kalan kazı alanında, şimdiye kadar toplam on bir fırın ateşhanesi tespit edilmiştir. Yaklaşık -4 metre kotuna kadar inilen kazı çalışmalarında ortaya çıkarılan fırın artıkları, fırın içerisinde pişirim sırasında kullanılan çeşitli pişmiş toprak malzemeler ile yanmış ya da defolu parçaların olduğu seramik çöplükleri her yıl ayrıştırılarak buradaki üretimin yoğunluğu ve niteliği konusunda yeni verilere ulaşılmasını sağlamaktadır. Üretim artığı olarak
creator: V. Belgin Demirsar Arlı, Hakan Arlı, Şennur Kaya

story: Under the town of İznik in Turkey lie the kilns where famous Ottoman tiles were fired. Digging started in 1981, and archaeologists have found eleven kiln fireboxes so far, working down to about four metres. This 2025 paper picks out tile fragments from the dig that match tiles on 17th-century buildings in Istanbul, linking broken pieces in the ground to walls you can still visit.

title: Abu Rayhan al-Biruni as an Indologist: Views and Reviews
summary: The great writer, astronomer, scientist and Indologist, Abu Rayhan Al-Biruni’s writings, researches, innovations and perceptions has been known for the whole academic world for over a thousand years, but the greatest and most interesting aspect of his works is his incisive and deep perception about the cultural, geographical, philosophical and social contours of Indian sub-continent especially Brahminical traditions.The proposed paper critically analyzes Abu Rayhan Al-Biruni’s legacy and contribution to the development of Indology. It is should be noted that Al-Biruni mostly wrote about the Brahminical tradition in India as the region’s dominant religious tradition, whereas Buddhism is almos
creator: Ahmad А
source_name: Meros

story: About a thousand years ago, al-Biruni, a scientist and astronomer, set out to understand India, a culture very different from his own. This 2019 paper from Uzbekistan treats him as an Indologist, someone who studies India. It argues the most interesting part of his work is his sharp reading of India's geography, philosophy and society, especially its Brahmin traditions.

title: Ramadan Fasting: Effect on Anxiety Using The DASS-42 Scoring System
summary: Introduction: Ramadan fasting affects dietary propensity and mental health. As part of their courses, medical students encounter stressors such as examinations, college assignments, and others that can impact their mental health and contribute to conditions such as anxiety. Limited research has been conducted to date on the impact of Ramadan fasting on anxiety scores among college students. This study aimed to explore the impact of Ramadan fasting on anxiety using DASS-42 scoring system. Methods: A prospective cohort analytic study was conducted with a cross-sectional approach and a one-group pretest-posttest design. A total of 242 medical students were sampled and selected by consecutive sa
creator: Sayid Ridho, Annisa Futihandayani
source_name: Malaysian Journal of Medicine and Health Sciences
locator: DOI=10.47836/mjmhs.20.1.24; journal="Malaysian Journal of Medicine and Health Sciences"
scope_basis: Crossref search "ramadan fasting health"; publisher hosted in Malaysia
story: Medical students already face exams and deadlines that can feed anxiety. So what happens when they also fast through Ramadan? This 2024 study points out that little research had looked at this among college students. It measures their anxiety with a standard test called the DASS-42 to see how a month of fasting affects it.

title: Apontamentos sobre a solução do problema do xadrez proposta por al-Biruni na obra A Cronologia das Nações Antigas
summary: O desenvolvimento das ciências e da matemática aconteceu em diversas regiões do mundo. Dessa forma, muitos estudiosos deixaram contribuições para esses campos do conhecimento. Entretanto, não é tão fácil encontrar bibliografias, em língua portuguesa, que os retratem. A exemplo desse contexto, citamos os estudiosos islâmicos da era medieval e em particular Abu Arrayhan Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Biruni (973 – 1048), que deixou estudos em diversas áreas do conhecimento, incluindo a que conhecemos hoje por matemática. creator: Maria Luíza dos Santos

scope_basis: Crossref search "al-biruni"; publisher hosted in Brazil
story: Al-Biruni (973 to 1048) left studies in many fields, and in his book The Chronology of Ancient Nations he took on a mathematical problem about the chessboard. This 2024 Brazilian paper works through his solution. Part of the point is to bring medieval Muslim scholars to Portuguese readers, who rarely find books about them in their own language.

title: Custody in Islamic Law: A Law Based on Presumptions
summary: Custody is a right of the child from its birth. Islamic law issues rules for custody in the light of the interest of the minor. In Islamic law custody goes to the mother unless she is disqualified and then to other relatives. This paper discusses and analyses the rules of child custody in Islamic law and argues that most of these rules are not divine. These are a product of ijtihad. A large extent of these rules is actually presumptions which may be rebutted in a given situation.
creator: Mudasra Sabreen
source_name: Islamic Studies
scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic law constitution"; publisher hosted in Pakistan
story: In Islamic law, custody is a right of the child from birth, and the rules are made in the child's interest. Custody goes to the mother unless she is disqualified, and then to other relatives. This 2017 paper argues the law rests on presumptions about what is best for the child.

Its record gives only the title and authors, so this is an outline.

title: Article 230 of the Moroccan Law of Obligations and Contracts
summary: Zaid Kadri Al Tarjuman examines Article 230 of the Moroccan Law of Obligations and Contracts, which states that contractually created obligations validly formed stand as law for those who created them and cannot be revoked except by mutual consent or in cases provided by law. This article establishes the principle of the authority of the will (principe de l'autonomie de la volonté), resting on two rules: the contract is the law of the parties, and a contract cannot be revoked without mutual consent or legal exception. However, the author notes that exceptions exist to this principle, some found within the DOC and others not mentioned due to the law's age (1913), including necessary exception
creator: Zaid Kadri Al Tarjuman
source_name: Revue Marocaine de Droit, d'Economie et de Gestion (Moroccan Journal of Law, Economics and Management)
locator: DOI=10.66499/2665-7112.1424; journal="Revue Marocaine de Droit, d'Economie et de Gestion (Moroccan Journal of Law, Economics and Management)"
scope_basis: Crossref search "moroccan zellige"; publisher hosted in Morocco
story: Article 230 of Morocco's law on contracts says something powerful: a contract that is properly made works as law for the people who made it, and it can only be undone if both sides agree or the law allows it. This 2026 paper unpacks the idea behind that rule, the authority of the will, which means your own free agreement binds you like a law.

title: Prinsip pembelajaran mentalis dalam pengajaran dan pembelajaran teks Kesusasteraan Melayu Sekolah Menengah
summary: Kajian ini bertujuan untuk meneliti peranan prinsip pembelajaran mentalis dalam pengajaran dan pembelajaran teks Kesusasteraan Melayu sekolah menengah. Kajian dijalankan secara kualititatif di tiga buah sekolah menengah di sekitar Kuching, Sarawak, melibatkan kaedah soal selidik. Data dianalisis menggunakan perisian kualititatif skala likert dan juga Cohen’s Kappa. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahawa prinsip pembelajaran mentalis ini memberi kesan dalam pengajaran dan pembelajaran guru yang mengajar Kesusasteraan Melayu malah dapat mempengaruhi karakter pelajar agar berfikir secara kritis. Dapatan kajian mendapati bahawa pelajar Kesusasteraan Melayu dapat memahami perkara yang dipelajari oleh me
creator: Cynthia Layah Geraman, Azhar Wahid
source_name: Jurnal Peradaban Melayu
scope_basis: Crossref search "kesusasteraan melayu"; publisher hosted in Malaysia
story: How do you get teenagers to actually think about a novel? This 2019 study visited three secondary schools around Kuching in Sarawak, Malaysia, to look at a "mentalist" approach to teaching Malay literature, one focused on what goes on in students' minds. It reports that the approach did have an effect on how the literature was taught and learned.

title: The Islamic Musical Sciences and the Andalusian Connection: Juan Andrés’ «Letter on Arabic Music» (1785)
summary: Music was an essential part of the philosophical knowledge in the classical antiquity and then in the medieval era. Music provided tools to foster a global speculative knowledge, and the classical Islamic thought developed different musical sciences. This paper tries to describe the different approaches to the musical phenomenon from an Islamic perspective, and the feasible transmission of this knowledge to Western music via al-Andalus. In doing so, the paper places attention in the Italian «Letter on Arabic Music» written by the Spanish Jesuit Juan Andrés in 1785, one of the first documents attesting this connection.
creator: Isaac Donoso Donoso
source_name: Journal of Usuluddin
scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic music"; publisher hosted in Malaysia
story: In 1785 a Spanish Jesuit named Juan Andrés wrote a letter in Italian on Arabic music. It is one of the first documents to show that Islamic musical science may have passed to Western music through al-Andalus, Muslim Spain. This 2021 paper explores how classical Islamic thought treated music as a science.

title: The ecological background of education in Turkish cinema
summary: Educational films, beginning with Çalıkuşu in the 1960s, have increasingly expanded their presence in Turkish cinema. These films not only reflect societal perceptions of education but also provide a condensed overview of the history of Turkish education. Thus, education in Turkish cinema has emerged as a significant cultural phenomenon. This study examined the most critically acclaimed Turkish film with an educational theme from each decade since the 1960s, as determined by Internet Movie Database (IMDb) scores (Çalıkuşu, The Chaos Class, A Season in Hakkari, Bullshit, On the Way to School, and Brother’s Keeper). Phenomenology was used as the research design to examine how education is repr
creator: Talha Göktentürk, Sevgen Özbaşı, Mehmet Hilmi Sağlam
source_name: Education and Science
scope_basis: Crossref search "turkish cinema"; publisher hosted in Türkiye
story: Turkish cinema has been making films about school since Çalıkuşu in the 1960s. This 2026 study argues those films do more than tell stories. Together they give a compressed history of Turkish education. The researchers picked the most critically praised school film from each decade and looked at what each one shows about the world around education.

title: The role of inflammatory markers following Ramadan Fasting
summary: Objectives: The aim of present study was to investigate the effect of fasting during Ramadan on plasma adiponectin and TNF-α levels. Methods: This is a cross sectional study, conducted at Federal Urdu University of Arts, Science & Technology (FUUAST), Karachi, comprising a total of 55 (50%) females and 55 (50%) males whose ages ranged between 20 and 40 years, and fasted during Ramadan (June-July 2014) were enrolled in the study. Subjects were separated into normal weight, overweight and obese males and females. Anthropometric measurements and Fasting venous blood samples were taken at first and last (29th) day of Ramadan. Plasma adiponectin and TNF-alpha levels were assayed with ELISA kits.
creator: Rubina Mushtaq, Ambreen Akram, Rehana Mushtaq
source_name: Pakistan Journal of Medical Sciences
locator: DOI=10.12669/pjms.35.1.95; journal="Pakistan Journal of Medical Sciences"
scope_basis: Crossref search "ramadan fasting health"; publisher hosted in Pakistan
story: Does a month of fasting change what is going on in your blood? Researchers in Karachi studied 110 people aged 20 to 40, half women and half men, who fasted in Ramadan in June and July 2014. They measured two blood signals connected with inflammation, adiponectin and TNF-α, to see how fasting changed them.

title: The personal is collective: Egyptian first-person – Documentary cinema as post-revolution diary
summary: The 2011 Egyptian revolution marked a watershed moment in the reconfiguration of individuality, autonomy and self-expression within Egyptian society. Challenging long-standing collectivist frameworks, the revolutionary moment opened new spaces for individual agency and subjective reflection. This paper examines how these shifts intersect with the rise of first-person documentary cinema as a powerful medium for articulating post-revolutionary subjectivity in Egypt. Focusing on The Past Will Return (2015) by Dina Hamza, Happily Ever After (2016) by Nada Riyadh and Ayman El Amir, and Little Eagles (2016) by Mohamed Rashad, the paper analyzes how filmmakers negotiate personal desires, familial p
creator: Eman Elharmeel
source_name: Regards
scope_basis: Crossref search "egyptian cinema"; publisher hosted in Lebanon
story: The 2011 Egyptian revolution changed how people thought about themselves as individuals. This 2026 paper links that shift to a rise in first-person documentaries, films where the director turns the camera on their own life. It reads them as diaries of life after the revolution, where a personal story also becomes a shared one.

summary: يهدف هذا البحث إلى بيان محاولات العلماء النيجيريين في حقل السرديات العربية في نيجيريا، حيث أكد البحث على أن هذا الفن المبدع حديث العهد في الأدب العربي النيجيري، تأخر ظهوره في نيجيريا لأسباب ثقافية ودينية وأدبية، ومن ثم اهتدى الأدباء المعاصرون إلى كتابة السرديات فبذلوا قصارى جهدهم في إصدار السرديات بحيث أصبحت القضايا السياسية والاجتماعية والعلمية والدينية موضوعات هذه السرديات؛ فظهرت الروايات، والقصص، والمسرحيات، وأدب الرحلات، والسيرة الذاتية، والترجمة من وإلى اللغة العربية

summary: The present status of Nigeria, since the fourth republic in 1999 under the democratic government, had become the talk of its citizens who are the victims of all irregularities therein, but such complaints could not be boldly said or addressed due to limited freedom of speech in the country. On this note, many poets like other artistes, remain silent to avoid getting apprehended, while others remain to be over-reacting not to care about the consequence. Arabic scholars are also in the terrain of addressing the national issues arising, especially those that need urgent corrections for the benefits of the citizenry. They used their creativity to fulfill their aspirations, in addition to their s

story: When speaking freely is risky, poets find other ways to talk. This 2023 study looks at a poem in Arabic by the Nigerian poet ʿIsa Alabi Abu Bakr, written about Nigeria's troubles since democracy returned in 1999. It examines how the poem uses symbols and unusual language to say what many people felt but could not safely say out loud.

title: Spirituality in Persian Poetry of the Seljuk Era
summary: The Seljuk period is (1040-1157 A.D) called the golden age of the development of Persian literature in Iran, because so many Persian poets emerged during this era that Persian literature acheved great development as a result of their writings. Those who wrote poetry especially on spiritual subjects are: Baba Taher Uryani, Abusayid Abul Khayer, Abdullah Ansari, Hakim omar Khayyam, Hakim Sanayi, Rasid Uddin, Adib Saber, Nizami Ganjubi etc. If we analayze their Persian poems, it can be seen that most of them were poets of Sufi idology. story: The Seljuk era, roughly 1040 to 1157, is called a golden age of Persian literature, because so many poets appeared at once. This 2025 paper from Bangladesh looks at the ones who wrote about the spiritual life, among them Baba Taher, Abu Saʿid Abu'l-Khayr, Abdullah Ansari, Omar Khayyam, Sanaʾi and Nizami.

title: An Analysis of Climate-Induced Displacement in Somalia through the Lens of Islamic Integral Ecology
summary: Somalia represents a critical convergence of ecological vulnerability, forced migration, and human insecurity. Recurring droughts and floods, combined with resource depletion, have displaced millions of people, exacerbated humanitarian conditions, and tested the precarious stability of government structures. This paper explores Islamic ecological ethics in relation to integral ecology as articulated in Laudato Si’. This study investigates how this framework illuminates the causes of climate-induced displacement in Somalia and offers pathways for response. Through the concepts of khalīfah (stewardship), amānah (trust), and mīzān (balance), the analysis draws on secondary academic literature.
creator: Fatuma Sarah
source_name: Hekima Review
scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic ecology"; publisher hosted in Kenya
story: In Somalia, repeated droughts and floods have pushed millions of people from their homes. This 2026 paper asks what faith can say about that. It puts Islamic ideas about caring for the earth alongside "integral ecology" from Laudato Si', a Catholic document by Pope Francis, to think about climate and the people it displaces.

title: Alaca Hisar Sancağına Ait 1536 Tarihli Bir Vakıf Defteri
summary: Osmanlı İmparatorluğu'nda ve bütün İslam dünyasında, dini ve insani yardım amacıyla tesis edilen en önemli kurum vakıflardı. Vakıflar genellikle dini kurumların, camilerin, mescidlerin, mekteblerin, medreselerin, tekke­lerin ve buna benzer binaların yapılması demektir. Balkanlarda bu konuyla ilgili çok yazı yazılmıştır. Yazımızda incelediğimiz ve transkripsyon ve tıpkı­basım şekilde verdiğimiz 1536 tarihli Alaca Hisar Sancağı Tahrir Defterine ait vakıf defterinde ihtiva edilen Alaca Hisar'da (bugünkü Kruşevaç) ve Leskovçe'de bulunan vakıflar hakkında da araştırma yapılmıştır. story: Waqfs, lasting gifts set up for religious and charitable use, were among the most important institutions in the Ottoman world. They paid for mosques, schools and lodges. This 2012 paper publishes a waqf register from 1536 for the district of Alaca Hisar in the Balkans, both copied out and as a facsimile, so readers can see the original record of who gave what.

title: Biography in Classical Arabic Poetry: Publicity, Immortalisation and Mythicisation
summary: The study investigates Arabic praise and lament poetry from the perspective of biographies that chronicle the life of the praised and the lamented. It assumes that the poet produces a three-dimensional biography that is axed on publicity, immortalization and mythicisation. The data under investigation in the current enquiry comprised poetry excerpts that were conveniently sampled. In particular, discourse analysis was employed to analyse rhetorical structure and text organisation in the target poetry excerpts, in such a way to capture the essence the biographies under scrutiny and their capacity to create extended rhetorics. The biographies were also investigated to evaluate their capacity t
creator: Said Bakour

story: Classical Arabic praise and mourning poems are secretly biographies. That is the claim of this 2024 study. It argues the poet builds a life story on three things: publicity (making a person known), immortalisation (making them last) and mythicisation (making them larger than life). So a poem could work a bit like a statue made of words.

Women who fasted for more than 15 days were compared with those who did not fast or fasted for less than 15 days in the month of Ramadan. summary: Makalah ini membincangkan analisis keperluan bahan bantu mengajar yang menerapkan elemen multimedia bagi Pengajaran dan Pembelajaran Kesusasteraan Melayu Komunikatif (KMK) secara interaktif. title: Prospects for the rapid development of pilgrimage and pilgrimage, tourism services in Uzbekistan
summary: This article discusses the potential for rapid growth and development of pilgrimage sites and tourism services in Uzbekistan. It explores the country's rich cultural and historical heritage, emphasizing the various religious sites that make it attractive to pilgrims and tourists. The analysis examines development strategies such as infrastructure improvements, promotion of religious and cultural tourism, international cooperation and sustainability practices. The note sheds light on the opportunities and challenges of using Uzbekistan's unique offerings to emerge as an influential player in pilgrimage tourism.

title: Effect of Ramadan Fasting on Cognitive Function of Physicians
summary: Introduction: Effect of fasting on human cognition has been a topic of recent research. The results of those studies are contradictory at best. Moreover, fasting as a religious ritual for an entire holy month of Ramadan has many denominators that differs from other pattern of fasting. Data on cognitive functions of physicians during Ramadan is scarce. We had investigated the effect of Ramadan fasting on physicians who are actively engaged in treating patients. Materials and Methods: This was a cross-sectional study conducted on 53 doctors working in a teaching hospital. Basic and task specific data were collected 1 week before and during Ramadan. story: Doctors treat patients all day, even in Ramadan. Does fasting change how sharply they think? This 2025 study notes that past research on fasting and thinking gives contradictory results, and that a whole month of religious fasting is not the same as other fasting. So it tested the thinking of working physicians while they fasted.

title: Muslim Dress Code and Its Health Benefits
summary: This article provided an overview of the history and benefits of Muslim dress code. It traced the origins and evolution of modest clothing styles prescribed in Islam and explored regional variations across Muslim majority cultures. Key benefits of adhering to Islamic dress standards around modesty are examined, including spiritual discipline, health aspects of loose fitting garments, and cultural identity affirmation. Common types of traditional Muslim attire such as hijāb, jalbāb and abāya are defined. The paper also looked at modern trends integrating Islamic dress principles with contemporary fashion design. story: This 2023 article from Ghana traces where modest Islamic dress came from and how it changed in different Muslim cultures. It also lists what it sees as the benefits: spiritual discipline, a sense of cultural identity, and the health side of wearing loose clothing.

title: The Misidentification of Maqām Kurd as Maqām Bayātī Among Gambus Players in Malaysia:Historical Perspectives and Theoretical Implications
summary: This article explores the misidentification of maqām Kurd as maqām Bayātī among Gambus players in Malaysia, a phenomenon rooted in traditional rote learning practices. Despite the similarities between the two maqāmāt, their theoretical distinction—particularly the half-flat E (quater-tones)—has been overlooked, leading to the blending of the two maqāmāt in performance. This study examines the historical and cultural factors that contributed to this misidentification, focusing on the challenges faced by players in recognizing and producing quarter-tones . By integrating historical and theoretical perspectives, the article analyzes how this misinterpretation has influenced the Malaysian Gambus
creator: Raja Zulkarnain Raja Yusof

story: Two Arabic musical scales, maqam Kurd and maqam Bayati, sound alike but differ in one note, the E. In Bayati it sits a quarter tone flat, between the notes a piano can play. This 2025 study finds that gambus players in Malaysia often mix the two up, and it traces the habit to learning by ear and by rote.

The whole episode being stitched with my political experience as a student has made immense impact on my take on contemporary democracy vis a vis the Muslim question.

This 2017 essay by Muhammed Shah S is personal: he writes about his own political struggle as a Muslim student during those protests, and how the experience changed the way he sees democracy and the "Muslim question" in India.

The objective of the study is to assess the infrastructural gap at Madarsas in Bihar. The study findings reveal the lack of infrastructural facilities in the Madrasas of Bihar. title: Diyarbakır’da Su Mimarisi Üzerine Bir Değerlendirme
summary: Anadolu'nun uygarlaşması diyebileceğimiz dönem içinde, çeşitli yerleşim alanlarında ve güzergâhlar üzerinde çok sayıda su yapısı inşa edilmiştir. title: History or Project? The Double Life of Islamic Art Since the 1970s
summary: This article argues that since the 1970s a duality divides the concept of Islamic Art. On the one hand, we have Islamic Art as the subject matter of a modern mode of historical inquiry, invented and developed in the colonial period in Europe but then taken up by scholars from around the world, including Muslim academics. This is the Islamic Art of Islamic Art History as a field of secular scholarship. But then, in the decolonization period, and more pronouncedly since the 1970s, we witness the birth of another concept of Islamic Art that is not focused on the past. This second notion of Islamic Art seeks to envisage Islamic Art as a component of a future-oriented project of reorganizing life

summary: The history of the gambus in Malaysia has long been framed through a “trade-route diffusion” model, which assumes Arab merchants introduced the instrument to Melaka as part of Indian Ocean exchange. It points to a "third sector" of cooperatives, social enterprises, waqf endowments and charities, and argues that Islamic principles of business could bring that sector into the mainstream, for growth with fairness.

title: Various Portrayals of Drugs and Drug Abuse in Turkish Cinema: A Sociological Analysis of Drug-related Turkish Movies
summary: This study aimed to analyze the portrayals of drugs and drug abuse in Turkish movies within a sociological context. Considering the mutual relationship between cinema and society, the question of whether drugs and drug abuse have been represented in these movies in a problem-based manner constitutes the main problematic of this study, which aims to analyze a variety of drug-related films. Therefore, 54 Turkish movies including the element of drugs have been chosen in a purposive sampling and they have been analyzed by using sociological film analysis as a research technique. Of the 54 movies in the sampling, only 27 depicted drug abuse and only 24 of them portrayed negative outcomes of drug
creator: Melih Çoban
source_name: Addicta: The Turkish Journal on Addictions
locator: DOI=10.5152/addicta.2021.21049; journal="Addicta: The Turkish Journal on Addictions"
scope_basis: Crossref search "turkish cinema"; publisher hosted in Türkiye
story: How do Turkish films show drugs? This 2021 study by Melih Çoban watched 54 Turkish movies that include drugs. Only 27 of them actually showed drug abuse, and only 24 showed it having bad results. The study asks whether cinema treats drugs as a problem, since films and society shape each other.

title: Qibla Orolboʻyi va Amudaryo oʻng sohilida shahar tuzilishining ekologik, diniy va iqtisodiy asoslari
summary: Maqola Qibla Orolbo‘yi va Amudaryo o‘ng sohili hududida antik davr shahar qurilishining murakkab ekologik, diniy va iqtisodiy asoslarini yoritadi. Mazkur hududdagi arxitekturaviy dizayn, urbanistik funksiyalar, zardushtiylik va boshqa diniy g‘oyalar asosida shakllangan makonlar tahlil qilinadi. Sug‘orish, mahsulot yetishtirish, diniy marosimlar o‘tkazish, aholi joylashuvi va mahalliy resurslardan foydalanish orqali shakllangan shahar hayoti zamonaviy arxeologik, antropologik va geofazoviy tadqiqotlar asosida o‘rganiladi.

story: What shaped ancient cities in the southern Aral Sea region and on the right bank of the Amu Darya? This 2025 Uzbek article explores the ecological, religious and economic foundations of their design, including the influence of Zoroastrianism.

title: Limestone In Islamic Religious Architecture: İstanbul And Turkish Thrace
summary: Research article in METU JOURNAL OF THE FACULTY OF ARCHITECTURE, 2013.
source_name: METU JOURNAL OF THE FACULTY OF ARCHITECTURE

story: Many mosques in Istanbul and Turkish Thrace were built of limestone. This 2013 article in the METU Journal of the Faculty of Architecture looks at the use of limestone in Islamic religious buildings in that region.

title: Alignment of Film and Society: Cancer in Iranian Cinema
summary: Research article in Motaleat-e Tatbiqi-e Honar by Ehsan Aqababaee, Zahra Lotfi Foroushani, 2023.
creator: Ehsan Aqababaee, Zahra Lotfi Foroushani
source_name: Motaleat-e Tatbiqi-e Honar
scope_basis: Crossref search "iranian cinema"; publisher hosted in Iran
story: Art has always tried to keep pace with society, and cinema is no exception. This 2023 Iranian study looks at how Iranian films have shown cancer, and how film can bring a practical, human side to the illness.

title: Journalism Transformation and Challenges in the Era of Artificial Intelligence: Exploring Malaysian Journalists’ and Journalism Students’ Perspectives
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) in the journalism industry, which is known as automated journalism, helps to improve the efficiency of the newsrooms. The purpose of this research was to emphasise the importance of technological advancement in the Malaysian journalism industry. Furthermore, this research fills a research gap in Malaysian journalists’ and journalism students’ perspectives on the development of AI technology in the industry. Drowning from that, technological determinism (TD) theory was applied in this research to explain the relationship between technological development and the changes in news readers’ social attitudes. This research was conducted as a qualitative study using the
creator: Jodie Ng
source_name: Al-i’lam - Journal of Contemporary Islamic Communication and Media
locator: DOI=10.33102/jcicom.vol4no2.111; journal="Al-i’lam - Journal of Contemporary Islamic Communication and Media"
scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic media journalism"; publisher hosted in Malaysia
story: Some newsrooms now use AI to help write and sort the news, sometimes called automated journalism. This 2024 study by Jodie Ng asked Malaysian journalists and journalism students what they think of it. It used the idea of technological determinism, which says new technology drives how society changes, including how readers see the news.

title: Imagining Lebanon with Islamic Art: The 1974 Exhibition at the Nicolas Sursock Museum
summary: Focusing on the first exhibition of Islamic art in Lebanon, organized by the Nicolas Sursock Museum in 1974, this article shows how the construction and the operationalization of the concept Islamic art overlapped with postcolonial endeavors to foster national identity. By closely examining the making of the art exhibition and tracing material histories intersecting in Beirut, it elicits constructions of the national, the secular, and the spiritual via the notion of art. It contributes to the growing scholarship on the historiography of Islamic art, regional museums, and nation-building in the second half of the 20th century.
creator: Sarah SABBAN
source_name: Regards
scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic art brazil"; publisher hosted in Lebanon
story: In 1974 the Nicolas Sursock Museum in Beirut held the first exhibition of Islamic art in Lebanon. This 2022 article shows how the very idea of "Islamic art" in that show became tangled up with questions of identity in a country leaving colonial rule behind, and how a museum helped imagine a nation.

title: Analysing Concept and Meaning of the Word “Eslimi” (An Arabesque) in Islamic Art from The Viewpoint of Islamic Wisdom
summary: Research article in Kimiya-ye-Honar by Mahdi Radjaei, Hasam Bolkhari, Seyed Mohammad Fadavi, 2023.
creator: Mahdi Radjaei, Hasam Bolkhari, Seyed Mohammad Fadavi
source_name: Kimiya-ye-Honar
scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic art brazil"; publisher hosted in Iran
story: Eslimi is the Persian word for arabesque, the curling plant patterns of Islamic art. This 2023 article explores the word's meaning through Islamic philosophy. It was written by Mahdi Radjaei, Hasam Bolkhari, Seyed Mohammad Fadavi and published in Kimiya-ye-Honar in 2023. Its record gives only the title and authors, so this is an outline.

title: Nigerian Film Industry and The New Normal
summary: In an interconnected world, film patently transcends boundaries. Film narratives occupy a significant position in configuring cultural narratives, political ideologies, religious identities, and social discourses. All these have resulted in the present evolution of the Nigerian film industry. However, the film industry keeps responding to the increasing transformation of the human world, from digital technologies to COVID-19. The COVID-19 pandemic, for instance, birthed significant innovative initiatives that have led to what can be called a “new normal,” especially in terms of a wider digital platform and accelerated expansion of the digital world. This growth permits both global and local
creator: Tolulope Ibikunle
source_name: International Journal of Indigenous Languages
locator: DOI=10.67432/ijilan.2026.0101.4-j; journal="International Journal of Indigenous Languages"
scope_basis: Crossref search "nigerian film hausa"; publisher hosted in Nigeria
story: Films cross borders and shape how people see culture, politics and religion. This 2026 paper by Tolulope Ibikunle looks at how Nigeria's film industry keeps changing with the world. COVID-19, it argues, pushed the industry onto digital platforms faster, creating a "new normal" that lets Nigerian films reach both local and global audiences.

title: Identification of Social Commerce Service Quality (SCSQ) dimensions for Malaysian modest fashion industry
summary: The purpose of this study is to identify emerging themes in the Social Commerce Service Quality (SCSQ) that are appropriate for the Malaysian modest fashion industry to improve the online shopping experience for Malaysian consumers. This qualitative research applied semi-structured online interviews that include nine respondents from Malaysian modest fashion sellers, direct and indirect distributors, and buyers. Thematic analysis was used to analyze the participants' responses in determining and identifying the SCSQ dimensions. Eight themes are identified which are Social Interaction Quality, Functional Quality, Design Quality, Information Quality, Privacy and Security, Responsiveness, Perso
creator: Izzati Hanafi, Rafikul Islam, Suharni Maulan
source_name: Global Business Management Review (GBMR)
scope_basis: Crossref search "modest fashion"; publisher hosted in Malaysia
story: Modest fashion, clothing that covers more of the body, is big business online in Malaysia, much of it sold through social media. This 2023 study by Izzati Hanafi, Rafikul Islam and Suharni Maulan interviewed nine sellers, distributors and buyers. It found eight things that make the shopping good, including social interaction, design, information, and privacy and security.

title: Kepatuhan Beraga Dalam Kalangan Usahawan Wanita Muslim Dalam Membangunkan Produk Kesihatan Di Malaysia [Religious Devotion Among Malaysian Muslim Women Entrepreneurs Dealing In Health Products]
summary: Setiap individu yang beragama Islam perlu memiliki elemen berpegang teguh pada agama Allah SWT bagi mencapai kejayaan dalam bidang keusahawanan. Elemen berpegang teguh pada agama Allah SWT yang dimaksudkan adalah berkait rapat dengan konsep dua kalimah syahadah yang digariskan dalam agama Islam. Kejayaan yang dikecapi oleh usahawan wanita Muslim yang mengusahakan produk kesihatan sudah tentu mempunyai pelbagai cabaran dan terpaksa menempuhi segala rintangan dalam dunia perniagaan. Sungguh pun begitu, cabaran sebagai seorang usahawan Muslim berjaya bukan sahaja dilihat dari segi jumlah pendapatan dalam perniagaan semata-mata, namun perlu juga berpegang teguh kepada ajaran Islam. Persoalannya,
creator: Yusma Fariza Yasin, Mohd Shukri Hanapi
source_name: Jurnal Islam dan Masyarakat Kontemporari
locator: DOI=10.37231/jimk.2023.24.1.774; journal="Jurnal Islam dan Masyarakat Kontemporari"
scope_basis: Crossref search "muslim health"; publisher hosted in Malaysia
story: For a Muslim businesswoman, does success mean only profit? This 2023 study by Yusma Fariza Yasin and Mohd Shukri Hanapi looks at Malaysian Muslim women who make health products. It argues that success also means holding firmly to Islam, tied to the shahada, the declaration of faith, while facing the many challenges of running a business.

title: A proposed program for the development of creativity in the Arabic calligraphy course among visual arts students
summary: The research deals with a proposed program to develop the creative ability associated with Arabic calligraphy among students of the fifth level of the Department of Visual Arts at the College of Design and Arts according to the creative activities and strategies used, and this study seeks to prepare a teaching program to develop the creativity of visual arts students to produce artworks related to Arabic calligraphy and Islamic art in a way General, and aims to raise the level of skill and technical performance of students at the fifth level in the Arabic calligraphy course based on the strategies and creative activities used for teaching, and allowing visual arts students to create artworks
creator: مها محمد ناصر, بدور عبدالله منصور
source_name: Basrah Arts Journal
scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic calligraphy art"; publisher hosted in Iraq
story: Can you teach creativity in Arabic calligraphy, an art with strict rules? This 2023 study from Iraq designs a teaching programme for fifth-level visual arts students at a college of design and arts. Using creative activities and strategies, it aims to raise their skill and help them make their own artworks linked to calligraphy and Islamic art.

title: Pelaksanaan Haji dan Umrah bagi Golongan Khuntha dan Mukhannath
summary: Research article in Jurnal Fiqh by Razali Shahabudin, Anisah Ab Ghani, 2015.

source_name: Jurnal Fiqh
scope_basis: Crossref search "umrah travel"; publisher hosted in Malaysia
story: How should people who are intersex (khuntha) or who act as the other gender (mukhannath) do hajj and umrah? This 2015 Malaysian study looks at Islamic law. It was written by Razali Shahabudin, Anisah Ab Ghani and published in Jurnal Fiqh in 2015. Its record gives only the title and authors, so this is an outline.

title: Diasporic Intertextual Musings: The Relevance of Classical Urdu Poetry to Contemporary Pakistani Situation in Nadeem Aslam’s The Golden Legend
summary: Anglophone literary works usually refer implicitly or explicitly to the culture, language and literature of authors’ native lands. Nadeem Aslam is one such author who makes explicit use of native language and literature in his fiction. Most of his works refer to classical Urdu poetry, phrases and extended adjectives to embellish as well as celebrate the rich legacy of the classical Urdu poetry tradition. Thus, intertextuality is a predominant feature of Aslam’s latest novel, The Golden Legend (2017). It is is not only an intertextual narrative but also an intercultural and inter-linguistic text because it incorporates popular classical Urdu poetry’s diction, metaphors and symbols. Aslam empl
creator: Qurratulaen Liaqat, Amra Raza
source_name: NUML journal of critical inquiry
locator: DOI=10.52015/numljci.v18ii.125; journal="NUML journal of critical inquiry"
scope_basis: Crossref search "urdu poetry"; publisher hosted in Pakistan
story: Nadeem Aslam is a novelist who writes in English but fills his books with classical Urdu poetry. This 2020 study by Qurratulaen Liaqat and Amra Raza looks at his 2017 novel The Golden Legend. It shows how he borrows Urdu poetry's words, metaphors and symbols, so the book reads across two languages and two cultures, and uses them to speak to Pakistan today.

title: The Role of Architecture Documentaries in The Adoption of Contemporary Design Approaches in Mosque Architecture: A Research on Architecture Students
summary: Research article in Iconarp International J. of Architecture and Planning by Begüm Aköz Çevrimli, Ceyhan Tazefidan, Hande Büşra Geyikli, 2024.

story: Can watching documentaries change how future architects design mosques? This 2024 study by Begüm Aköz Çevrimli, Ceyhan Tazefidan and Hande Büşra Geyikli asked architecture students in Turkey whether architecture documentaries made them more open to contemporary approaches to mosque design.

title: Ankara’daki Vakıf Üniversite Kütüphanelerinde Bütçe Yönetimi
summary: Teknolojinin ilerlemesi, bilgi kaynaklarının niteliğini ve kullanıcıların bilgi ihtiyaçlarını ve bilgi erişim davranışlarını değiştirmiştir. Kütüphaneler, bu değişimi takip etmek ve kullanıcıların bilgi gereksinimlerini karşılayabilmek için yeterli finansal kaynaklara ihtiyaç duymaktadır. Küresel ve yerel ekonomik gelişmeler, özellikle dövizdeki ve enflasyondaki yükseliş, üniversite kütüphanesi yöneticilerini bütçelerini daha etkin ve verimli kullanmaya zorlamaktadır. Bütçe yönetimi doğrultusunda hazırlanan etkili bir bütçeleme planlaması ve uygulaması, kütüphanenin belirlediği hedeflere ulaşmasını kolaylaştıracaktır. Bu araştırmada, Ankara’daki vakıf üniversitesi kütüphanelerinde bütçe yöne
creator: Mücahit Sert, Malik Yılmaz
source_name: Bilgi Dünyası
scope_basis: Crossref search "vakıf sistemi"; publisher hosted in Türkiye
story: Libraries need money to keep up with technology, and rising exchange rates and inflation in Turkey have squeezed university library budgets. This 2024 study by Mücahit Sert and Malik Yılmaz looked at how libraries at foundation, or private non-profit, universities in Ankara manage their budgets, since a good plan helps a library reach its goals.

title: A Comparative study of prison literature in Persian and Arabic literature: The case study of “ya sahebi- al- sejen” and “fifty three people”
summary: Research article in Studies in Arabic Narratology by Abdollah Hosseini, Kaveh Rahimi, 2022.
creator: Abdollah Hosseini, Kaveh Rahimi
source_name: Studies in Arabic Narratology
scope_basis: Crossref search "arabic literature"; publisher hosted in Iran
story: Prison has produced its own kind of literature. This 2022 article by Abdollah Hosseini and Kaveh Rahimi compares prison writing in Persian and Arabic, using two works, "Ya Sahebi al-Sejen" and "Fifty Three People."

title: Whistleblowing and Ethical Responsibility: Strengthening Accountability in Public Institutions through the Lens of Islamic Governance
summary: Whistleblowing has gained global recognition as a vital mechanism for combating corruption, enhancing transparency, and ensuring accountability across public institutions. In Islamic governance, whistleblowing is not merely a procedural tool but an ethical obligation rooted in foundational religious principles. Ethics encompasses a framework of moral principles that guide individual behavior and the execution of activities, underpinning standards of right and wrong related to human conduct in terms of rights, obligations, societal benefits, fairness, and virtues. It serves to assist individuals in considering the perspectives of the majority in their decision-making processes. Corruption is
creator: Engr. Sadia kalsoom
source_name: Al-Amīr Research Journal for Islamic Studies
locator: DOI=10.67101/alamir.v6i03.349; journal="Al-Amīr Research Journal for Islamic Studies"
scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic governance"; publisher hosted in Pakistan
story: A whistleblower is someone who reports wrongdoing from inside an organisation. This 2025 paper by Sadia Kalsoom argues that in Islamic governance, blowing the whistle on corruption is more than a procedure: it is an ethical duty rooted in religious principles, and a way to make public institutions more open and accountable.

title: Operation and Performance of Sufi-Led Political Parties in Contemporary Bangladesh
summary: Although Sufi-led political parties have been active in Bangladesh for almost four decades, they have received little scholarly attention. Therefore, this article discusses the historical context within which post-independence Sufi/Pir-centred political parties emerged, their interaction with other parties, and their electoral performance. It also touches upon some basic issues relating to Pir-cum political leaders: once a Pir becomes a politician, does his previous relationship with his murids (disciple) remain intact? This paper concludes that instead of posing any meaningful challenge to the political regimes, Pir-led parties have developed a tendency to maximise their political opportuni
creator: Mamun Al Mostofa
source_name: Social Science Review
scope_basis: Crossref search "sufi music performance"; publisher hosted in Africa (multi-country)
story: In Bangladesh, some political parties are led by pirs, Sufi spiritual guides with disciples called murids. They have been active for almost forty years but little studied. This 2023 article by Mamun Al Mostofa traces how they arose, how they do in elections, and asks whether a pir's bond with his followers survives when he becomes a politician. It finds they mostly chase opportunities rather than challenge governments.

title: Role of Waqf Investment Funds in the Development of Waqf (Applied Study on the Waqf Invest-ment Fund Human Rights Association)
summary: Development of endowments (an applied study on the endowment investment fund of the Human Association). In an attempt to extrapolate the reality of these funds and the extent of their need and results, the research aimed to stand on the experience of the Human Association Fund in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in this regard, where the research included two sections: An introductory study that dealt with the theoretical aspect of the subject of the study in terms of the concept of endowment, its importance and its origin in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. The first section went deeper by mentioning the nature of endowment investment funds, their origin, and their importance. The second topic has b
creator: Omar Al-Mehsen

story: A waqf is an endowment set up so its income does good forever. Some are now run as investment funds. This 2024 study by Omar Al-Mehsen, published in Saudi Arabia, looks at one such fund belonging to a charity in the kingdom, explaining how waqf investment funds began and why they matter.

title: Kırsal Mimari Miras Araştırması: Çavdarhisar Evleri
summary: Kütahya’nın Çavdarhisar ilçe sınırları içinde yer alan Aizanoi Antik Kenti’nde 2011-2020 yılları arasında yürütülen arkeolojik kazı çalışmalarının yanı sıra 2012-2015 yılları arasında Türk İslam Dönemi araştırmaları da yapılmıştır. Bu araştırma kapsamında eski ilçe merkezini oluşturan dört mahallede, saha ve ofis olmak üzere iki aşamalı olarak ilerleyen faaliyetler gerçekleştirilmiştir. Sahadan elde edilen ham veriler, ofis çalışmaları sırasında işlenerek kendi içinde gruplara ayrılmış ve envanter numarası verilerek arşivlenmiştir. Çalışmaların tam
creator: Kasım İnce, Mustafa Ekmekci
source_name: Arış

story: Near the ruins of the ancient city of Aizanoi, in Çavdarhisar in Turkey, archaeologists dug from 2011 to 2020. Alongside them, from 2012 to 2015, a team studied the much later Turkish-Islamic village around the site. In four old neighbourhoods they recorded houses on the spot, sketched plans and took photos, then catalogued every one. This 2024 study by Kasım İnce and Mustafa Ekmekci presents those rural houses.

title: İstanbul’daki 21. Yüzyıl Cami Minberlerinde Yenilikçi Yaklaşımlar
summary: Bu araştırmada İstanbul’da yenilikçi anlayışla inşa edilen 21. yüzyıl cami minberlerinde Modernizm kavramı ile gelişen fikir akımlarının minber üzerindeki etkisi, minber tasarımını oluşturan mimarların hangi fikir akımlarından etkilendiği, modern formların minber tasarımında nasıl karşılık bulduğu, geleneksel çizgilerden ne kadar uzaklaşıldığı saptanmaya çalışılmıştır. İncelenen minber formlarının çoğunlukla birbirini takip etmeyen farklı tasarımlara sahip olduğu belirlenmiştir. Minberlerin geleneksel minber tasarımlarından uzak formları, farklı teknik ve malzeme kullanımı, dönemin değişen mimari anlayışının bir yansıması olarak karşımıza çıkmaktadır. Endüstri Devrimi inşaat sektörünü etkile
creator: Bülent Oral, Zeliha Kılıç
source_name: Arış
scope_basis: Crossref search "cami mimarisi"; publisher hosted in Türkiye
story: A minbar is the pulpit in a mosque, usually a staircase with a fixed traditional shape. In twenty-first-century Istanbul, some architects have reimagined it. This 2026 study by Bülent Oral and Zeliha Kılıç found the new minbars mostly look nothing like each other, using new forms, techniques and materials, a sign of how ideas from modernism have reached even this old piece of mosque furniture.

title: Study and Identification of the Ornamental Architecture of Tabrizi Mosque in the Kashan City, and Comparison with Sepah Salar Mosque in Tehran City
summary: Research article in Parseh Journal of Archaeological Studies by Milad Baghsheikhi, 2021.

title: The Islamic Influences In Malay Manuscripts Writing:An Overview of Some Selected Manuscripts
summary: Malay manuscripts that have been produced in Malay Archipelago since 15th century had experienced some improvements due to Hinduism-Buddhism and Islamic transnational religious movements. Main aims of this paperwork are (i) to study a brief history of Malay manuscripts writing and (ii) to identify the contribution of Islam in Malay Manuscript literature. This paper will try to shed Islamic influences on a few works that have been wrote by Malay scholars in old Malay manuscripts. Within the context of this study, qualitative methodology has been applied to reveal a diverse array of topics by gathering data from Malay manuscripts, books, paper works and website. As a result, Islam play a huge
creator: Norhasnira Ibrahim, Faisal Ahmad Shah
source_name: Sains Insani
scope_basis: Crossref search "malay literature islamic"; publisher hosted in Malaysia
story: Malay manuscripts have been written in the Malay Archipelago since the 1400s, shaped first by Hindu-Buddhist and then by Islamic influences. This 2020 paper by Norhasnira Ibrahim and Faisal Ahmad Shah gives a short history of Malay manuscript writing and looks at selected works by Malay scholars, concluding that Islam played a huge part in them.

title: Rights of Women in Islamic and Pakistan Law and Constitution
summary: Men and women are two important groups universally inhabiting all thesocieties. Pakistan is a patriarchal society where men dominate women in all aspectsof life. story: What rights do women have under Islamic law and under Pakistan's laws and constitution, and do the two match? This 2020 article by Muhammad Akram Rana asks that question. It describes Pakistan as a patriarchal society and goes through laws including the Family Law Ordinance of 1961, the Hudood ordinances and the law of evidence.

title: An Explanatory Dictionary of Plant Names Based on Selected Examples of Classical Persian Poetry

story: Classical Persian poems are full of plants. This 2026 study builds a dictionary of their names, from examples in the poems. Its record says little more than this, so this is an outline.

Selain itu, terdapat isu dalam pemilihan, kandungan serta kualiti teks mata pelajaran Kesusasteraan Melayu Komunikatif yang boleh menjejaskan nilai karya-karya tersebut, pemikiran serta minat para pelajar. summary: This article examines debates surrounding the proper performance of communal dhikr, or reciting God’s name, within the Fayḍa Tijāniyya Sufi community in Senegal. story: In Senegal, some young members of the Fayda Tijaniyya Sufi community dance and drum while chanting God's name, a practice called yëngu, meaning "moving oneself". It is controversial. This 2023 article follows the debate over the right way to perform dhikr.

title: Ramadan Fasting: Perception and maternal outcomes during Pregnancy
summary: Objectives: To see perception and knowledge of women about Ramadan fasting and maternal effects of fasting. Methods: The study design was prospective, case-controlled. This study was conducted at Holy Family Hospital from 1st May 2020 to July 2020. Pregnant women with spontaneous conception and singleton pregnancies, who fasted for seven or more days, were cases, and those who did not fast were taken as controls. Questionnaire was filled regarding perception of women about maternal fasting. Primary maternal outcomes included preterm delivery, pregnancy induced hypertension, and gestational diabetes mellitus. The analysis was conducted using Statistical Package for Social Sciences version 16.

title: The Influence of Persian Poetry on Urdu Ghazal
summary: Urdu ghazal is a poetic form that encapsulates the emotions of love, loss, and mysticism, resonating deeply with readers across cultures. While the origins of ghazal can be traced back to Arabic poetry, its most significant development occurred in the Indian subcontinent, heavily influenced by Persian poetry. This paper highlights the historical context and literary techniques that Persian poetry introduced to Urdu ghazal, enriching its thematic depth and aesthetic appeal.
creator: Dr. Yasmeen Sultana Siddiqui

story: The Urdu ghazal is a poem about love, loss and mysticism. Its roots go back to Arabic poetry, but this 2023 study looks at how Persian poetry shaped it most, and how the form came to move readers across cultures.

title: Investigation on the Ergonomics Design of Wudhu' (Ablution) Station at a Mosque in a Higher Learning Institution
summary: The ablution area is compulsory for each mosque, and it is essential for Muslims to perform ablution ritual. Supposedly, the well-design of ablution station is one of the crucial aspects to be considered in prayer facility infrastructure, but certain mosques provide poor ablution. The objectives of the study were to investigate if there is a mismatch between the design of the existing ablution station with Malaysian anthropometry measurement, to identify the user’s satisfaction on existing ablution design through survey and to propose the improvement of the existing ablution station based on suitable anthropometry dimension and ergonomic aspects. The quantitative appraoch study was adopted.

summary: The issue of determining the Qibla direction in Indonesia is a problem in worship that is rarely considered by Muslims, as they typically follow the established direction without rechecking its accuracy. title: Analisis Pendapatan AdSense YouTube dengan Penayangan Iklan di Video YouTube Menurut Hukum Islam
summary: YouTube adalah situs berbagi video paling populer di dunia, dan bahkan dapat dianggap sebagai situs video yang paling sering dikunjungi dan diakses oleh pengguna internet. summary: Scholarship on the interaction between Islamic law and international humanitarian law (IHL) has grown considerably, yet much of it remains confined to abstract doctrinal comparison and has yet to engage seriously with how these frameworks operate in real armed conflicts shaped by religious identity. summary: This study aims to examine the trust of millennial generation in the role of sharia mobile banking in the ease of solving their financial problems. summary: This study aims to determine the role and function of the Sharia Supervisory Board in supervising BPRS Maslahat Dana Syariah Nusantara, the supervisory mechanism implemented by the Sharia Supervisory Board towards BPRS Maslahat Dana Syariah Nusantara, and the obstacles faced by the Sharia Supervisory Board in carrying out its supervisory function at BPRS Maslahat Dana Syariah Nusantara. summary: Khiyar ‘aib merupakan hak pembeli untuk membatalkan transaksi apabila ditemukan cacat pada barang yang dibeli. title: Analysis of the Effectiveness of Disbursement and Efficiency of Zakat and Alms Fund Management at the Zakat Amil Institution (LAZ) of Zakat Sukses
summary: This study aims to analyze the effectiveness and efficiency of zakat disbursement and management, as well as the management of infaq/sadaqah funds at the Zakat Amil Zakat Institution (LAZ) and Zakat Sukses. summary: This study examines the roots of traditional Islamic thought in Indonesia with a focus on the paradigm, influencing factors, and educational implications of Islamic boarding schools (pesantren). However, there are many problems with child adoption in Banda Aceh that aim to adopt children, especially civil servants, not only because they want to have children or help children and give love, but because there are civil servant allowances. summary: According to the potential zakat data in Indonesia, as reported by TEMPO.CO Jakarta, the National Zakat Agency (BAZNAS) states that the potential zakat in Indonesia reaches Rp 327 trillion per year. title: Kopyo'an Marriage(Education Of Students' Ketaawadhu’an At The Boarding School Al-Urwatul Wutsqo Islamic Boarding School, Jombang)
summary: Tawadhu' or 'humility' is an attitude that cannot arise by itself, because tawadhu' must bring his heart to submit, be obedient, surrender to Allah, and have compassion for humans. There are four aspects of attitude in compiling the tawadhu scale, namely showing respect and gentleness, communicating in a polite manner, apologizing if you act, and praying. If a person carries out these four aspects seriously, he will achieve an attitude of humility in him. One form of tawadhu' of a santri to Kyai is shown by the students of the Pondok Pesantren Al-urwatul Wutsqo Jombang in the way of marriage. summary: This study aims to describe efforts to determine the role of digital literacy in learning Islamic Religious Education in MAN 2 Surakarta. summary: Competition in the world of education is very tight, this is due to the many existing educational institutions. summary: The lifestyle of consumer behavior is growing very rapidly, especially with regard to the halal lifestyle. summary: Purpose – This study provides a comprehensive mapping of research developments on the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in the halal industry and identifies global trends, collaboration patterns, and contributing regions. summary: The global rashd al-qiblah is currently considered the most accurate and easily applicable method for measuring the qibla direction, as it utilizes the sun’s shadow during its transit above the Kaaba. The problem is that it happens only twice a year. This 2025 study proposes using stars that pass over the Kaaba's latitude instead.

summary: Halal tourism has become a business trend in various countries, including Indonesia. Its existence requires the support of various sharia-based financial institutions, such as Islamic banks. summary: Electronic cinema has transformed the worldwide movie industry by providing spectators with various movie content on digital platform. summary: This study reconstructs al-Farghānī’s concept of the southern astrolabe through an interdisciplinary approach combining Arabic philology and computational astronomy. summary: This study formulates a theoretical model based on field experience to integrate Bugis Makassar local wisdom into Islamic Religious Education (PAI) at IAIN Parepare. summary: The implementation of the "Merdeka Curriculum" (Independent Curriculum) in Arabic language learning at Madrasah Aliyah Negeri Pangkep aims to foster student-centred learning, promote autonomy, and align education with the needs of 21st-century skills. summary: This paper attempts to examine the historical development of astronomy, focusing on the lineage from Prophet Seth to Prophet Idris. summary: Both Daar El Qolam 2 and La Tansa Mashiro are Islamic Educational Institution that has a special characteristic. title: Blended Learning in Islamic Religious Education At Al-Manshur Al-Islamy Islamic Boarding School and Al-Atsary Islamic Junior High School (MTs) Kediri
summary: This study examines implementing the blended learning method in Islamic Religious Education (PAI) at Al Manshur Al Islamy Islamic Boarding School and Al-Atsary Islamic Junior High School (MTs) in Kediri. The research utilizes a descriptive qualitative approach, collecting data through field observations, interviews, and document analysis. The findings reveal that both institutions employ a blended learning model, which integrates traditional and modern approaches to PAI instruction. summary: Waqf is one of the financing instruments in Islam. Along with the times, waqf is transformed not only consumptive but also productive. In reality, this potential cannot be optimally realized, one of which is due to the low level of literacy in public knowledge about waqf. summary: As the country with the largest Muslim population, Indonesia faces multiple challenges in implementing an effective Halal Product Assurance (JPH) system. story: Indonesia has the largest Muslim population in the world, and its halal product guarantee system is key to public trust. This 2025 study points out a paradox: inconsistent laws on halal certification can get in the way of innovation.

summary: Toilet Masjid merupakan bagian dari tempat peribadatan ummat Islam yang tidak boleh luput dari aturan posisi dan arahnya, karena Rasulullah saw. telah menjelaskan suatu larangan buang hajat dengan menghadap atau membelakangi kiblat. summary: Abstract This article will explain about the integration of Islam and local culture in the architecture of ancient mosques in Java. summary: The increased role of technology and the complexity of societal changes have ushered in a new era in education, known as Civil Society 5.0.
