summary: The integration of Islamic ethics into pro-environmental consumer behavior has emerged as a rapidly expanding research domain; however, extant frameworks remain fragmented. summary: This study aims to analyze strategies for moral education for students through a community-based approach at the Al-Hidayah Islamic Boarding School in Tenggarong. title: Prioritization of barriers to halal certification adoption for food SME: a study using Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process
summary: Halal certification plays a crucial role in boosting Muslim consumer confidence and expanding both domestic and international market opportunities. summary: Technology has a significant influence on various aspects of life, particularly in education. summary: This study aims to determine the extent and how much influence the criminal content of YouTube Nessie Judge on the anxiety level of University of North Sumatra students and how the anxiety level of University of North Sumatra students who watch criminal content YouTube Nessie Judge based on the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HARS). summary: The rapid growth of Shariah banking in Indonesia has prompted significant regulatory developments to align financial practices with Islamic principles. title: Revitalization of Islamic Family Law Through the Management of Islamic Philanthropy Based on Zakat, Infaq, and Alms
summary: This study examines the revitalization of Islamic family law through strengthening the management of Islamic philanthropy based on zakat, infaq, and sedekah (ZIS) in response to the increasing socio-economic challenges of modern Muslim families. The main problem lies in the weak implementation of family law, which is often influenced by economic conditions, such as alimony, divorce, and child protection. This study aims to analyze the strategic contribution of ZIS management in strengthening the function of Islamic family law. The research method uses a library study approach with content analysis of primary and secondary literature related to ZIS, family law, and national zakat regulations.
creator: Muhammad Romi, Akbarizan Akbarizan, Nurcahaya Nurcahaya
source_name: Tasyri' :  Journal of Islamic Law
locator: DOI=10.53038/tsyr.v5i1.425; journal="Tasyri' :  Journal of Islamic Law"
scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic law constitution"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: When money is tight, family law often breaks down, over things like maintenance, divorce and protecting children. This 2026 study by Muhammad Romi, Akbarizan Akbarizan and Nurcahaya Nurcahaya argues that better management of Islamic giving, zakat, infaq and sadaqah, could help Islamic family law do its job for struggling Muslim families.

title: Implementing Blockchain Technology in Halal Certification: A Systematic Literature Review of Opportunities and Challenges
summary: Objectives: This study aims to identify trends, key themes, opportunities, and challenges in the application of blockchain technology in halal certification activities. Design/Method/Approach: This study used the Systematic Literature Review (SLR) method with the PRISMA guidelines. Data were collected from Google Scholar using Publish or Perish (PoP). Findings: the research found that blockchain has significant potential to enhance transparency, efficiency, traceability, and accountability in halal certification through features such as smart contracts and decentralized storage. However, significant challenges remain, including infrastructure readiness, human resource limitations, the absenc
creator: Tri Wahyuni, Luqman Hakim Handoko
source_name: AL-FALAH : Journal of Islamic Economics
locator: DOI=10.29240/alfalah.v2i10.14669; journal="AL-FALAH : Journal of Islamic Economics"
scope_basis: Crossref search "halal blockchain"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: A blockchain is a shared digital record that is very hard to change secretly. This 2025 review by Tri Wahyuni and Luqman Hakim Handoko looked at research on using it for halal certification. It found it could make certification more transparent, efficient and traceable, but faces real problems, including weak infrastructure and too few trained people.

title: The Role of the Government in the Development of Indonesian Sharia Banking
summary: Research article in Journal of Private and Commercial Law, 2021.
source_name: Journal of Private and Commercial Law
locator: DOI=10.15294/jpcl.v5i1.30123; journal="Journal of Private and Commercial Law"
scope_basis: Crossref search "sharia banking"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Governments can help a new kind of banking grow. This 2021 study in the Journal of Private and Commercial Law looks at the role the Indonesian government has played in developing sharia banking.

title: Cash Waqf Management in the Tabung Waqf Program Dompet Dhuafa and its Implications for Sustainable Development Goals
summary: The low level of public literacy and understanding of waqf, especially cash waqf and productive waqf which are currently developing, has resulted in the non-optimal utilization of the potential of waqf as an instrument to improve people's welfare. The purpose of this study is to analyze cash waqf management in the Dompet Dhuafa waqf savings program in accordance with the waqf core principle and its implications for sustainable development goals. The research method is a descriptive qualitative approach with library research. The results of this study indicate that the Dompet Dhuafa waqf savings program is in accordance with the waqf core principle, namely having a legal foundation, waqf supe
creator: Habibah Moslem, Erika Amalia
source_name: Proceeding of International Conference on Islamic Economics, Islamic Banking, Zakah and Waqf
locator: DOI=10.24090/ieibzawa.v1i.776; journal="Proceeding of International Conference on Islamic Economics, Islamic Banking, Zakah and Waqf"
scope_basis: Crossref search "waqf innovation"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Cash waqf lets people give money, not land, as an endowment whose returns help others forever. But many people barely understand it. This 2023 study by Habibah Moslem and Erika Amalia looks at the waqf savings programme of Dompet Dhuafa, an Indonesian charity, and finds it follows the core principles of waqf, with links to the UN's Sustainable Development Goals.

title: Kajian Estetika Simbolik Mihrab Masjid Raya Al Jabbar Bandung
summary: Tulisan ini menelusuri makna estetika simbolik bentuk mihrab pada Masjid Raya Al Jabbar Bandung. Bentuk mihrab pada masjid ini berbeda dengan bentuk mihrab masjid konvensional, sehingga menarik untuk dicari latar belakang makna dan konteksnya. Analisis ini mengunakan metode etnografi yaitu dengan membuat analisis deskriptif bentuk mihrab tersebut dikaitkan dengan makna bentuk sejenis yang terdapat pada kebudayaan lokal tempat masjid tersebut berada. Analisis kajian menggunakan makna bentuk dasar pada kebudayaan lokal Sunda, khususnya yang relevan dengan bentuk mihrab. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa meskipun bentuknya berbeda dengan model mihrab konvensional, tetapi memiliki makna simboli
creator: Jamaludin Jamaludin, Boyke Arief TF, Utami Utami
source_name: Panggung
scope_basis: Crossref search "masjid seni bina"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: The mihrab is the niche in a mosque that shows the direction of prayer. At the Al Jabbar Grand Mosque in Bandung, Indonesia, it does not look like a normal mihrab. This 2024 study by Jamaludin Jamaludin, Boyke Arief TF and Utami Utami compares its shape with basic forms from local Sundanese culture, and finds that even though it looks different, it still carries symbolic meaning.

title: Etika Bisnis dalam Pemasaran Travel Haji dan Umrah (Studi pada PT. Andamas Mabrur Wisata Cabang Surabaya)
summary: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui penerapan etika bisnis dalam strategi pemasaran di PT Andamas Mabrur Wisata Cabang Surabaya, yang menghadapi tantangan bersaing di industri pariwisata religi. Etika bisnis, sebagai landasan moral, menekankan integritas, transparansi, keadilan, kejujuran, amanah, dan tanggung jawab sosial dalam kegiatan bisnis. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan metode analisis deskriptif. Data dikumpulkan melalui wawancara dengan pegawai, observasi langsung, serta analisis dokumen. Teori taraf makro, meso, dan mikro digunakan sebagai landasan untuk mengetahui penerapan etika bisnis dalam komunikasi pemasaran di berbagai konteks. Hasil penelitian
creator: Muhammad Rafi Sechan, Ahmad Khairul Hakim, Airlangga Bramayudha
source_name: JIESP Journal of Islamic Economics Studies and Practices
locator: DOI=10.54180/jiesp.2025.4.1.1-12; journal="JIESP Journal of Islamic Economics Studies and Practices"
scope_basis: Crossref search "umrah travel"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Selling pilgrim trips to Mecca is a competitive business. This 2025 study by Muhammad Rafi Sechan, Ahmad Khairul Hakim and Airlangga Bramayudha looks at PT Andamas Mabrur Wisata in Surabaya, Indonesia, and how it builds business ethics, honesty, transparency, fairness and trustworthiness, into the way it markets Hajj and Umrah travel.

title: Islamic Boarding School Strategies for Preventing Underage Marriage
summary: Underage marriage remains a persistent social issue in Indonesia despite the enactment of Law Number 16 of 2019, which raised the minimum legal age of marriage for both men and women to nineteen years. Although legal reform provides stronger protection for children, its effectiveness largely depends on the active participation of educational institutions, particularly Islamic boarding schools (pesantren), in promoting awareness and preventive education. This study aims to analyze the strategies implemented by Nurul Azhar Talawe Islamic Boarding School, Sidenreng Rappang Regency, in preventing underage marriage following the legal reform of marriage age. This study employed a qualitative fiel
creator: Hasdar B Haryanto, Agus Muchsin, M. Ali Rusdi
source_name: Golden Ratio of Law and Social Policy Review
locator: DOI=10.52970/grlspr.v6i1.2481; journal="Golden Ratio of Law and Social Policy Review"
scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic boarding school"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: In 2019, Indonesia raised the minimum age of marriage for both men and women to nineteen. Laws alone do not stop child marriage, though. This 2026 study by Hasdar B Haryanto, Agus Muchsin and M. Ali Rusdi looks at how one Islamic boarding school, Nurul Azhar Talawe in Sidenreng Rappang, works to prevent underage marriage among its students.

title: Management And Technology In Islamic Education: Integrative Strategies For The Digital Era
summary: ABSTRACT The development of information and communication technology has significantly influenced the education sector, including Islamic educational institutions. In the digital era, Islamic education is challenged to adapt to technological advancements while upholding its core religious and ethical values. This study aims to explore integrative strategies that combine educational management and technology within Islamic institutions. Using a qualitative descriptive approach through literature review, the study examines various scholarly sources related to Islamic educational management, digital transformation, and educational technology. The findings indicate that effective integration of
creator: Arini Sadiyah, Nuri Firdausiah, Ifan Ali Alfatani
source_name: EDUSHOPIA : Journal of Progressive Pedagogy
locator: DOI=10.64431/edushopia.v2i2.354; journal="EDUSHOPIA : Journal of Progressive Pedagogy"
scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic app digital technology"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Islamic schools face a double task in the digital age: keep up with technology while holding on to their religious and ethical values. This 2025 review by Arini Sadiyah, Nuri Firdausiah and Ifan Ali Alfatani explores strategies that combine good school management with educational technology to do both.

title: Green banking practices and HRM in enchancing innovation capability: A knowledge management perspective on sharia banking performance
summary: This study investigates the influence of green banking practices and human resource management (HRM) on innovation capability and examines the mediating role of knowledge management in enhancing Sharia banking performance. Using a quantitative approach with Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) based on Partial Least Squares (PLS), data were collected through questionnaires distributed to employees using a saturated sampling technique. The findings reveal that HRM significantly affects green banking, innovation capability, and knowledge management. However, innovation capability does not significantly mediate the relationship between green banking and performance, nor between HRM and performanc
creator: Satria Avianda Nurcahyo, Tri Wikaningrum, Anis Malik Thoha
source_name: Diponegoro International Journal of Business
locator: DOI=10.14710/dijb.8.1.2025.28-49; journal="Diponegoro International Journal of Business"
scope_basis: Crossref search "sharia banking"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Green banking means banks trying to protect the environment through how they work. This 2025 study by Satria Avianda Nurcahyo, Tri Wikaningrum and Anis Malik Thoha surveyed employees of an Indonesian sharia bank. It found good management of staff boosted green banking, innovation and knowledge-sharing, but innovation did not turn those into better performance the way expected.

title: Bridging Waqf and Sukuk: Cross-Country Insights from Indonesia and Malaysia on Islamic Social Finance Innovation
summary: Abstract The integration of waqf and sukuk is a strategic innovation in productive waqf management to support socio-economic development. Indonesia and Malaysia, as two countries with the largest Muslim populations and rapidly growing Islamic financial infrastructures, are relevant case studies to explore the implementation of this model. This research aims to examine sukuk-based productive waqf management in Indonesia and Malaysia, highlighting the challenges, potentials, and implementation of the integration model. This research utilizes a descriptive qualitative method with a phenomenological approach. The results show that waqf-based sukuk is a strategic innovation to optimize waqf asset
creator: Mufti Afif, Syahruddin, Khurun’in Zahro’
source_name: Muslim Heritage
scope_basis: Crossref search "waqf innovation"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Sukuk are Islamic bonds, and waqf is an endowment that gives forever. Indonesia and Malaysia have tried combining the two. This 2025 study by Mufti Afif, Syahruddin and Khurun'in Zahro' compares how both countries do it, and argues waqf-based sukuk are a smart way to make waqf assets do more for society.

title: Comparison of Condition of Male Pencak Silat Athletes Suriname and Male Pencak Silat West Sumatera
summary: Purpose. This study aims to compare the physical condition of male pencak silat athletes from West Sumatra and Suriname through nine physical tests (endurance, agility, speed, strength, explosive power, balance, and flexibility). Methods. Descriptive analysis shows that the average physical condition test carried out for speed, agility, strength, flexibility, balance and endurance of athletes from West Sumatra is higher in all components. Result. However, the independent t test showed no statistically significant difference (p > 0.05) in all variables, which means the physical condition of both groups is relatively equal. Conclussions. Research with a larger sample is needed to confirm this
creator: Florence Wangsabesari Jamin, Japhet Ndayisenga, Juanda Putra
source_name: International Martial Arts and Culture Journal
locator: DOI=10.24036/imacj85019; journal="International Martial Arts and Culture Journal"
scope_basis: Crossref search "martial art pencak silat"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Pencak silat is a martial art with athletes in both West Sumatra and Suriname. This 2026 study compared male athletes from West Sumatra and Suriname on nine physical tests. West Sumatra's averages were higher on every one, but statistically the difference was not significant, so the two groups were about equal. A bigger study is needed to be sure.

title: The Role of Islam Religious Scholars in Politics
summary: Usaama al-Azami’s Islam and the Arab Revolutions: The Ulama Between Democracy and Autocracy represents a significant contribution to the growing body of literature examining the political role of religious scholars in the modern Muslim world, particularly in the context of the Arab Spring. Published in 2022 by Oxford University Press, the book seeks to disturb centuries-old presumptions over the "apolitical" or "quietist" nature of most of these traditional ulama and instead lays bare how intimately involved they remain within broader systems of politics—either as the carriers of dissent or tools of authoritarian rule. Al-Azami’s work is distinguished not only by its bold argumentation but a
creator: Syeda Dur e Nayab Haider
source_name: Muslim Politics Review
scope_basis: Crossref search "muslim politics democracy"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Are Muslim religious scholars really above politics? This 2025 review by Syeda Dur e Nayab Haider looks at Usaama al-Azami's 2022 book Islam and the Arab Revolutions, from Oxford University Press. The book challenges the old idea that traditional ulama stay out of politics, showing them deeply involved during the Arab Spring, sometimes as voices of protest and sometimes as tools of authoritarian rule.

title: Standardization of Handover Procedures for Officials Empowered to Draw Up Waqf Pledge Deeds An Effort to Overcome Administrative Barriers to Historical Waqf Documents
summary: The weakness of waqf land certification in Indonesia is often rooted in internal management issues at the upstream level, particularly regarding document integrity at the Office of Religious Affairs (KUA). This policy paper examines the phenomenon of personnel rotation occurring without strict archive handover procedures and the weak documentation management at the district level, which systematically triggers administrative procedural complexities. Such conditions cause historical data, such as the original Waqf Pledge Deeds, to frequently be lost or damaged, thereby hindering the judicial evidentiary process before land authorities. This documentary uncertainty triggers high risks of land
creator: Khamdani
source_name: AMUYA: INDONESIAN JOURNAL OF MANAGEMENT REVIEWS
locator: DOI=10.61860/amuya.v2i2.90; journal="AMUYA: INDONESIAN JOURNAL OF MANAGEMENT REVIEWS"
scope_basis: Crossref search "waqf innovation"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: In Indonesia, land given as waqf is recorded in pledge deeds kept at the local Office of Religious Affairs. This 2026 policy paper by Khamdani finds that when staff change jobs without properly handing over files, original deeds get lost or damaged, which then makes it hard to prove the land is waqf in court. It proposes standard handover procedures.

title: Clifford's Algebraic Approach in Determining the Direction of Qibla
summary: While classical methods and hisab methods based on spherical trigonometry and vector algebra are commonly used, this article introduces a more elegant, purely geometric alternative using Clifford Algebra (within the framework of Geometric Algebra). This method uses unit vectors in three-dimensional space to represent the positions of the observer and the Kaaba, then projects these vectors onto the local horizontal plane using geometric operations such as the dot product and the outer product. The results of the Qibla direction calculations for five major cities in Indonesia—Jakarta, Surabaya, Medan, Bandung, and Makassar—when compared with the spherical trigonometry and vector algebra method
creator: Muhamad Imam Mutamaqin, Muhamad Safa’udin
source_name: Noumerico: Journal of Technology in Mathematics Education
locator: DOI=10.33367/jtme.v4i1.8810; journal="Noumerico: Journal of Technology in Mathematics Education"
scope_basis: Crossref search "qibla determination"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Muslims pray facing the Kaaba in Mecca, so you need to know which way that is. This 2026 paper by Muhamad Imam Mutamaqin and Muhamad Safa'udin uses Clifford algebra, a branch of geometry, treating the observer and the Kaaba as arrows in 3D space and projecting them onto the ground. It tested the method on five Indonesian cities, including Jakarta and Makassar, against the usual methods.

title: Analisis Strategi Pemasaran Syariah Pada UMKM Fashion Muslim Nibras House Sooko Mojokerto di Era Digital
summary: Micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) play an important role in the Indonesian economy, both in creating jobs and strengthening the national economy. However, amid the rapid pace of digital technology development, MSMEs cannot rely solely on traditional methods such as manual or offline marketing. Indonesia is a country with a Muslim majority population. This presents a huge opportunity for the Muslim fashion industry, including the Nibras brand located in Sooko Mojokerto. This study aims to examine in depth the application of sharia marketing strategies through the 7Ps at Nibras House Sooko Mojokerto, as well as its implementation in digital marketing. The research method used a desc
creator: Nur Fadhilah Ahmadah, Mustofa Mustofa
source_name: Akuntansi Pajak dan Kebijakan Ekonomi Digital
locator: DOI=10.61132/apke.v2i4.1768; journal="Akuntansi Pajak dan Kebijakan Ekonomi Digital"

story: Nibras is a Muslim fashion brand in Sooko, Mojokerto, Indonesia. This 2025 study by Nur Fadhilah Ahmadah and Mustofa Mustofa looks at how its local store uses sharia marketing, the "7Ps" of marketing guided by Islamic values, and how it takes that approach online in the digital era.

title: Analisis Model AISAS (Attention, Interest, Search, Action, Dan Share) Pada Branding Bisnis Fashion Muslim (Studi Kasus: Dian Pelangi)
summary: Perkembangan bisnis fashion muslim di Indonesia telah mengalami pertumbuhan yang pesat dalam beberapa tahun terakhir. Dalam menghadapi persaingan yang semakin ketat, para pelaku bisnis fashion muslim perlu mengembangkan strategi branding yang efektif untuk menarik perhatian konsumen potensial. Oleh karena itu, penting untuk memahami metode yang efektif dalam mempromosikan merek dan produk dalam industri ini. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis metode model AISAS (Attention, Interest, Search, Action, dan Share) dalam konteks bisnis fashion muslim Dian Pelangi, analisis dengan model AISAS diharapkan dapat meningkatkan brand awareness, memperluas basis konsumen, dan meningkatkan penjual
creator: Chantika Qintara Fatharani, Ira Wirasari
source_name: Journal of Economic, Bussines and Accounting (COSTING)
locator: DOI=10.31539/costing.v7i4.10368; journal="Journal of Economic, Bussines and Accounting (COSTING)"
scope_basis: Crossref search "muslim fashion"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Dian Pelangi is an Indonesian Muslim fashion brand. This 2024 study by Chantika Qintara Fatharani and Ira Wirasari analyses its branding with the AISAS model: Attention, Interest, Search, Action and Share, the steps a shopper goes through online, as a way to grow awareness, customers and sales in a crowded market.

title: Syawalan Lopis in Krapyak: Culinary Tradition as an Expression of Coastal Islam and Social Cohesion
summary: The Syawalan Lopis tradition in Krapyak, Pekalongan, represents an expression of coastal Muslim religiosity by integrating religious rituals, social gatherings, and local culture into a unified communal celebration held on the 8th of Shawwal. In this tradition, lopis—typically recognized as a glutinous rice delicacy in other regions—is prepared as a giant lopis that serves as the ritual centerpiece. The event involves religious leaders, descendants of the tradition’s founder, local residents, and the municipal government, transforming Krapyak annually into a communal space where the religious and cultural identity and solidarity of coastal communities are celebrated. This study analyzes the
creator: Irfa Nadhifatul Ulya, Annisa Rahmalia Dardiri
source_name: Tabéq: Journal of Local Wisdom, Belief, and Peace
locator: DOI=10.67377/tabeq.v1i2.21; journal="Tabéq: Journal of Local Wisdom, Belief, and Peace"
scope_basis: Crossref search "culinary tradition muslim"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Every year on the 8th of Shawwal, a week after Eid, the Krapyak area of Pekalongan, Indonesia, celebrates with a giant lopis, a sticky-rice treat that is normally small. The Syawalan Lopis tradition brings together religious leaders, descendants of its founder, local people and the city government. This 2026 study by Irfa Nadhifatul Ulya and Annisa Rahmalia Dardiri shows how one huge dish holds a coastal community together.

title: Exploring Islamic Character Values in Nussa The Movie: Relevance and Implementation in Islamic Education
summary: This research delves into depicting Islamic character values in 'Nussa The Movie,' examining its relevance and application in Islamic education. Employing a qualitative methodology with descriptive content analysis, the study scrutinizes the movie's narrative, dialogues, and visual elements. Seven key Islamic character values identified include good role modeling, wisdom, generosity, patience, honesty, justice, and sincerity. The findings suggest that 'Nussa The Movie' transcends mere entertainment, emerging as a potent tool for imparting Islamic character education to children. These values are intricately interwoven with the movie’s narrative, offering viewers examples of character traits
creator: M. Ferry Irawan, Nikentari Rizky, Alia Latifah
source_name: HEUTAGOGIA: Journal of Islamic Education
locator: DOI=10.14421/hjie.2023.32-05; journal="HEUTAGOGIA: Journal of Islamic Education"
scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic education brazil"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Nussa The Movie is an Indonesian animated film for children. This 2023 study by M. Ferry Irawan, Nikentari Rizky and Alia Latifah watched its story, dialogue and visuals closely and found seven Islamic character values: being a good role model, wisdom, generosity, patience, honesty, justice and sincerity, arguing the film can help teach children character.

title: Pengaruh Tiktok Shop, Uang Saku Dan Literasi Keuangan Terhadap Perilaku Konsumtif Pengguna Aplikasi Tiktok Pada Mahasiswa Fakultas Keguruan Dan Ilmu Pendidikan Universitas Islam Riau
summary: Research article in JPEK (Jurnal Pendidikan Ekonomi dan Kewirausahaan) by Siti Maimunah, 2024.
creator: Siti Maimunah
source_name: JPEK (Jurnal Pendidikan Ekonomi dan Kewirausahaan)

scope_basis: Crossref search "tiktok religious"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Does TikTok Shop make students spend more? This 2024 study at the Islamic University of Riau, Indonesia, looked at teacher-training students and tested how TikTok Shop, pocket money and money skills affect their spending habits.

title: Developing A Maslahah-Based Model Of Islamic Social Entrepreneurship Through Impact Investment: An Al-Ghazali Perspective
summary: This study aims to analyze Islamic Social Entrepreneurship (ISE) and impact investment from the perspective of Al-Ghazali’s maslahah and to develop a conceptual model for sustainable economic development. This research employs a qualitative approach using a systematic literature review of Scopus and Sinta-indexed journals from 2020–2025. The findings reveal that ISE and impact investment are inherently aligned with Islamic economic principles, emphasizing a balance between financial returns and social impact. From Al-Ghazali’s perspective, economic activities should be oriented toward maslahah, encompassing justice, social welfare, and public benefit. This study proposes a novel conceptual m
creator: Sifwatir Rif'ah, Muhammad Lathoif Ghozali
source_name: JOURNAL OF SHARIA ECONOMICS
scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic social entrepreneurship"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Can you make money and do good at the same time? This 2026 paper by Sifwatir Rif'ah and Muhammad Lathoif Ghozali looks at Islamic social entrepreneurship and impact investing through the ideas of al-Ghazali, the medieval scholar, who said economic life should aim at maslahah: justice, welfare and the public good. It proposes a model built on that.

title: Assessing Social Sustainability in Mosque as Religious Building, Case Study: Al-Lathiif Mosque, Bandung-West Java, Indonesia
summary: A mosque is a place of worship for Muslims that emphasizes the concept of Rahmatan Lil Alamin, meaning to bring blessings to all people. Based on this statement, a mosque serves as a safe and comfortable space for performing ritual prayers and as a venue for accommodating social activities for its congregants. The function of mosques evolves, especially during the month of Ramadan. It becomes more active and serves various purposes beyond prayers, including religious, political, economic, educational, commercial, social, and cultural activities. All of these activities aim to foster social interaction among Muslim communities. This research aims to uncover the behavior and movements of worsh
creator: Indri Astrina Fitria Indrarani, Shaufa Salsabila Sari, Aldyfra Luhulima Lukman
source_name: Journal of Islamic Architecture
scope_basis: Crossref search "mosque architecture"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: A mosque is not only for prayer. In Ramadan especially, it hosts religious, educational, social and cultural life. This 2025 study by Indri Astrina Fitria Indrarani, Shaufa Salsabila Sari and Aldyfra Luhulima Lukman watched how worshippers moved and behaved at Al-Lathiif Mosque in Bandung, Indonesia, to judge how well it supports community life.

title: Uji Akurasi Arah Kiblat Masjid Pondok Pesantren Sunan Drajat Kecamatan Paciran Kabupaten Lamongan Dengan Metode Mizwala Qibla Finder
summary: The mosque is one of the most important places for Muslims, one of which is the mosque at the Sunan Drajat Islamic Boarding School. The mosque is a place of worship for all Muslims, where one of the conditions and pillars that must be met is facing the Qibla, therefore further research is needed to determine the Qibla direction of the Sunan Drajat Islamic Boarding School Mosque. One of the measurement methods that can be applied is the Mizwala Qibla Finder Method. This study uses a field research method and the data collected includes general information about the Sunan Drajat Islamic Boarding School Mosque and the method of determining the Qibla direction of the mosque. Data collection tech
creator: Yasirul Amin, Sutopo Sutopo
source_name: JOSH: Journal of Sharia
scope_basis: Crossref search "qibla determination"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Facing the Qibla, the direction of Mecca, is a condition of prayer, so a mosque must point the right way. This 2022 study by Yasirul Amin and Sutopo Sutopo checked the mosque at Sunan Drajat Islamic Boarding School in Lamongan, Indonesia, using a tool called the Mizwala Qibla Finder.

title: Kiai Kampung and Traditional Islamic Orthodoxy: A Socio-religious Study of Mosque-based Authority in Rembang, Central Java, Indonesia
summary: The role of kiai kampung as local religious authorities in Indonesia has evolved dynamically in response to shifting socio-political landscapes and changing patterns of Islamic religious authority. This paper examines the role of kiai kampung as socio-religious agents in managing mosques and preserving traditional Islamic orthodoxy in Indonesia's Reform era. Kiai kampung effectively translates Islamic principles to grassroots levels as they influence social, religious, and political discussions through regular preaching and sermons (khutbah). The study uses field research to observe da'wah practices and institutional affiliations in Rembang, Central Java. Using the concepts of agency and cul
creator: Ali Ja'far
source_name: Walisongo: Jurnal Penelitian Sosial Keagamaan
locator: DOI=10.21580/ws.32.2.23455; journal="Walisongo: Jurnal Penelitian Sosial Keagamaan"
scope_basis: Crossref search "traditional mosque design"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: In Indonesian villages, the local religious teacher, the kiai kampung, often runs the mosque. This 2024 study by Ali Ja'far looks at these village kiai in Rembang, Central Java, and finds they carry Islamic teaching down to everyday people and shape social, religious and political talk through their regular sermons.

title: Barriers to halal cosmetic certification: Insights from local cosmetic producers in Brunei
summary: Purpose – This study investigates the experiences and challenges encountered by local cosmetic producers in Brunei in obtaining halal certification for their products.Methodology – A qualitative research design was employed in this study, with data collected through semi-structured interviews involving eight local cosmetic producers in Brunei, all of whom were considered MSMEs.Findings – The study identifies the bottlenecks to obtaining halal certification revolving around inexpedient requirements during application, tedious approval process, costly application fee, and compressed-operating counter hours. However, the findings revealed that the challenges were not directly linked to the hala

story: Why is it hard for small cosmetics makers in Brunei to get halal certified? This 2025 study by Aiman Samhani Abdul Halim and Zeiad Amjad Aghwan interviewed eight of them. The problems were awkward application requirements, a slow approval process, high fees and short counter opening hours, and not the halal standards themselves.

title: Javanese and Islamic Syncretism in the Meaning of the Singo Mengkok Batik Motif by Sunan Drajat, Lamongan
summary: The Singo Mengkok batik motif from the time of Sunan Drajat's missionary work in Lamongan is a cultural artifact resulting from sophisticated syncretism, combining Javanese-Hindu symbolism (Padma Flower/Tunjung), Chinese (Qilin/Kirin), and Islamic values. Using Clifford Geertz's symbolic interpretation approach, this study reveals that this motif functions as a complex symbol system. At the cognitive/mythical level, the shape of the squatting lion transforms the concept of physical strength into a spiritual one, reflecting the subjugation of desires, in line with Surah Al-Qasas: 50. creator: Kartika Herlina Candraning Shiam

story: Singo Mengkok is a batik pattern from Lamongan, Indonesia, linked to Sunan Drajat's missionary work. It mixes Javanese-Hindu symbols like the lotus, the Chinese qilin, and Islamic values. This 2025 study by Kartika Herlina Candraning Shiam reads its squatting lion as turning physical strength into spiritual strength, the control of desire, and its small filler patterns as a kind of picture lesson in faith.

summary: The limited understanding of prospective umrah pilgrims, particularly in Batu City, serves as the background of this community service activity. The understanding of prospective pilgrims should not only focus on technical aspects but also encompass deeper spiritual dimensions. Based on preliminary observations in Batu City, some participants were still primarily focused on procedural aspects without fully comprehending the spiritual meaning of the worship. Therefore, this activity aims to enhance participants’ understanding, improve the quality of worship, and strengthen spiritual awareness through educational mentoring in umrah rituals. creator: Eko Setiawan, Humaidi KH

story: Going on Umrah is more than knowing which steps to take. In Batu City, Indonesia, some would-be pilgrims focused only on the procedures. This 2026 community project by Eko Setiawan and Humaidi KH ran mentoring sessions to help them understand the spiritual meaning of the rituals too.

title: Islamic Higher Education Role on Teacher Competence and Students' Learning Difficulties in Islamic School
summary: Education is an inseparable integration regarding level and resources in higher education. This study aims to analyse the role of Islamic higher education in improving teacher competence and student learning difficulties. This research uses a qualitative method with a literature study approach. Research shows that Islamic higher education’s role is to build education, especially human resources, by developing and improving teacher competence to help students with learning difficulties. Islamic higher education is more attention to problem-solving in madrasah through seminars, training, research and educational evaluation. source_name: JIE (Journal of Islamic Education)

story: How can Islamic universities help children who struggle at school? This 2023 study by Muhamad Fauzi, Nursalim Nursalim and Arif Fadilah argues they do it by training better teachers, through seminars, training, research and evaluation aimed at the problems madrasas actually face.

title: The Relationship between Management Information Systems Based on Rapor Digital Madrasah (RDM) and the Quality of Madrasah Education

title: Islamic Music In Banyuwangi: Artists’adaptation After The 1965 Political Violence
summary: This study examines the adaptation strategies of Banyuwangi artists in musical practices after the 1965 political violence. The stigma attached to the song Genjer-genjer and its allegedly association with the Indonesian Communist Party (PKI) affected the local art scene. The research applies the historical method through heuristics, source criticism, interpretation, and historiography. The findings revealed that Banyuwangi musicians shifted their repertoire from social themes to Islamic genres. This transformation constructed a socio-religious identity that protected them from political accusations and sustained local musical traditions. story: After the political violence of 1965 in Indonesia, a song called "Genjer-genjer" was stigmatised for its alleged link to the Communist Party, and that hit the music scene in Banyuwangi hard. This 2025 study by Hervina Nurullita found local musicians switched from social songs to Islamic music. That gave them a religious identity that shielded them from political accusations, and kept their local traditions alive.

title: Epistemology of Islamic Education: Criticism and Alternative Solutions
summary: The purpose of this study is to critique the epistemology of Islamic education in the 21st century, analyze existing problems, and propose alternative solutions. This research employs a qualitative approach, using descriptive analysis methods and a literature review to explore various discussions on the epistemology of Islamic education. Data is validated through source triangulation and then analyzed through collection, presentation, and conclusion drawing. The findings indicate that, despite rapid advancements in education due to technology and globalization, there remain unresolved issues. story: Epistemology is the study of how we know what we know. This 2023 study by Hellen Tiara and Danu criticises how Islamic education thinks about knowledge in the 21st century. Despite fast change from technology and globalisation, it argues, problems remain, and it proposes alternative solutions.

title: Religiosity and fashion store patronage intention among Muslim consumers

Data were collected using a structured questionnaire administered to 300 customers of Muslim fashion retail stores in Yogyakarta.Findings – The results demonstrate that religiosity positively and significantly influences perceived value, customer satisfaction, and patronage intention. story: Does being more religious make you more loyal to a shop? This 2026 study by Fikri Farhan, Edvin Perdana Yulianto and Banin Nuril Aulia surveyed 300 customers of Muslim fashion stores in Yogyakarta, Indonesia. It found religiosity raised how much customers valued the store, how satisfied they were, and whether they meant to come back.

summary: This research aims to analyze the integration of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in Islamic teaching materials in higher education. The research method used is a case study design. Data were collected through observations, interviews, and documentation studies of existing Islamic teaching materials. The data analysis process was carried out through data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing using FGD (Focus Group Discussion) technique. The results showed that the Islamic Religion course integrated various dimensions of the SDGs in the teaching materials. This 2025 study by Ega Nasrudin, Saepul Anwar and Edi Suresman checked how a university Islamic Religion course in Indonesia includes them. Social inclusion turned out to be the strongest theme, appearing in every chapter.

title: Promoting Green Madrasa as Environmental Education Program: How to Implement and Maintain It
summary: Global attention is currently focused on environmental issues, particularly Indonesia's environmental degradation, and one way to increase environmental literacy is through education, such as through the green school program. This study aims to describe the implementation of green schools in madrasas in West Lampung Regency, Lampung Province. This study utilizes a qualitative method. Data collection tools use interviews, observation and documentation. Analysis steps include data reduction, data display and conclusion drawing. story: Indonesia faces serious environmental damage, and one answer is teaching children about it. This 2025 study by Junaidah, Nikita Putri Mahardika and Muhammad Anas Ma'arif looks at "green madrasas" in West Lampung, Indonesia: Islamic schools running environmental programmes, and how they set them up and keep them going.

title: Women's Leadership in Islamic Boarding Schools: A Case Study at Darus Salam Islamic Boarding School Mandigu Hamlet Suco Village Mumbulsari District Jember Regency
summary: The discourse on women's leadership is still very doubtful in the lives of the people of Mandigu Hamlet, Suco Village, Mumbulsari District, Jember Regency. This can be concluded from the public response that is still very strong toward patriarchal culture and the lack of education. This study has two research focuses, first, what is the mindset of the community towards women's leadership in Darus Salam Islamic Boarding School? Second, is the decline in the number of students related to women's leadership at the Darus Salam Islamic Boarding School? This 2022 study by Muhammad Arif Mustaqim, Heidiah Waskito Rini and Imron Sadewo looks at women's leadership at Darus Salam Islamic Boarding School. It asks what the community thinks, and whether a drop in student numbers is linked to it.

title: Cost-Free Policy and the Pursuit of Quality Education: An Exploratory Study in Islamic Secondary Education
summary: This study explores the implementation of cost-free education policies in Islamic secondary schools, with a focus on how such policies contribute to the pursuit of quality education. Rooted in the national initiative to improve educational access and equity, the research specifically examines the management of School Operational Assistance (Bantuan Operasional Sekolah/ BOS) funds in a religious education setting. Using a qualitative exploratory design, data were gathered through observations, in-depth interviews, and document analysis. story: In Indonesia, a government fund called BOS helps schools run without charging fees. This 2025 study by Muhtadin looked at how Islamic secondary schools use it, and found planning that involved many people, careful spending and digital transparency, with school leadership making the difference to quality.

title: Effects of the Madrasah Research Program and Flipped Classroom on Students’ Digital Literacy in an Indonesian Madrasah
summary: Fostering students’ digital literacy is essential for preparing them with 21st-century skills in the digital era. This study aims to examine the effect of the Research Madrasah Program and the Flipped Classroom learning model on students’ digital literacy skills at MAN 1 Gresik. A quantitative, causal-comparative design was employed involving 60 students selected through purposive sampling. title: Analysis of Food and Beverage MSMEs' Readiness in Fulfilling Halal Certification to Improve Business Competitiveness
summary: This study aims to analyze the readiness and constraints of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in the food and beverage sector in Serang City in fulfilling halal certification requirements and to examine the role of technical assistance in supporting the certification process. A descriptive qualitative approach with a case study method was employed. Data were collected from 60 food and beverage MSMEs through questionnaires, interviews, observations, and supporting documentation. This 2026 study by Elis Badariah, Mela Sandra and Ahmad Solihin looks at what held the others back and how technical help made a difference.

title: Islamic Religious Education and Muslim Youth Identity on Social Media: A Critical Discourse Analysis of Instagram and TikTok Content in Indonesia
summary: The rapid growth of digital technology has led to the proliferation of social media platforms, significantly influencing various aspects of life, including the formation of religious identity among Muslim adolescents. This study examines the role of Islamic education in shaping Muslim identity in the digital era through critical discourse analysis. Using a qualitative approach, data were collected from social media content related to Islamic education and identity formation. summary: [English]: The rapid expansion of halal tourism in Lombok requires Islamic higher education to prepare graduates with competencies beyond religious knowledge, including professional, digital, interpersonal, and cultural capabilities. This 2026 study by Hendri Hermawan Adinugraha, Muhammad Khoirul Fikri and Rizky Andrean looked at three Islamic universities there and how they are changing their courses to give graduates professional, digital, people and cultural skills, not just religious knowledge.

title: Policy Analysis and Characteristics of the Independent Curriculum in Madrasah Aliyah
summary: The implementation of the Independent Curriculum in Madrasah Aliyah presents opportunities to improve the relevance and quality of Islamic education through greater flexibility, contextual learning, and student-centered approaches. However, its implementation still faces challenges related to teacher competence, unequal access to technology, limited learning resources, assessment practices, and institutional readiness. This study aims to examine the characteristics, implementation practices, and main challenges of the Independent Curriculum in Madrasah Aliyah. title: New Public Management in The Changing Status of Higher Education Institution in Indonesia
summary: Global competition among universities in the world has become more challenging over years. Meanwhile, New Public Management approach which was initially introduced in 1990s has been proposing administrative reforms on the old inefficient bureaucracy. story: Universities worldwide now compete like companies. This 2021 study looks at how Indonesia changed the legal status of its universities using New Public Management, an approach that runs public institutions more like businesses, to keep up.

title: Ecological Justice in Islamic Family Law: Integrating Maqasid al-Shari'ah with Environmental Ethics in Post-Pandemic Societies
summary: This study addresses a critical gap in Islamic legal discourse: the marginalization of ecological justice (ʻadālat al-bīʻah) within Islamic family law, despite the family’s central role in shaping consumption, education, and environmental ethics. The post-pandemic era has intensified this urgency, as lockdowns revealed both heightened household waste and increased dependence on local ecosystems, prompting a reevaluation of domestic responsibility under sharī‘ah. Drawing on Jasser Auda’s maqāṣid al-sharīʻah, Robert D. title: Fashion, Sustainability, and Tourism: How Soerakarta Walking Tour Engages Muslim Community in Green Tourism
summary: The Soerakarta Walking Tour (SWT) is an innovative urban tourism initiative that integrates cultural preservation, environmental sustainability, and inclusivity. This study examines how SWT's promotes green tourism through a mixed-methods approach, combining quantitative surveys and qualitative interviews with participants. The quantitative findings reveal high levels of participant satisfaction, including understanding green tourism principles and satisfaction with cultural storytelling. summary: The Muslim fashion industry is one of the creative sectors with rapid growth in the ASEAN region, along with the increase of the Muslim middle class, internet penetration, and halal lifestyle trends. Digital transformation through e-commerce is a key catalyst that allows local brands to expand their market reach to the regional level. However, this dynamic also presents challenges in the form of cross-border regulations, logistical barriers, low digital literacy, and global competition. summary: The need for cosmetics with various types and innovation and quality in providing functions for consumers, requires the cosmetics industry to continue to develop technology both in terms of innovation and product variety and must also increase ease and practicality in use. The aim of this research is to determine the influence of product innovation, product quality and halal labels on consumer credibility in competition in the halal cosmetic product industry (case study of the people of Malang City). summary: The digitalization of zakat management in Indonesia has grown rapidly alongside the increasing use of Islamic financial technology and internet access. However, Law Number 23 of 2011 as the main legal foundation has not explicitly regulated digital zakat mechanisms. This creates a gap between rapidly evolving digital practices and relatively static regulations. This study aims to analyze digital zakat management from the perspective of the law, as well as to identify areas of compliance and limitations. summary: This study explores the perceptions of medical students regarding the role of podcasts and YouTube in enhancing their understanding of medical knowledge, while also examining the factors influencing their usage and reviewing these media from an Islamic perspective. summary: The integrative Islamic education paradigm is increasingly important for Islamic higher education as institutions seek to preserve Islamic identity while responding to academic rationality, contextual learning, and digital transformation. title: Innovation Product and Halal Labelization in Buying Repurchase
summary: Indonesia is a developing country which has many Small and Medium Firms (SMEs). It has a vital role in development and economic growth. The purpose of this research is to know and analyze the effect of product innovation and halal labelling in buying Repurchase. The method used in this study is descriptive analysis method by describing the data. It has been collected without intending to make conclusions to the public or generalization. Data analysis used is Multiple Linear by using SPSS software. The results showed that product innovation and halal labeling simultaneously had a positive and significant effect on buying repurchase. creator: Bunga Aditi
source_name: International Research Journal of Business Studies
locator: DOI=10.21632/irjbs.12.1.87-100; journal="International Research Journal of Business Studies"
scope_basis: Crossref search "halal innovation"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Why do shoppers come back for more? This 2019 study by Bunga Aditi looked at small businesses in Indonesia and found that both product innovation and a halal label had a clear positive effect on whether customers bought again.

title: Uji Akurasi Arah Kiblat Masjid dan Makam di Kecamatan Bontotiro Kabupaten Bulukumba
summary: Penelitian ini membahas tentang penentuan arah kiblat masjid dan makam di Kecamatan Bontotiro Kabupaten Bulukumba dan hasil uji akurasi arah kiblat masjid dan makam di Kecamatan Bontotiro Kabupaten Bulukumba. Tujuan dalam penelitian ini adalah untuk memperoleh informasi terkait bagaimana tingkat pengetahuan dan pemahaman masyarakat tentang arah kiblat masjid dan makam serta menerapkan metode falak dalam menentukan arah kiblat masjid dan makam di Kecamatan Bontotiro Kabupaten Bulukumba hingga dapat memberikan pemahaman yang lebih jelas mengenai pentingnya penentuan arah kiblat masjid dan makam di kecamatan Bontotiro Kabupaten Bulukumba. creator: Sulastri, Supardin, Intan Cahyani
source_name: HISABUNA: Jurnal Ilmu Falak
scope_basis: Crossref search "falak astronomy"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Are the mosques and graves in Bontotiro, a district of Bulukumba in Indonesia, really facing the Qibla, the direction of Mecca? This 2024 field study by Sulastri, Supardin and Intan Cahyani tested them with the methods of falak, Islamic astronomy, and asked how much local people know about getting the direction right.

title: Eco-Pesantren and Islamic Environmental Education: A Phenomenological Study in Boarding Culture
summary: Purpose – This study investigates why formal eco-pesantren cleanliness regulations at MAN 2 Yogyakarta have not consistently translated into students’ everyday ecological behaviour. While Islamic environmental education has institutionalized cleanliness policies, a gap persists between normative rules and lived practice. This research addresses that gap by examining how boarding culture shapes, mediates, and is experienced in students’ cleanliness practices and ecological awareness. The principal argument advanced is that ecological behaviour in Islamic boarding schools is not solely regulation-driven but is constructed through layered meaning-making within micro-level room culture. Design/m
creator: Salsabila Nur Imatul Adzillah, Dwi Ratnasari, Taufan Jannata
source_name: Indonesian Journal of Action Research
locator: DOI=10.14421/ijar.2025.42-07; journal="Indonesian Journal of Action Research"
scope_basis: Crossref search "eco pesantren"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: MAN 2 Yogyakarta has strict cleanliness rules for its boarding students, but students don't always follow them. This 2025 study by Salsabila Nur Imatul Adzillah, Dwi Ratnasari and Taufan Jannata asks why. It argues that green habits at boarding schools come less from rules and more from the culture inside each dorm room.

title: Measuring Sharia Bank Performance by Syari'ate Value Added Approach: Sharia Enter-prise Implementation in Sharia Banking in Indonesia
summary: This study aims to measure the financial performance of Islamic banking in Indonesia using Shariâ€™ate Value Added Approach. This research also analyzes whether there are significant differences of financial performance of Islamic banking using the income statement approach and shariâ€™ate value added approach. The sample of this study is islamic banking, with research period 2010-2015, selected using a purposive sampling. Financial performance used in this study is Return on Asset (ROA), Return on Equity (ROE), Net Profit to Productive Asset (NPPA), and Net Profit Margin (NPM). They were analyzed using independent sample t test. The result shows that financial performance of Islamic banking
creator: Sri Wahyuni, Pujiharto Pujiharto
source_name: Journal of Economics, Business, & Accountancy Ventura
locator: DOI=10.14414/jebav.v20i3.769; journal="Journal of Economics, Business, & Accountancy Ventura"
scope_basis: Crossref search "sharia banking"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: How do you judge whether an Islamic bank is doing well? This 2018 study by Sri Wahyuni and Pujiharto Pujiharto measured Indonesian Islamic banks from 2010 to 2015 in two ways: the normal income statement, and a "Shari'ate Value Added" approach, and checked whether the two give different answers on measures like return on assets.

title: Permissioned Blockchain and Smart Contracts for Halal Supply Chain Traceability in Indonesia
summary: Assurance of halal integrity along the supply chain carries major economic and religious weight in Indonesia, yet conventional traceability relies on centralized databases and paper certificates that are difficult to verify, easy to tamper with, and fragmented across the many actors between farm and consumer. This study designs and evaluates HalalChain, a permissioned-blockchain and smart-contract traceability framework that records each custody transfer on a shared, tamper-evident ledger and encodes halal certification rules as executable logic. Using a design science methodology, supply-chain actors participate as permissioned nodes on Hyperledger Fabric, bulky documents are stored off cha
creator: Rafi Farizki, Rani Santika, Vo Hung Cuong
source_name: Jurnal Indonesia Sosial Teknologi
scope_basis: Crossref search "halal blockchain"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Halal checks often depend on paper certificates that are hard to verify and easy to fake. This 2026 study by Rafi Farizki, Rani Santika and Vo Hung Cuong designs HalalChain, a system where every handover from farm to shop is recorded on a shared blockchain ledger that shows any tampering, and halal rules run automatically as code.

title: Digitalisasi Pengelolaan Zakat, Efisiensi dan Kepatuhan Muzaki di Indonesia
summary: Penelitian ini membahas persoalan ketidaksesuaian antara pesatnya digitalisasi pengelolaan zakat dan belum optimalnya efisiensi lembaga serta kepatuhan muzaki di Indonesia. Setiap sesuatu pasti mempunyai tujuan yang hendak dicapai, begitu pula penelitian ini. Tujuan dari penelitian adalah mendeskripsikan perkembangan digitalisasi zakat, menganalisis pengaruhnya terhadap efisiensi operasional dan kepatuhan muzaki, serta mengidentifikasi faktor pendukung dan penghambat implementasinya. Metode yang digunakan adalah penelitian kepustakaan dengan mengkaji literatur, buku, jurnal, laporan, dan penelitian relevan sebagai sumber data primer dan sekunder. Hasil menunjukkan bahwa digitalisasi memberi
creator: A. Fahrur Rozi, Ana Nurwakhidah, Irfan Faroqi
source_name: Jihbiz : Jurnal Ekonomi, Keuangan dan Perbankan Syariah
locator: DOI=10.33379/jihbiz.v10i1.8754; journal="Jihbiz : Jurnal Ekonomi, Keuangan dan Perbankan Syariah"
scope_basis: Crossref search "zakat management"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Zakat collection in Indonesia is going digital fast, but organisations have not become as efficient as hoped, and not everyone pays. This 2026 review by A. Fahrur Rozi, Ana Nurwakhidah and Irfan Faroqi looks at how digitalisation affects efficiency and the compliance of muzaki, the people who owe zakat, and what helps or holds it back.

title: Shaping Ethical Digital Citizens through Islamic Education
summary: General Background: Education in Indonesia faces complex challenges related to concepts, regulations, and implementation across various educational systems. A critical issue is the development of student character, particularly in the digital era where graduates struggle to remain competitive globally. Specific Background: Islamic education plays a vital role in shaping students' characters, imparting religious values, ethics, and morality. In the digital era, this education extends beyond traditional religious teaching to address ethical and moral use of technology. Knowledge Gap: Despite significant research on Islamic education, little attention has been given to its role in teaching digi
creator: Bayu Ady Pranoto, Budi Haryanto
source_name: Indonesian Journal of Islamic Studies
locator: DOI=10.21070/ijis.v12i4.1740; journal="Indonesian Journal of Islamic Studies"
scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic app digital technology"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Students today live online. This 2024 study by Bayu Ady Pranoto and Budi Haryanto argues Islamic education in Indonesia can do more than teach religion: it can teach students to use technology ethically and morally, a role it says research has largely ignored.

title: Differences in Halal Food Knowledge among Business Actors by Providing Digital Flipbook and E-booklet Media Education
summary: The current halal lifestyle is not only limited to Muslims, but many non-Muslim countries have also started implementing halal food products. This research aims to determine the effect of providing education using visual media on halal food knowledge for Surabaya culinary center businesses. This type of research is True Experimental using a pre-post test design. The sample in the research consisted of 40 respondents. The samples taken in this study used total sampling, then divided into 2 groups (digital Flipbook education group and Ebooklet group). The test analysis used was Mann Whitney okewith a significance level (α=0.05). The research results showed that there were differences in the kn
creator: Khikmah Widianti, Endah Budi Permana Putri
source_name: Journal of Halal Research, Policy, and Industry
locator: DOI=10.33086/jhrpi.v2i2.5457; journal="Journal of Halal Research, Policy, and Industry"
scope_basis: Crossref search "halal industry business"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Is a digital flipbook or an e-booklet better for teaching food sellers about halal food? This 2023 experiment by Khikmah Widianti and Endah Budi Permana Putri split 40 businesses at a Surabaya food centre into two groups, one for each, and tested what they knew before and after. The two groups ended up with different results.

title: Forensic Psychological Evidence in Ḥaḍānah Disputes: A Content Analysis of Fifty Indonesian Religious Court Decisions
summary: This study analyzes how forensic psychological evidence is used in child custody (ḥaḍānah) decisions of Indonesian Religious Courts. Prior research suggests judicial inconsistency in accommodating psychological evidence, but no systematic mapping of the pattern exists. This study employs quantitative content analysis of 50 Religious Court and Sharia Court decisions issued between 2015 and 2026, retrieved from the Supreme Court Decision Directory and coded for party characteristics, outcomes, the presence and judicial treatment of psychological evidence, and the ratio decidendi. The findings show that custody was awarded to mothers in 58% of cases, consistent with Article 105 of the Compilati
creator: Fathul Lubabin Nuqul
source_name: Sakina: Journal of Family Studies
locator: DOI=10.18860/jfs.v10i3.25303; journal="Sakina: Journal of Family Studies"
scope_basis: Crossref search "religious court"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: When parents in Indonesia fight over custody in a religious court, does psychology count? This 2026 study by Fathul Lubabin Nuqul analysed 50 decisions from 2015 to 2026. Mothers got custody in 58% of cases, in line with Indonesian Islamic law, and the study maps how judges treated psychological evidence, which earlier research found inconsistent.

title: Instagram Content Engagement in Islamic Philanthropy: Evidence from BAZNAS Indonesia
summary: This study examines how Instagram content characteristics shape audience engagement in Islamic philanthropy, using BAZNAS Indonesia as a case. A quantitative content analysis was conducted on 544 organic posts published by @baznasindonesia from January to May 2025. Post type, publication timing, message interactivity, and post appeal were manually coded, and Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) models were estimated for log-transformed likes and comments. Entertainment appeal significantly increased likes (β = 1.451, p = 0.015) and comments (β = 2.176, p = 0.002).
