creator: Nadia Nurfitria
source_name: Digital Muslim Review
scope_basis: Crossref search "media representation muslims"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Cancel culture, where online crowds turn on a person, plays out among Indonesian Muslims too. This 2025 study by Nadia Nurfitria tracked cases including those of Ahok and Tuan Guru Mizan using trending topics on X and Google Trends, and found it deepens splits between conservative, moderate and liberal Muslims, and feeds stereotypes of Islam as intolerant.

title: The Integration of Islamic Religious Education (PAI) and Islamic Humanistic Ecology
summary: The purpose of this study is to formulate the integration of Islamic humanistic ecology principles in religious education as a moral and spiritual foundation for environmental preservation. The method used is a qualitative approach through library research, where data is collected from literature and analyzed descriptively using thematic and conceptual approaches. The results show that integrating Islamic humanistic ecological values into Islamic Education forms the foundation for building students' character, faith, and ecological responsibility. scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic ecology"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Can religion lessons help protect the environment? This 2026 study by Norjamilah Norjamilah, Hamdanah Hamdanah and Normuslim Normuslim argues that Islamic principles like tawhid, amanah (trust), balance, justice and ihsan (excellence) can teach students their role as khalifah, caretakers of the earth.

title: Perlindungan Hukum Bagi Calon Jemaah Umrah Pasca Pencabutan Izin Penyelenggara Perjalanan Ibadah Umrah (PPIU)
summary: This study examines the forms of legal protection and legal remedies available to prospective Umrah pilgrims following the revocation of licenses of Umrah Travel Organizers (PPIU) by the Ministry of Religious Affairs. The problem arises from the growing number of cases where pilgrims had fully paid for Umrah services but were not departed, such as in the case of PT. Naila Syafaah Wisata Mandiri. The license revocation has caused legal uncertainty, a lack of accountability, and financial harm to affected pilgrims. This research highlights the urgency of providing effective legal protection for prospective pilgrims who are placed in a vulnerable position due to the failure of the organizers to
creator: Aini Widya Utami, Putri Eka Ramadhani Batubara
source_name: JURNAL USM LAW REVIEW
scope_basis: Crossref search "umrah travel"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Imagine paying in full for a pilgrimage and never leaving home. That happened to customers of PT Naila Syafaah Wisata Mandiri and other Umrah firms whose licences Indonesia's Ministry of Religious Affairs took away. This 2025 study by Aini Widya Utami and Putri Eka Ramadhani Batubara looks at how the law can protect those pilgrims.

title: Pengaruh Metode Continuous Running Terhadap Peningktan Daya Tahan Siswa Ekstrakurikuler Pencak Silat di Pondok Pesantren Modern Nurussalam
summary: Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh kurangnya daya tahan siswa ekstrakurikuler pencak silat di Pondok Pesantren Modern Nurussalam. Jenis penelitian ini merupakan penelitian kuantitatif yaitu untuk mengetahui pengaruh metode Continuous Running Terhadap penngkatan daya tahan siswa ekstrakurikuler pencak silat di Pondok Pesantren Modern Nurussalam. Metode yang digunakan dalam penelitian ini adalah eksperimen. Desain penelitian pretest post. Subjek penelitian adalah siswa ekstrakurikuler pencak silat di Pondok Pesantren Modern Nurussalam yang berjumlah 14 peserta. Dalam penelitian ini terdapat 2 variabel. Yaitu, Variabel bebas : Metode Continuous Running, dan variabel terikat : Daya tahan peser
creator: Muhammad Fajriyudin, Rizki Aminudin, Fahrudin Fahrudin
source_name: Jurnal Literasi Olahraga
scope_basis: Crossref search "martial art pencak silat"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Students in the pencak silat club at Nurussalam Modern Islamic Boarding School were tiring too fast. This 2021 experiment by Muhammad Fajriyudin, Rizki Aminudin and Fahrudin Fahrudin had 14 of them do continuous running, and tested whether their endurance improved.

title: Semiotika Batik Motif Weton Indonesia karya Omah Kreatif Dongaji dengan Pendekatan Charles S.Peirce
summary: Tujuan penelitian ini adalah untuk mendeskripsikan semiotika batik Weton Indonesia karya Omah Kreatif Dongaji berdasarkan pendekatan Charles S. Peirce. Jenis penelitian ini adalah dekriptif kualitatif dan pengambilan sampel dilakukan secara purposive dan snowball. Teknik pengumpulan dengan triangulasi (gabungan). Teknik analisis data yang digunakan adalah teknik analisis deskriptif kualitatif dengan menggunakan pendekatan analisis menurut teori Pierce. Motif-motif batik Weton memiliki makna masing masing dalam penggambarannya yang menampilkan motif batik Weton Indonesia, hal itu merupakan bentuk bahasa yang divisualkan. Hasil penelitian mengungkapkan bahwa penciptaan motif batik Weton oleh R
creator: Muhajirin Muhajirin, Alifia Zahra Khoirunisa
source_name: Sungging
scope_basis: Crossref search "batik islamic motif"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Omah Kreatif Dongaji makes a batik design called Weton Indonesia. This 2022 study by Muhajirin Muhajirin and Alifia Zahra Khoirunisa reads its patterns through the semiotics of Charles S. Peirce, the study of signs, and finds each motif has its own meaning, a kind of language made visible.

title: Model Pemetaan Destinasi Wisata Syariah di Jawa Timur Berbasis Teknologi Blockchain: Pendekatan Smart Halal Tourism Ecosystem
summary: The development of halal tourism in East Java has shown significant potential, reflected in the growth of religious destinations, Islamic cultural attractions, and a rapidly expanding halal industry. However, the current halal tourism ecosystem faces challenges related to fragmented destination data, limited integration of halal certification, and low transparency of information for visitors. This study aims to formulate a blockchain-based mapping model for halal tourism destinations, designed as a foundation for a Smart Halal Tourism Ecosystem. A mixed-methods approach was applied through ecosystem needs assessment, digital readiness surveys of industry actors, and expert interviews with ha
creator: Amran Suradi, Siti Musfiqoh
source_name: Journal of Industrial and Syariah Economics
locator: DOI=10.63321/jise.v3i2.137; journal="Journal of Industrial and Syariah Economics"
scope_basis: Crossref search "halal blockchain"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: East Java has many religious and Islamic cultural sites, but information about them is scattered, and halal certification is not well linked up. This 2026 study by Amran Suradi and Siti Musfiqoh designs a blockchain-based map of halal tourism destinations, as the base for a "smart halal tourism ecosystem".

title: Assistance for Micro Entrepreneurs to Obtain Halal Certification from SEHATI 2022
summary: Purpose: This research examines the challenges faced by MSMEs in Indonesia when obtaining halal certification through the SEHATI 2022 program. It focuses on obstacles like the complexity of procedures and lack of awareness about the program and SIHALAL system, impacting micro-businesses' ability to secure halal certification.Method: The study uses qualitative methods, including interviews with halal facilitators and MSMEs, and document analysis related to the SEHATI 2022 program. creator: Irma Hidayati
source_name: Jurnal Pengabdian Masyarakat
scope_basis: Crossref search "halal certification food"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: SEHATI 2022 was an Indonesian programme to help micro businesses get halal certification. This 2024 study by Irma Hidayati interviewed facilitators and business owners and found the main obstacles were complicated procedures and not knowing enough about the programme or SIHALAL, the online system used to apply.

title: Sufi Tradition as Legitimization of Guardianship in The Java: The Study of Manuscripts of Babad Demak Pesisiran
summary: The development of Islam in Java is inseparable from the role of wali as a preacher of Islam. The title of wali is given to selected people who get privileges such karamah and knowledge about Islam. This research aims to analyze sufi tradition carried out by Java sufi until they reach the degree of wali. This research uses a qualitative method with descriptive analysis. The research source used is Babad Demak Pesisiran, which was transliterated by the Indonesian Education and Culture Ministry in 1984. The result of this research is about sufi tradition carried out by wali, such as fasting to curb the lust (tan dhahar rikala rina), praying all night long to get closer to God (tan sare rikala
creator: Shofwatul Qolbiyah
source_name: Journal of Islamic History and Manuscript
locator: DOI=10.24090/jihm.v3i1.10732; journal="Journal of Islamic History and Manuscript"
scope_basis: Crossref search "sufi literature manuscript"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Islam spread in Java partly through wali, holy men believed to have special blessings and knowledge. How did someone become a wali? This 2024 study by Shofwatul Qolbiyah reads the Babad Demak Pesisiran, a Javanese chronicle transliterated by Indonesia's education ministry in 1984. It describes their practices, like fasting by day to tame desire and praying through the night to get closer to God.

title: Impact of Ramadan Fasting on Health Parameters among Elementary School Teachers in Medan
summary: Ramadan fasting, a globally significant religious practice, involves abstaining from food and drink from dawn to sunset for 29 to 30 days. While previous studies have linked fasting to various health outcomes, the results remain inconsistent. This study examines the effects of Ramadan fasting on several health indicators among elementary school teachers in Medan, focusing on body weight, glucose levels, uric acid levels, cholesterol levels, and blood pressure. Using a prospective cohort design, the study involved teachers from diverse backgrounds at Perguruan Islam Cendekia in Medan, North Sumatra. Baseline health measurements were recorded before Ramadan, with follow-up assessments conducte
creator: Siti Nurbaya, Yusra Yusra, Supri Irianti Handayani
source_name: eJournal Kedokteran Indonesia
scope_basis: Crossref search "ramadan fasting health"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: What does a month of Ramadan fasting do to your body? This 2025 study by Siti Nurbaya, Yusra Yusra and Supri Irianti Handayani measured primary school teachers at Perguruan Islam Cendekia in Medan, Indonesia, before and after Ramadan, checking weight, blood sugar, uric acid, cholesterol and blood pressure.

title: Implementation of Progressive Law in Sharia Banking Dispute Settlement: Case Study of Religious Court Decisions in Indonesia
summary: This research aims to analyze the extent to which judges have applied progressive legal paradigm in deciding Sharia banking disputes and the extent to which the decisions have fulfilled the principles of legal certainty, justice, and value. This normative legal research uses statutory and case study approaches by analyzing Sharia banking dispute decisions obtained from the website of the Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia. This research found that decisions based on textual legal interpretations tend to less implement progressive law, lacking of accommodating people's sense of justice as they put more emphasis on legal certainty. creator: Nur Hidayah, Abdul Azis
source_name: Ulumuna
scope_basis: Crossref search "religious court"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: When a customer and an Islamic bank go to court in Indonesia, how do judges decide? This 2023 study by Nur Hidayah and Abdul Azis found judges who read the law word for word focus on legal certainty and less on what feels fair, while judges who read it in context are more "progressive", giving more weight to people's sense of justice.

title: Impact of Marketing Mix and Brand Religiosity Aura on Consumer Purchase Decisions: A Study of Rabbani Muslim Fashion
summary: Muslim fashion has emerged as a significant segment within the global halal economy, yet empirical studies examining the interplay between conventional marketing strategies and religion-based brand identity in driving consumer purchase behavior remain limited. This study investigates the influence of the marketing mix comprising product, price, place, and promotion alongside brand religiosity aura on consumer purchase decisions within the context of Rabbani, an established Indonesian Muslim fashion brand. Employing a quantitative cross-sectional design, data were collected from 100 purposively selected consumers with prior purchasing experience of Rabbani products. The findings reveal that a
creator: Reny Fitriana Kaban, Prameswara Samofa Nadya, Maulana Ilham Akbar
source_name: Journal of Business, Finance, and Banking
locator: DOI=10.56174/jbfb.v2i2.1328; journal="Journal of Business, Finance, and Banking"
scope_basis: Crossref search "muslim fashion"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Rabbani is a well-known Indonesian Muslim fashion brand. This 2026 study by Reny Fitriana Kaban, Prameswara Samofa Nadya and Maulana Ilham Akbar asked 100 of its customers what made them buy: the usual product, price, place and promotion, or the brand's "religiosity aura", its religious image.

title: Green Islamic Education: Integrating Environmental Ethics into Islamic Religious Education for Sustainable Development
summary: This study aims to develop a conceptual framework of Green Islamic Education by integrating Islamic environmental ethics into Islamic Religious Education (IRE) to strengthen environmental responsibility and support sustainable development. The study employs a qualitative library research method through conceptual analysis and synthesis of relevant literature on Islamic environmental ethics, Islamic education, environmental education, Education for Sustainable Development (ESD), and ecological pedagogy. The findings demonstrate that Islamic education can foster environmental responsibility through the principles of tawhid, khalifah, amanah, mizan, maslahah, and the prohibition of environmenta
creator: Mahmoud Abdullah, Huzaiman Hushin, Salma Begum
source_name: Ar-rayyan: Journal Of Islamic Education
locator: DOI=10.67899/ar.v2i2.222; journal="Ar-rayyan: Journal Of Islamic Education"
scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic environmental ethics"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: What would a "green" Islamic education look like? This 2025 paper by Mahmoud Abdullah, Huzaiman Hushin and Salma Begum builds a framework that ties religious lessons to the environment through Islamic principles like tawhid, khalifah (stewardship), amanah (trust), mizan (balance), maslahah (public good) and the ban on causing damage.

title: Analysis of Halal Literacy, Halal Awareness, Motivation and Religiousity of SMES on Interest in Halal Certification in Banjarmasin
summary: Micro, Small, and Medium-Sized Enterprises (MSMEs) play a significant role in Banjarmasin City's local economic development. Along with this growth, halal products have great potential to gain the support of consumers whose awareness of halal products is increasing. Halal factors are becoming increasingly important to consumers when making routine product purchases. This study examines how the motivation,religiosity, halal literacy, and halal awareness of MSME (Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises) actors affect their desire to get halal certification in Banjarmasin City. This study is conducted using field research using a quantitative descriptive technique. Purposive sampling, a non-probab
creator: Abdul Wahab Wahab, Iman Setya Budi, Afina Putri Fatimah Amanda
source_name: Journal of Islamic Economic Laws
locator: DOI=10.23917/jisel.v7i02.5071; journal="Journal of Islamic Economic Laws"
scope_basis: Crossref search "halal certification food"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Why do some small businesses in Banjarmasin, Indonesia, want halal certification and others don't? This 2024 study by Abdul Wahab Wahab, Iman Setya Budi and Afina Putri Fatimah Amanda looked at the owners' motivation, religiosity, halal knowledge and halal awareness.

scope_basis: Crossref search "halal certification food"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: How do different countries certify food as halal? This 2024 study compares Indonesia and Malaysia, where Muslims are the majority, with Mexico, where they are a minority, looking at each country's halal certification procedures.

title: Islamic Law and National Law (Comparative Study of Islamic Criminal Law and Indonesian Criminal Law)
summary: The Indonesian state, although the country is not an Islamic state, but in terms of Islamic legal values, both partially and completely, which are the substantive norms in various laws and regulations in Indonesia, such as the Marriage Law, Waqf Law, Hajj Law, Banking Law (both Law No. /1998 as well as Law 21/2008). The Islamic criminal law that has been implemented is in the Province of Aceh Darus Salam, which is only a small part. This study aims to determine the description of Islamic law, Islamic criminal law, and to determine the purpose of Islamic law and Indonesian criminal law. This study uses a qualitative method with a normative juridical approach. The results of the study i

source_name: Al Hurriyah : Jurnal Hukum Islam
locator: DOI=10.30983/alhurriyah.v6i2.4952; journal="Al Hurriyah : Jurnal Hukum Islam"
scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic law constitution"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Indonesia is not an Islamic state, yet Islamic values sit inside many of its laws on marriage, waqf, hajj and banking. This 2022 study compares Islamic criminal law with Indonesia's own criminal law.

title: The Value of Exemplary in the Film Teach Me Islam and Its Relevance to Islamic Religious Education Materials
summary: The objectives achieved in this research are: 1). To find out and describe what exemplary values ​​are contained in the film Ajari Aku Islam, 2). To find out and explain the relevance of exemplary values ​​in the film Ajari Aku Islam to Islamic religious education materials. The type of research used in this study is a qualitative research content analysis with research subjects showing a film with the title Ajari Aku Islam in the form of scenes containing exemplary values ​​and other sources related to the research objectives, while the analytical technique used is Barthes' semiotics model. . Based on the research that has been done, there are several research results, namely exemplary valu

locator: DOI=10.21070/ijemd.v20i.684; journal="Indonesian Journal of Education Methods Development"

story: Ajari Aku Islam, "Teach Me Islam", is an Indonesian film. This 2022 study by Dinis Tyas Ayu Karisma Putri and Budi Haryanto studied its scenes with Roland Barthes's method of reading signs, to find the role-model values it shows and how they fit Islamic religious education lessons.

title: AN ANALYSIS OF PRICE NEGOTIATION STRATEGIES WITH CUSTOMERS AT A FASHION, ACCESSORIES AND HIJAB STORE (A Study Of Tasya Collection)
summary: This research analysed the price negotiation strategies employed at Tasya Collection, a fashion businessspecializing in the sale of hijabs and women’s accessories. The negotiation process between sellers and buyersis the primary focus, as many customers have complained about prices being higher than those found in onlineshops, as well as a lack of flexibility in bargaining. This study employs a descriptive qualitative method, withdata collected through direct observation and the author’s four years of work experience at the shop. scope_basis: Crossref search "hijab fashion industry"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: At Tasya Collection, a shop selling hijabs and women's accessories, customers complained prices were higher than online and that there was little room to bargain. The most a customer could get off was Rp5,000, whatever they bought or however loyal they were. This 2026 study draws on the author's four years working in the shop.

title: Strategi Komunikasi dalam Penanaman Nilai-Nilai Pancasila melalui Kurikulum Qasidah di Pondok Pesantren
summary: Modernisasi, digitalisasi, dan globalisasi secara perlahan mengikis budaya serta moral bangsa Indonesia, termasuk memudarnya pemahaman generasi muda terhadap nilai-nilai Pancasila. Pesantren, dengan tradisi pendidikan yang kuat dan berakar pada nilai kebangsaan, berperan penting dalam menjaga serta menanamkan kembali nilai dasar negara tersebut. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis strategi komunikasi dalam penanaman nilai-nilai Pancasila melalui kurikulum Qasidah di Pondok Pesantren Salafiyah Kapurejo Pagu Kediri. Metode penelitian yang digunakan adalah kualitatif dengan pendekatan fenomenologi serta analisis teori konstruktivisme. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa implementasi nila

locator: DOI=10.31538/altsiq.v10i2.7417; journal="Al-Tsiqoh : Jurnal Ekonomi dan Dakwah Islam"
scope_basis: Crossref search "gambus qasidah music"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Pancasila holds the founding values of the Indonesian state. This 2025 study by Ellyda Retpitasari, Nailal Muna and Muhammad Faqih looks at how one Islamic boarding school, Salafiyah Kapurejo in Pagu, Kediri, passes on those values through its qasidah curriculum.

title: The Perspective of Millenial Tourists on Halal Tourism and its Reflection to Halal Tourism Development in West Sumatera
summary: Research article in Journal of Indonesia Tourism and Policy Studies, 2020.

locator: DOI=10.7454/jitps.v5i2.219; journal="Journal of Indonesia Tourism and Policy Studies"

story: Muslim travellers are more aware of halal products and services, and millennials have become the most targeted group. This 2020 study asked millennial tourists what they think of halal tourism and what that means for developing it in West Sumatra, Indonesia.

title: Back To Muslim Identity: Framing the Khilafah Ideology on Social Media
summary: The purposes of this discussion are: first, to explain how is the development of Back To Muslim Identity in online media. Second, to describe the pattern of movement carried out by Back To Muslim Identity. Third, knowing the strategy of the Back To Muslim Identity movement in Indonesia. This article uses a text qualitative research method, examines the bulletins, lectures and blogs shared in online media by the Back To Muslim Identity group. The data and data sources in this study were obtained from the online media Back To Muslim Identity, Facebook, Instagram, Youtube, Twitter. creator: Yayan Saputra, Sarwan, Sabiruddin

locator: DOI=10.70062/incoils.v2i1.77; journal="Proceeding International Conference on Islam, Law, and Society (INCOILS)"
scope_basis: Crossref search "social media muslim"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Back To Muslim Identity is a group that promotes the idea of a khilafah, a caliphate, online. This 2023 study by Yayan Saputra, Sarwan and Sabiruddin examined its bulletins, lectures and posts on Facebook, Instagram, YouTube and Twitter, to show how the movement grows and the strategies it uses in Indonesia.

title: A Comparative Analysis of Qibla Direction Accuracy Using a Theodolite, Mizwala, and Right-Angle Triangle at As-Sakinah Mosque, Surabaya
summary: The Qibla direction is a fundamental aspect of Muslim prayer, requiring precise determination. This study evaluates the accuracy of the Qibla direction at the As-Sakinah Mosque in Surabaya by comparing three instruments: a Theodolite, a Mizwala, and a Right Triangle (Segitiga Siku-siku). Employing field experimental methods, the measurement data were analyzed using a comparative descriptive approach. The findings reveal significant variations in accuracy among the instruments: the Theodolite and Mizwala detected deviations of 5° 56' 48.71" and 5° 35' 4.21" respectively, whereas the Right Triangle method showed a substantial deviation of 25°. creator: Safna Farah Dila
source_name: Astroislamica: Journal of Islamic Astronomy
locator: DOI=10.47766/astroislamica.v4i2.4796; journal="Astroislamica: Journal of Islamic Astronomy"
scope_basis: Crossref search "qibla determination"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Is the As-Sakinah Mosque in Surabaya facing Mecca? This 2025 study by Safna Farah Dila measured it three ways. A theodolite and a mizwala, two direction-finding tools, found it about 5.6 to 5.9 degrees off. A simple right-angle triangle method said 25 degrees, showing how much the tool you choose matters.

title: Digital Transformation Through Islamic Digital Banking For Financial Inclusion
summary: Digitalization trends, to a certain extent, shape organizations and individuals in a similar way. The application of digitalization becoming widespread and is a necessity in a business today. Digitalization plays in improving the business landscape by creating the opportunity to enhance development, increase employment opportunities, and accelerate innovation. The introduction of information and communication technology has transformed the banking and financial services industry. The Islamic banks urge to react to these radical changes in order to meet the need of the society especially among Muslim community. The development and adoption of Shariah compliant digital banking in line with Maq
creator: Muhammad Ridhwan AB. Aziz

locator: DOI=10.36378/internationalconferenceuniks.v0i0.2818; journal="Proceeding of International Conference on Science and Technology"
scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic app digital technology"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Banking is going digital everywhere. This 2022 paper by Muhammad Ridhwan AB. Aziz argues Islamic banks must keep up to serve Muslim communities, and that Shariah-compliant digital banking could bring more people into the financial system.

title: The Potential of Halal Culinary Tourism Among Non-Muslim Communities in Bali
summary: Research article in Al-Amwal : Jurnal Ekonomi dan Perbankan Syari'ah by Rokhmat Subagiyo, Achmad Syaichoni, 2023.

story: Bali is mostly non-Muslim, and halal cooking there is still limited, even though halal culinary tourism has grown across Indonesia. This 2023 study asks how halal food tourism could develop among Bali's non-Muslim communities.

title: Integrating Waqf and Takaful: Developing the Inclusive Takaful Waqf Ecosystem (ITWE) in Indonesia
summary: This study examines the development of waqf-based takaful products in Indonesia through the integration of an inclusive Islamic financial ecosystem. The research was motivated by the significant disparity between the enormous potential of national waqf assets and the limited utilization of takaful as a mechanism for protecting waqf properties from various risks. Employing a mixed methods approach with an explanatory sequential design, the study collected quantitative and qualitative data from key stakeholders in the Islamic insurance and waqf sectors, including sharia insurance companies, regulators, and waqf institutions. creator: Sutrimo Sutrimo, Ucu Cahyana, Ahmad Subagyo
source_name: Journal of Indonesian Islamic Studies
locator: DOI=10.24256/jiis.v5i2.11154; journal="Journal of Indonesian Islamic Studies"
scope_basis: Crossref search "waqf innovation"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Waqf properties, endowed forever, can still be damaged or lost. Takaful is Islamic insurance. This 2026 study by Sutrimo Sutrimo, Ucu Cahyana and Ahmad Subagyo asked insurers, regulators and waqf bodies in Indonesia how to bring the two together, so waqf assets are protected.

title: Digital Transformation of Waqf Management: Innovation Pathways and Policy Directions in Muslim-Majority Developing Countries
summary: Waqf represents a powerful economic instrument with substantial potential to empower communities, particularly in countries with large Muslim populations. In the digital era, innovations in the management of productive waqf offer new opportunities to enhance the effectiveness and efficiency of waqf fund utilization. This study aims to explore innovative models of productive waqf management and their impact on community economic empowerment. Employing a qualitative descriptive approach, this research conducts a comprehensive literature review of journal articles, books, and other relevant sources to analyze digital waqf practices in developing countries. The findings reveal that digital innov
creator: Riduwan, Erwan Aristyanto
source_name: Muslim Heritage
scope_basis: Crossref search "waqf innovation"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: Waqf, the Islamic endowment, can lift whole communities. This 2025 review by Riduwan and Erwan Aristyanto looks at how digital tools are changing productive waqf management in Muslim-majority developing countries, and what policies could help.

title: Astronomical Aspects of the Early Determination of Subuh
summary: Research article in Al-Marshad: Jurnal Astronomi Islam dan Ilmu-Ilmu Berkaitan, 2023.

story: When does the dawn prayer, Subuh, begin? This 2023 study looks at the astronomy behind setting its early time. Its record says little more than this, so this is an outline.

title: Social Action of Conversion in Islamic Art: Study on the Larasmadya Art Form in the Sleman Geocultural Region
summary: The research concerned here had the purpose of learning the rationality in the social action of conversion by the farmer communities supporting the Larasmadya art form in the Sleman geocultural region. The research was qualitative in approach. The research subjects were members of the farmer communities supporting the Larasmadya art who previously supporting the Slawatan Maulud art form. The research data were compiled by means of observations, interviews, and documentation. These data were analyzed through the phases of data collection, data reduction, data examination, and drawing the conclusion. Data validation was done by means of triangulation. creator: Sutiyono Sutiyono
source_name: Indonesian Journal of Geography
scope_basis: Crossref search "islamic art brazil"; publisher hosted in Indonesia
story: In Sleman, near Yogyakarta, farming communities once supported an art form called Slawatan Maulud. Many switched to a different one, Larasmadya. This 2015 study by Sutiyono Sutiyono asks why, looking for the reasoning behind that switch.

title: Negotiating Faith and Food: The Implementation of Halal Certification Obligations in Community-Based Meatball Milling Practices at Tanjung Morawa Traditional Market
summary: Meatball grinding facilities process meat-based products and are therefore required to obtain halal certification due to several critical control points, such as meat sourcing, additives, hygiene, and potential contamination. However, none of the facilities at Pasar Rakyat Tanjung Morawa currently hold halal certification. This study investigates the factors hindering the implementation of Halal Product Assurance in these facilities. Using an empirical juridical approach, supported by a case study and sociological perspective, data were collected through observations and interviews, then analyzed qualitatively through deductive reasoning. In the perspective of Ibn Sina the essence of human being is composed of two elements, namely the body (jism) and soul (nafs). These two elements are really different from the ones found in animals and plants. The presence of soul (nafs) is its manifestation. While the body (jism) a tool for nafs. In addition, there is also a strong relationship between the jism and the nafs. Nafs will never achieve a phenomenal stage without the body. title: Early colour photograph, Bukhara, c. 1907–1911 (Ėmir Bukharskīĭ. Bukhara)
summary: Photo shows the Emir of Bukhara, Alim Khan (1880-1944), posing solemnly for his portrait, taken in 1911 shortly after his accession. As ruler of an autonomous city-state in Islamic Central Asia, the Emir presided over the internal affairs of his emirate as absolute monarch, although since the mid-1800s Bukhara had been a vassal state of the Russian Empire. With the establishment of Soviet power in Bukhara in 1920, the Emir fled to Afghanistan where he died in 1944.
